simple.en: Sahaj grows through Guru’s grace and inward Shabad-attention, not merely multiplying external ritual actions.
simple.pa: ਸਹਜ ਗੁਰੂ ਦੀ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਤੇ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਨਾਲ ਜੁੜਨ ਨਾਲ ਮਿਲਦਾ ਹੈ; ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਬਾਹਰਲੇ ਕਰਮ ਕਾਫ਼ੀ ਨਹੀਂ।

study.focus: The question “how can the mind be cleansed?”
study.closeReading: The pauri repeatedly pairs ritual action with lingering doubt, then asks how the inward stain can be washed. The practical turn is the fourth line—attach the mind to the Shabad and Hari. The final line attributes enduring Sahaj to Guru’s grace instead of technique alone.
study.interpretationCare: Sahaj is not simply a measurable calm state, and “doubt” is not a diagnosis. Do not promise a religious practice as a treatment for anxiety disorders or other health conditions.
study.reflection: When have repeated routines failed to address what was troubling me inwardly?
study.teachBack: Which line moves from criticism of ritual to an inward practice?

simple.en: A spotless outward appearance cannot substitute for inner truth when craving and falsehood rule the mind.
simple.pa: ਬਾਹਰਲੀ ਸੁਚਾਈ ਅੰਦਰਲੀ ਸੱਚਾਈ ਦਾ ਬਦਲ ਨਹੀਂ; ਤ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਨਾ ਅਤੇ ਕੂੜ ਜੀਵਨ ਦੀ ਸੇਧ ਖੋਹ ਸਕਦੇ ਹਨ।

study.focus: Contrasting visible purity with inward responsibility.
study.closeReading: The first two lines set the direct inner–outer contrast and the striking image of life lost in gambling. The third names unsatisfied craving and mortality; the fourth points to Naam yet describes people ignoring it. The concluding line binds them to the truth-versus-falsehood decision. This imagery is a warning about values, not a label for people.

words.workingGloss: Falsehood or what lacks Truth, context dependent

study.interpretationCare: The word “rog” for craving is metaphorical. Never equate this spiritual critique with diagnosis, shame people with substance-use or other medical conditions, or present it as clinical care.
study.reflection: How can I compare what I appear to value with what I actually do?
study.teachBack: How does the image of gambling away life connect to abandoning Truth?

simple.en: The companion to Pauri 19 emphasizes outward and inward truth together, cultivated through the Guru’s teaching.
simple.pa: ਉੱਨੀਵੀਂ ਪਉੜੀ ਦੇ ਉਲਟ, ਇੱਥੇ ਮਨ ਤੇ ਕਰਮ ਦੋਹਾਂ ਦੀ ਸਚਾਈ ਗੁਰੂ ਦੀ ਸਿੱਖਿਆ ਨਾਲ ਜੁੜਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: The paired answer to Pauri 19.
study.closeReading: The immediately previous pauri began “dirty inside, clean outside.” This one deliberately reverses that to “clean inside, clean outside,” then explains the Guru-oriented conduct behind it. The trade/gem imagery means the human opportunity has been used wisely, not that spiritual life is a financial enterprise.

words.workingGloss: Traders, used as a metaphor for people making good use of life

study.interpretationCare: Do not make “purity” into caste hierarchy or claim that a person with illness, disability or grief is spiritually unclean. The trading image has no promise of monetary profit.
study.reflection: What concrete action could bring my outer behaviour closer to my inner commitments?
study.teachBack: How does Pauri 20 answer the inner–outer contrast begun in Pauri 19?

simple.en: Being sanmukh means orienting one’s heart and conduct toward the Guru, not merely appearing religious.
simple.pa: ਸਨਮੁਖ ਹੋਣਾ ਕੇਵਲ ਬਾਹਰਲਾ ਰੂਪ ਨਹੀਂ; ਮਨ ਤੇ ਆਚਰਨ ਨੂੰ ਗੁਰੂ ਦੀ ਸਿੱਖਿਆ ਨਾਲ ਜੋੜਨਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: An inward relationship rather than an external label.
study.closeReading: The first and last lines define sanmukh as facing the Guru. The middle three explain its lived meaning: staying near in one’s heart, remembering the Guru’s feet and setting down self-centred pride. Spiritual refuge is described as a sustained orientation, not as obedience to any unaccountable individual.

words.workingGloss: Facing or turning toward the Guru

study.interpretationCare: An instruction to relinquish ego is not authorization for a religious leader to coerce, exploit or isolate a person; it refers to the Guru’s teaching in context.
study.reflection: What action today would show the difference between saying I follow a teaching and living it?
study.teachBack: Which inner qualities define sanmukh in lines two through four?

simple.en: The pauri contrasts turning away from the Guru with returning to the Guru’s Shabad for freedom.
simple.pa: ਇਹ ਪਉੜੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਤੋਂ ਦੂਰ ਹੋਣ ਅਤੇ ਮੁੜ ਗੁਰੂ ਦੇ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਨਾਲ ਜੁੜਨ ਦੇ ਫ਼ਰਕ ਨੂੰ ਸਮਝਾਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Vemukh and sanmukh as paired teachings.
study.closeReading: This pauri deliberately answers Pauri 21. Rather than listing outward marks of a Sikh, it speaks about estrangement, recurring confusion and the possibility of return through the Guru’s Shabad. It is a theological picture of liberation, not a licence to shame someone who has questions or a different religious background.

words.workingGloss: Turned away or estranged from the Guru
Liberation or release in spiritual teaching

study.interpretationCare: Do not turn a Sikh source’s liberation teaching into declarations that members of other faiths are inferior, or use it to pressure a person into unsafe obedience.
study.reflection: When have I turned away from helpful guidance, and what helped me return?
study.teachBack: How does the fourth line offer a way back after the first three describe estrangement?

simple.en: The sangat is invited to sing, receive and inwardly live the Guru’s true Bani.
simple.pa: ਸੰਗਤ ਨੂੰ ਸੱਚੀ ਗੁਰਬਾਣੀ ਗਾਉਣ, ਸੁਣਨ ਤੇ ਹਿਰਦੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਵਸਾਉਣ ਦਾ ਸੱਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Singing as a form of attentive learning.
study.closeReading: The repeated invitation to sing Bani frames the pauri. The central lines move from vocal singing to grace, dwelling within the heart, and the imagery of drinking amrit and being coloured by Hari. Thus the teaching is not merely musical performance: it is attentive remembrance in a shared community.

words.workingGloss: The Guru’s sacred Word in this source context

study.interpretationCare: Amrit here is poetic/spiritual nourishment; do not turn it into a supplement, magic drink, medical promise or claim about a particular singer’s virtue.
study.reflection: When I read or sing, am I also allowing the teaching to guide a real choice?
study.teachBack: Which line shifts the focus from audible singing to Bani dwelling in the heart?

simple.en: The Guru’s priceless Shabad becomes a lasting source of inward love and understanding of the True One.
simple.pa: ਗੁਰੂ ਦਾ ਬੇਮੋਲ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਮਨ ਨੂੰ ਸੱਚੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨਾਲ ਪਿਆਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਜੋੜਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: A precious jewel as an image for transformative wisdom.
study.closeReading: The first and final lines repeat the jewel-and-diamond image. The middle connects that preciousness to the mind’s growing attachment to the Guru’s Word, love for the True One, and understanding bestowed by the Divine. This metaphor conveys enduring value, not a literal mineral hidden in scripture.
study.interpretationCare: No physical gem, financial investment or magical gem power is being promised by this imagery. Exact morphology of the jeweled phrase needs review.
study.reflection: What kind of wisdom has greater value to me than a temporary possession?
study.teachBack: Why might the poet describe the Shabad as a jewel rather than as a price?

simple.en: Hukam, Shabad and the Guru-oriented mind lead toward freedom from inner bondage.
simple.pa: ਹੁਕਮ ਦੀ ਸਮਝ, ਸ਼ਬਦ ਅਤੇ ਗੁਰਮੁਖ ਜੀਵਨ ਬੰਧਨਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਛੁਟਕਾਰੇ ਵੱਲ ਲੈ ਜਾਂਦੇ ਹਨ।

study.focus: The Creator as source of order and inner freedom.
study.closeReading: The first two lines name creation and the operation of Hukam. The third shifts the focus from cosmic description to individual spiritual bondage. The fourth speaks of a person drawn to the One, and the last credits the Creator with granting understanding. The Shiva–Shakti expression is a complex historical religious idiom.

words.workingGloss: Divine order or command in context

study.interpretationCare: Shiva/Shakti here must be interpreted carefully within Gurbani and not treated as a literal scientific description of cosmic forces or an attack on other communities.
study.reflection: What kind of attachment might loosen when I remember a principle larger than my ego?
study.teachBack: Which line turns the subject from the Creator’s universal Hukam toward an inward change?

simple.en: The deepest essence is not merely argued about in scripture; it is understood through the Guru and a wakeful life of Naam.
simple.pa: ਤੱਤ ਦੀ ਅਸਲ ਸਮਝ ਕੇਵਲ ਸ਼ਾਸਤਰੀ ਚਰਚਾ ਨਾਲ ਨਹੀਂ; ਗੁਰੂ ਦੀ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਤੇ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਲ ਲਿਵ ਰਾਹੀਂ ਆਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: From discussion to lived awakening.
study.closeReading: The first two lines question reliance on book knowledge alone. The third portrays people asleep within confusion as the night passes. The fourth and fifth introduce an awakening through grace, Bani, and steadfast awareness. The imagery holds learning and transformation together rather than rejecting thoughtful study.

words.workingGloss: Nectar-like, life-giving quality of spiritual Bani

study.interpretationCare: The “three qualities” are a traditional framework, not a modern psychological diagnosis. The poem critiques insufficient engagement, not the human worth of other scriptural traditions.
study.reflection: How can studying a teaching become a change in how I act?
study.teachBack: Which line marks the transition from sleeping in confusion to awakening?

simple.en: Care from before birth is a poetic reason for gratitude and remembrance of the Divine Giver.
simple.pa: ਜਨਮ ਤੋਂ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਦੀ ਸੰਭਾਲ ਦੀ ਤਸਵੀਰ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੇ ਸ਼ੁਕਰਾਨੇ ਤੇ ਸਿਮਰਨ ਵੱਲ ਸੱਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Remembrance through vulnerability and care.
study.closeReading: The opening and final lines ask the same question about forgetting the Giver. The centre describes nourishment in the womb and a continuing bond of loving attention through Guru-oriented life. The womb’s heat is a devotional image of vulnerability and care, not an obstetric explanation.
study.interpretationCare: Do not infer a promise of risk-free pregnancy, protection from congenital disease or medical immunity. The mother and child both deserve ordinary health care and support.
study.reflection: What kindness and care in my life have I begun taking for granted?
study.teachBack: What repeated question binds this pauri together?

simple.en: Life outside the womb brings Maya and forgetfulness, yet Guru’s grace permits remembrance within ordinary life.
simple.pa: ਜਨਮ ਮਗਰੋਂ ਮਾਇਆ ਦਾ ਮੋਹ ਮਨ ਨੂੰ ਭੁਲਾ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ, ਪਰ ਗੁਰੂ ਦੀ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਨਾਲ ਇਸੇ ਜੀਵਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਾਮ ਨਾਲ ਜੁੜਿਆ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: The two fires and returning to connection.
study.closeReading: This stanza follows Pauri 28’s womb imagery. The first two compare the inward and worldly “fires”; the middle depicts birth, familial love and the arising of craving. The fifth defines harmful Maya as forgetfulness of Hari, and the sixth offers an important hope: the connection can return through the Guru while one still lives in the world.
study.interpretationCare: Do not imply that parenting or family affection causes a clinical disorder or that the physical womb literally burns. Maya describes attachment that displaces remembrance, not children or women.
study.reflection: How can I enjoy everyday responsibilities without letting craving direct my whole life?
study.teachBack: How does the final line complicate a simple story that the material world is entirely bad?

simple.en: No worldly price can measure the Divine; the Guru points the mind from ego toward closeness with Hari.
simple.pa: ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦਾ ਮੁੱਲ ਨਹੀਂ ਪਾਇਆ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ; ਗੁਰੂ ਦੀ ਸੇਧ ਹਉਮੈ ਛੱਡ ਕੇ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਲ ਜੁੜਨ ਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Worth beyond commerce and surrender of ego.
study.closeReading: The first two lines deny that the Divine can be priced. The third says that meeting the True Guru calls for a giving-up of self-importance, and the next two turn toward relationship, Hari dwelling in the mind and the privilege of receiving that priceless gift. The metaphor is not a financial transaction or transfer of authority to a human.

words.workingGloss: Head, used for humble offering of oneself in this context

study.interpretationCare: The phrase “give one’s head” is traditional devotion and cannot justify coercion, self-harm, surrender of rights, money or bodily safety to another person.
study.reflection: What matters to me that has value no price tag can express?
study.teachBack: How is letting go of ego connected to the poem’s insistence that Hari is priceless?

simple.en: The Guru shows the mind a form of wealth that cannot be measured in money: remembrance of Hari.
simple.pa: ਗੁਰੂ ਮਨ ਨੂੰ ਅਜਿਹੀ ਦੌਲਤ ਨਾਲ ਜੋੜਦਾ ਹੈ ਜਿਸ ਦੀ ਕੀਮਤ ਪੈਸਿਆਂ ਨਾਲ ਨਹੀਂ—ਹਰਿ ਦਾ ਸਿਮਰਨ।

study.focus: Trading language reorients what the mind treasures.
study.closeReading: The pauri opens and closes with the same merchant and capital imagery. The Guru helps the mind recognize real capital, then the daily act of remembrance is named an earned “profit.” The fourth line returns to grace: spiritual wealth is not a possession bought by effort. This imagery does not celebrate exploitation or encourage financial speculation.

words.workingGloss: Capital, spiritual treasure in this comparison
Trader or merchant; a metaphor for the mind

study.interpretationCare: The language of profit is spiritual, not financial or transactional. Never sell Naam, promise material income, or interpret poverty as a failure of prayer.
study.reflection: What am I investing attention in today that will still matter later?
study.teachBack: Which two words carry the trade metaphor through the first and final lines?

simple.en: The taste of Hari represents the fulfilment that outward pleasures alone cannot provide.
simple.pa: ਹਰਿ-ਰਸ ਅਜਿਹੀ ਆਤਮਕ ਤ੍ਰਿਪਤੀ ਦੀ ਤਸਵੀਰ ਹੈ ਜੋ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਬਾਹਰਲੇ ਸੁਆਦਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਨਹੀਂ ਮਿਲਦੀ।

study.focus: A tongue addressed as a doorway to the heart.
study.closeReading: The poet addresses the rasna directly, repeating thirst and rasa before pointing to the Guru and grace. The ending is not a rule about food or taste, but about what truly satisfies the mind. The contrast between worldly pleasure and Hari’s sweetness is a spiritual critique of attachment, not of human senses themselves.

words.workingGloss: Tongue; poetically the faculty of tasting and speaking

study.interpretationCare: Do not turn spiritual thirst into instructions to avoid eating, hydration, medication, pleasure or family meals; Hari ras is devotional imagery, not a special chemical substance.
study.reflection: Which short-lived pleasures can distract me from deeper values?
study.teachBack: How does the repeated word “ras” shift meaning across this pauri?

simple.en: The body is honoured as a place where the Divine light and creative care are remembered.
simple.pa: ਸਰੀਰ ਅੰਦਰ ਰੱਬੀ ਜੋਤ ਤੇ ਸਿਰਜਣਹਾਰ ਦੀ ਸੰਭਾਲ ਯਾਦ ਕਰਵਾਈ ਜਾਂਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Speaking to the body, not despising it.
study.closeReading: Beginning and end repeat that the Divine places light within the human body. In the middle, parental images of God emphasize care, and the Guru makes the wonder of creation understandable. The “light” is sacred metaphor, not a measured physical illumination or proof of a specific fetal process.
study.interpretationCare: Do not use this poetic origin story as a claim about photons, inheritance, pregnancy science or disability. Honor actual human bodies and medical care.
study.reflection: How would my choices change if I treated my body with greater respect and gratitude?
study.teachBack: Why does the pauri speak to the body directly rather than calling it worthless?

simple.en: The Guru’s Shabad is celebrated as a joyful welcome to the Divine Beloved within the heart.
simple.pa: ਗੁਰੂ ਦਾ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਮਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੇ ਮਿਲਾਪ ਦੀ ਖੁਸ਼ੀ ਅਤੇ ਮੰਗਲ ਦਾ ਸੱਦਾ ਦਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: The language of a festive home and spiritual union.
study.closeReading: The first line announces joy; the second and third invite companions to celebrate as if a beloved guest has arrived. The fourth credits closeness to the Guru, and the fifth places anhad Bani and Hari Naam at the centre. The conclusion names the Lord as the true agent of meeting. This is poetic marital/household imagery, not a claim that sincere people never experience sadness.
study.interpretationCare: Do not market prayer as preventing clinical depression or sorrow, or interpret “anhad” as a measurable external acoustic frequency or special recording.
study.reflection: How can gratitude become something I share quietly with others?
study.teachBack: How do the welcoming-home and Shabad images reinforce one another?

simple.en: Human life is an opportunity for thoughtful action and remembrance, not merely outward achievement.
simple.pa: ਮਨੁੱਖਾ ਜਨਮ ਚੰਗੇ ਕਰਮ ਅਤੇ ਹਰਿ ਦੀ ਯਾਦ ਦਾ ਮੌਕਾ ਹੈ, ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਬਾਹਰਲੀ ਕਾਮਯਾਬੀ ਨਹੀਂ।

study.focus: A second intimate address to the body.
study.closeReading: Like Pauri33, the poet addresses the body. This time the question concerns conduct: what did one do with life? The middle reveals forgetfulness of the Creator and the possibility of returning through Guru’s grace; the final line treats connection to the True Guru as the measure of meaningful life.

words.workingGloss: Actions or deeds, with context-dependent meanings
Accepted, worthwhile or spiritually approved in this idiom

study.interpretationCare: Do not treat a person with illness, disability or limited opportunities as having a “failed body”; spiritual worth is not bodily productivity or medical status.
study.reflection: What meaningful action can I take within my own real abilities today?
study.teachBack: How does Pauri35 answer the earlier description of Divine light placed within the body?

simple.en: The eye’s purpose in this pauri is to recognize the Divine throughout creation through Guru-given insight.
simple.pa: ਇਸ ਪਉੜੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਨੇਤਰਾਂ ਦੀ ਸੇਧ ਗੁਰੂ ਦੀ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਨਾਲ ਸ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਟੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਰੱਬੀ ਜੋਤਿ ਪਛਾਣਣਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: From looking at forms to seeing a shared Divine presence.
study.closeReading: The first line addresses the eyes and recalls the Divine light that enabled life. Lines two through four teach a change of perspective: everything seen can invite recognition of the One. The final “blindness” is the lack of spiritual insight, not a judgment of actual vision ability; the Guru grants a different kind of understanding.

words.workingGloss: O eyes; direct address to the faculty of seeing
Sight, insight or vision by context

study.interpretationCare: Do not imply that blind or visually impaired people lack spirituality, or promise that Gurbani restores sight. Divine “light” here is not measurable optical radiation.
study.reflection: How can I look at another person with respect rather than making quick judgments?
study.teachBack: Which phrase in the final line describes spiritual insight rather than physical eyesight?

simple.en: Attentive listening to true Bani can deepen remembrance and ethical awareness in the heart.
simple.pa: ਸੱਚੀ ਬਾਣੀ ਨੂੰ ਧਿਆਨ ਨਾਲ ਸੁਣਨਾ ਹਿਰਦੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਾਮ ਦੀ ਯਾਦ ਤੇ ਸੂਝ ਨੂੰ ਡੂੰਘਾ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Listening is presented as an active spiritual practice.
study.closeReading: The poet addresses the ears directly, much as Pauri36 addressed the eyes. Hearing the true Bani is connected with inner flourishing and sweetness. The fourth line reminds us that the Divine cannot be fully captured by words, even as the fifth returns to listening and Naam. This is attentive spiritual reception, not an exclusion of learners who communicate differently.

words.workingGloss: O ears or listeners; direct address
Sacred Word or spoken teaching in this context

study.interpretationCare: Hearing disability or deafness does not make a person impure or less able to engage with Gurbani through reading, signing or other accessible means. No clinical hearing improvement is promised.
study.reflection: What changes when I listen carefully rather than only waiting to speak?
study.teachBack: How do the references to ears and tongue work together in the middle of this pauri?

simple.en: The body’s breath and inward spiritual attention are described through a cave, a wind instrument and a hidden doorway.
simple.pa: ਸਰੀਰ ਦੀ ਸਾਂਸ ਤੇ ਅੰਦਰਲੀ ਸੂਝ ਨੂੰ ਗੁਫਾ, ਪਵਣ ਦੇ ਵਾਜੇ ਅਤੇ ਗੁਪਤ ਦੁਆਰ ਦੇ ਰੂਪਕਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਸਮਝਾਇਆ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Respect symbolic traditional anatomy without treating it as a device manual.
study.closeReading: The pauri’s opening and ending describe the body as a cave holding life, with breath as an instrument. The middle invokes nine visible and one hidden door, then says the Guru grants awareness. The “tenth doorway” has a rich Sikh interpretive history and needs qualified theological review; the poem does not specify an anatomical opening or a breath-control exercise.

words.workingGloss: Cave; a metaphor for the embodied inner space
Doorway; symbol of spiritual awareness in context

study.interpretationCare: Do not claim a literal tenth anatomical hole, prescribe breath-holding/hyperventilation, promise altered consciousness, or instruct children to attempt a bodily exercise. An expert Sikh/Santhiya reviewer must approve contextual interpretation.
study.reflection: How might ordinary breathing remind me to be attentive without forcing any special technique?
study.teachBack: Which features of the body are presented as musical or architectural imagery?

simple.en: True praise grows where the heart remembers the Divine through grace and Guru-given understanding.
simple.pa: ਸੱਚਾ ਸੋਹਿਲਾ ਉਥੇ ਗੂੰਜਦਾ ਹੈ ਜਿੱਥੇ ਮਨ ਨਾਮ ਨਾਲ ਜੁੜਦਾ ਅਤੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਦੀ ਸੇਧ ਪਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Sohila as the song of the true home.
study.closeReading: The first and final lines frame the pauri with “sacha sohila” and “sachai ghar.” The middle identifies what fills that home: remembrance of Truth, Guru-oriented understanding and Divine grace shared without regard to status. This use of “sohila” is a poetic description within Anand Sahib; it is not the text identity of the separate Kirtan Sohila night composition.

words.workingGloss: A joyful song of praise or celebration
Lord, Protector or Sovereign in devotional usage

study.interpretationCare: Do not confuse this Anand stanza with all five shabads of Kirtan Sohila merely because both use the word “sohila.” Nor equate the “true home” with one physical building.
study.reflection: What might a home devoted to truth look like in ordinary relationships?
study.teachBack: What belongs in the “true home” according to the central lines?

simple.en: The closing Anand Pauri celebrates the joy and spiritual relief of listening to true Bani through the Guru.
simple.pa: ਅਨੰਦ ਦੀ ਅੰਤਲੀ ਪਉੜੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਰਾਹੀਂ ਸੱਚੀ ਬਾਣੀ ਸੁਣਨ, ਸਮਝਣ ਤੇ ਆਤਮਕ ਖੁਸ਼ੀ ਦੀ ਵਡਿਆਈ ਕਰਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: A closing blessing rather than a measurable treatment claim.
study.closeReading: The last pauri gathers the bani’s themes into a blessing: listening, finding the One, relief from distress, joy among companions, purification and the music of spiritual celebration. The third line explicitly mentions “dookh rog santaap”; this must be presented faithfully as what the sacred text says, **not** as an empirical guarantee that hearing the bani cures infections, cancer, mental illness or disability. The closing anhad trumpets are spiritual imagery, not a literal recorded concert.

words.workingGloss: Illness or affliction, used in this devotional blessing

study.interpretationCare: Do NOT market Gurbani as a replacement for medical care or a guaranteed cure for physical or mental illness. “Manorath poore” is devotional hope, not a contractual promise of every worldly desire being met.
study.reflection: How could hearing these teachings help me face suffering with compassion while still seeking appropriate help?
study.teachBack: What themes from the whole Anand Sahib return in this final pauri?

simple.en: The prayer asks for defence against harm and wellbeing for one’s family and community.
simple.pa: ਬੇਨਤੀ ਵਿਚ ਦੁੱਖ ਤੇ ਵੈਰ ਤੋਂ ਬਚਾਅ ਨਾਲ ਪਰਿਵਾਰ ਅਤੇ ਸਿੱਖ ਸੇਵਕਾਂ ਦੀ ਸੁਖ-ਸ਼ਾਂਤੀ ਵੀ ਮੰਗੀ ਜਾਂਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Protection of self and community.
study.closeReading: The movement expands from “me” to family and other servants or Sikhs. It is meaningful to study this communal scope alongside the martial language rather than isolating one aggressive phrase.
study.interpretationCare: Language about destroying enemies belongs to a particular literary and historical context. Do not use a devotional lesson to label actual neighbours as enemies or excuse violence. The exact same original source stanza also occurs here as Rehras rehras.chaupai02; source context differs, do not silently conflate variant or recitation order.
study.reflection: Whose safety do I include when I pray for my own?
study.teachBack: What does the stanza ask for beyond the speaker alone?

simple.en: The speaker asks for help against danger and for a lasting thirst for divine remembrance.
simple.pa: ਸੰਕਟ ਤੋਂ ਬਚਾਅ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਭਜਨ ਦੀ ਪਿਆਸ ਕਾਇਮ ਰਹਿਣ ਦੀ ਬੇਨਤੀ ਵੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Courage and remembrance.
study.closeReading: The final request for longing toward devotion gives direction to the earlier images of protection. Learning should preserve both the martial and inward language.
study.interpretationCare: The image of a “foe” should not be automatically converted into a diagnosis of someone’s psychology. The exact same original source stanza also occurs here as Rehras rehras.chaupai03; source context differs, do not silently conflate variant or recitation order.
study.reflection: What kind of longing would help direct your actions?
study.teachBack: How does the final line reshape the earlier appeal for protection?

rehras|rehras.chaupai03.sourceContext: Exact full unit/source-text hash checked against chaupai|chaupai-rehras03

simple.en: The speaker pledges reliance on the One and asks that the community be carried through danger.
simple.pa: ਬਾਣੀ ਵਿਚ ਹੋਰ ਆਸਰਿਆਂ ਤੋਂ ਉਪਰ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਉੱਤੇ ਭਰੋਸਾ ਅਤੇ ਸੇਵਕ ਸਿੱਖਾਂ ਦੀ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਦੀ ਬੇਨਤੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Exclusive reliance and responsibility.
study.closeReading: The pauri places trust and a plea for others side by side. Martial expressions are present, but a learning application should not flatten them into an invitation to personal aggression.
study.interpretationCare: The boundaries of historically contextual enemy-language need qualified literary review. The exact same original source stanza also occurs here as Rehras rehras.chaupai04; source context differs, do not silently conflate variant or recitation order.
study.reflection: What does loyalty to the One look like in the way I treat others?
study.teachBack: What are the two kinds of requests in this pauri?

rehras|rehras.chaupai04.sourceContext: Exact full unit/source-text hash checked against chaupai|chaupai-rehras04

simple.en: The prayer asks the Divine to remain close through fear, even the fear of death.
simple.pa: ਮੌਤ ਦੇ ਡਰ ਸਮੇਤ ਹਰ ਸੰਕਟ ਵੇਲੇ ਸਹਾਰੇ ਅਤੇ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਦੀ ਬੇਨਤੀ ਕੀਤੀ ਜਾਂਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Protection through mortality.
study.closeReading: The appeal becomes more personal: the speaker asks to be lifted up when afraid. It expresses dependence and hope, not an empirically guaranteed escape from danger.
study.interpretationCare: Do not tell vulnerable people that danger can be ignored because the prayer has been recited. The exact same original source stanza also occurs here as Rehras rehras.chaupai05; source context differs, do not silently conflate variant or recitation order.
study.reflection: What support helps a person face fear more wisely?
study.teachBack: How does this pauri describe the speaker’s relationship to fear?

rehras|rehras.chaupai05.sourceContext: Exact full unit/source-text hash checked against chaupai|chaupai-rehras05

simple.en: The Divine is addressed as protector, helper of the humble and Sovereign beyond ordinary limits.
simple.pa: ਰੱਖਣਹਾਰ, ਦੀਨਬੰਧੂ ਅਤੇ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਡੇ ਸਹਾਰੇ ਨੂੰ ਯਾਦ ਕਰਕੇ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਮੰਗੀ ਗਈ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Names of shelter and sovereignty.
study.closeReading: Each title develops the speaker’s trust in the One. The phrase about the fourteen realms is a traditional cosmic image of breadth, not modern astronomical measurement.
study.interpretationCare: Treat cosmic imagery as poetry in its historical context, not a scientific map. The exact same original source stanza also occurs here as Rehras rehras.chaupai06; source context differs, do not silently conflate variant or recitation order.
study.reflection: Whom do I need to include in the care shown to the lowly?
study.teachBack: How do the various titles expand the idea of protection?

rehras|rehras.chaupai06.sourceContext: Exact full unit/source-text hash checked against chaupai|chaupai-rehras06

simple.en: The stanza places famous figures of traditional cosmology inside time, while pointing beyond them toward the One.
simple.pa: ਬ੍ਰਹਮਾ, ਸ਼ਿਵ ਅਤੇ ਵਿਸ਼ਨੂ ਦੇ ਨਾਮ ਲੈ ਕੇ ਵੀ ਬਾਣੀ ਸਮੇਂ ਤੇ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਅਸਲ ਸਹਾਰੇ ਵੱਲ ਧਿਆਨ ਕਰਵਾਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: The changing within time and the One beyond it.
study.closeReading: The names of divine figures are used within the poem’s traditional vocabulary. The important comparison is that manifestations occur in time; do not collapse the imagery into a literal historical timetable.
study.interpretationCare: This is a theological poem, not data proving a precise age of the universe. The exact same original source stanza also occurs here as Rehras rehras.chaupai07; source context differs, do not silently conflate variant or recitation order.
study.reflection: What helps me remember that even impressive systems change?
study.teachBack: What contrast does the repetition of ਕਾਲ create?

rehras|rehras.chaupai07.sourceContext: Exact full unit/source-text hash checked against chaupai|chaupai-rehras07

simple.en: The poem looks beyond named divine figures to the source that orders and sustains the worlds.
simple.pa: ਬਾਣੀ ਵੱਖਰੇ ਪੁਰਾਣਕ ਪਾਤਰਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਉਪਰ ਉਸ ਇੱਕ ਸਰੋਤ ਨੂੰ ਯਾਦ ਕਰਦੀ ਹੈ ਜੋ ਸਾਰੇ ਜਗਤ ਦੀ ਰਚਨਾ ਅਤੇ ਸੰਭਾਲ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: The creative power beyond familiar images.
study.closeReading: The sequence begins with Shiva as yogi and Brahma in relation to the Vedas, then widens to all worlds. Its closing salutation makes the object of devotion clearer: not separate historical heroes, but the one Divine Source that exceeds them.

words.workingGloss: That which or the One who; a Braj relative expression

study.interpretationCare: Kaal can mean time or a divine epithet in Dasam poetry; precise morphology and comparison of printed editions are not cleared. The exact same original source stanza also occurs here as Rehras rehras.chaupai08; source context differs, do not silently conflate variant or recitation order.
study.reflection: How can recognizing one source deepen respect without disparaging anyone else?
study.teachBack: Where does the fourth line direct the salutation after the first three images?

rehras|rehras.chaupai08.sourceContext: Exact full unit/source-text hash checked against chaupai|chaupai-rehras08

simple.en: The Creator who fashioned the world and its diverse beings is the same One the poet accepts as Guru.
simple.pa: ਜਿਸ ਇੱਕ ਨੇ ਜਗਤ ਅਤੇ ਅਨੇਕ ਜੀਵ ਰਚੇ ਹਨ, ਕਵੀ ਉਸੇ ਨੂੰ ਆਪਣਾ ਗੁਰੂ ਮੰਨਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Creation, beginning and the One who guides.
study.closeReading: The first two lines give the breadth of creation by naming the world and traditional classes of beings. The last two turn from diversity to unity: the Divine remains the Source through beginning and end, and the speaker declares that One to be the Guru.

words.workingGloss: Enlightening teacher; the Divine guide in this context

study.interpretationCare: Names for devas, daits and yakshas belong to traditional poetic cosmology; they are not a verified biological catalogue. The exact same original source stanza also occurs here as Rehras rehras.chaupai09; source context differs, do not silently conflate variant or recitation order.
study.reflection: Does my sense of guidance rest on forms that change or on principles that endure?
study.teachBack: Why does the poet end a list of created beings with “That is my Guru”?

rehras|rehras.chaupai09.sourceContext: Exact full unit/source-text hash checked against chaupai|chaupai-rehras09

simple.en: The speaker offers salutations to the Creator who sustains beings and stands with devotees.
simple.pa: ਕਵੀ ਸਭ ਜੀਵਾਂ ਦੀ ਸੰਭਾਲ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਤੇ ਉਸ ਦੇ ਸਹਾਰੇ ਨੂੰ ਯਾਦ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: From gratitude for creation to protection.
study.closeReading: This pauri begins with a direct act of praise, names the Divine as maker of all people and ends with sharply drawn distinctions between care for devotees and defeat of hostile forces. Reading the whole unit avoids isolating the battle image from its prayerful beginning.

words.workingGloss: Good qualities or blessings; working lexical reading

study.interpretationCare: The end uses martial rhetoric; it does not empower a reader to name neighbours as enemies, and no real-world protection outcome is guaranteed. The exact same original source stanza also occurs here as Rehras rehras.chaupai10; source context differs, do not silently conflate variant or recitation order.
study.reflection: How can I be grateful for care without treating prayer as a substitute for responsibility?
study.teachBack: What movement occurs between praise in line one and the ending battle imagery?

rehras|rehras.chaupai10.sourceContext: Exact full unit/source-text hash checked against chaupai|chaupai-rehras10

simple.en: From the smallest to the greatest, the Divine knows every heart and looks upon beings with compassion.
simple.pa: ਨਿੱਕੇ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਡੇ ਜੀਵ ਤੱਕ ਸਭ ਦੇ ਅੰਦਰਲਾ ਹਾਲ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਜਾਣਦਾ ਅਤੇ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਉੱਤੇ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਦੀ ਨਿਗਾਹ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Universal care and intimate knowledge.
study.closeReading: The poem says “ghat ghat”—heart after heart—before contrasting an ant and elephant. Size and status do not limit attention from the Divine. The final line connects this knowing to compassionate regard, a crucial correction to fear-based readings of omniscience.

words.workingGloss: A vessel; a living body or heart in devotional idiom

study.interpretationCare: Do not claim a human teacher can read another person’s heart because this verse praises Divine knowledge. The exact same original source stanza also occurs here as Rehras rehras.chaupai11; source context differs, do not silently conflate variant or recitation order.
study.reflection: Whose pain have I overlooked because they seem unimportant?
study.teachBack: Why does the ant–elephant comparison matter beside “every heart”?

rehras|rehras.chaupai11.sourceContext: Exact full unit/source-text hash checked against chaupai|chaupai-rehras11

simple.en: The speaker describes a Divine presence attentive to each person’s joy, sorrow and hidden pain.
simple.pa: ਇਹ ਪਉੜੀ ਹਰ ਜੀਵ ਦੇ ਸੁੱਖ, ਦੁੱਖ ਅਤੇ ਅੰਦਰਲੀ ਪੀੜ ਨੂੰ ਜਾਣਨ ਵਾਲੀ ਦਇਆ ਦੀ ਤਸਵੀਰ ਪੇਸ਼ ਕਰਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: A prayer of empathic awareness.
study.closeReading: The repeated pairs of suffering and happiness build toward “each one’s pain.” The final line deepens the image from outward emotions to the hidden folds within every heart. This is the poem’s language of compassion, not an instruction to read people’s minds.
study.interpretationCare: It does not mean human grief is evidence of failed prayer or that hardship can be prevented by a particular verse. The exact same original source stanza also occurs here as Rehras rehras.chaupai12; source context differs, do not silently conflate variant or recitation order.
study.reflection: How might I respond differently when another person is quietly struggling?
study.teachBack: Which phrase in this unit moves from groups of people to each individual?

rehras|rehras.chaupai12.sourceContext: Exact full unit/source-text hash checked against chaupai|chaupai-rehras12

simple.en: All embodied life comes forth through the Creator and is pictured as returning into that same Source.
simple.pa: ਸਾਰੇ ਜੀਵ ਕਰਤਾਰ ਦੇ ਪਸਾਰੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਰੂਪ ਧਾਰਦੇ ਅਤੇ ਅੰਤ ਵਿੱਚ ਉਸੇ ਮੂਲ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਮਾਉਂਦੇ ਦਿਖਾਏ ਹਨ।

study.focus: The poetic rhythm of manifestation and return.
study.closeReading: The first half imagines expansion or bringing forth of forms; the second imagines contraction or withdrawal. Both describe dependence on the Creator. The paired verbs carry the theological picture, and their exact Braj meanings still need a qualified review.
study.interpretationCare: This is not a scientific cosmology, a measured timeline or a substitute for studying physical origins of life. The exact same original source stanza also occurs here as Rehras rehras.chaupai13; source context differs, do not silently conflate variant or recitation order.
study.reflection: Can I value things that change without expecting them to last forever?
study.teachBack: What contrasting actions in lines one and three structure this pauri?

rehras|rehras.chaupai13.sourceContext: Exact full unit/source-text hash checked against chaupai|chaupai-rehras13

simple.en: Many voices speak of the Creator through their own limits, while the One remains beyond every limited description.
simple.pa: ਮਨੁੱਖ ਆਪਣੇ-ਆਪਣੇ ਗਿਆਨ ਨਾਲ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਵਰਣਦੇ ਹਨ, ਪਰ ਉਹ ਇੱਕ ਹਰ ਵਰਣਨ ਦੀ ਹੱਦ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈ।

study.focus: The humility of partial human descriptions.
study.closeReading: The opening alludes to countless mouths and ways of speaking, then names the bounds of each individual understanding. The turning point is “You remain distinct.” The lesson is not that study is useless, but that honest study remembers its own limits.

words.workingGloss: Face or mouth in this context
Separate, beyond limiting association; working gloss

study.interpretationCare: Do not use the plurality of descriptions as proof that all beliefs or religious communities hold the same teachings. The exact same original source stanza also occurs here as Rehras rehras.chaupai14; source context differs, do not silently conflate variant or recitation order.
study.reflection: When has admitting uncertainty improved a conversation?
study.teachBack: Which line stops the many descriptions from becoming a final definition of the One?

rehras|rehras.chaupai14.sourceContext: Exact full unit/source-text hash checked against chaupai|chaupai-rehras14

simple.en: The One is praised as formless, uncorrupted and beyond the beginning, while human descriptions remain incomplete.
simple.pa: ਨਿਰੰਕਾਰ, ਵਿਕਾਰ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ ਅਤੇ ਅਨਾਦਿ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਵਡਿਆਈ ਹੈ; ਮਨੁੱਖੀ ਸਮਝ ਉਸ ਦਾ ਸਾਰਾ ਭੇਦ ਨਹੀਂ ਲੱਭ ਸਕਦੀ।

study.focus: An accumulation of Divine attributes.
study.closeReading: Two densely packed lines of attributes give way to a warning about making distinctions without knowledge. The closing line notes that even venerable texts cannot exhaust the One’s mystery. This is reverence expressed through language that also confesses language is insufficient.
study.interpretationCare: Individual Sanskritic/Dasam inflections such as nirlambh and asambh require qualified philology; this is not a claim against education. The exact same original source stanza also occurs here as Rehras rehras.chaupai15; source context differs, do not silently conflate variant or recitation order.
study.reflection: How can names illuminate a reality without fully containing it?
study.teachBack: Why does a stanza full of names conclude with a warning about naming?

rehras|rehras.chaupai15.sourceContext: Exact full unit/source-text hash checked against chaupai|chaupai-rehras15

simple.en: The poet criticizes attempts to reduce the formless Divine to one object or familiar named deity.
simple.pa: ਕਵੀ ਨਿਰੰਕਾਰ ਨੂੰ ਕੇਵਲ ਇੱਕ ਵਸਤੂ ਜਾਂ ਇੱਕ ਨਾਂ ਦੀ ਹੱਦ ਵਿੱਚ ਬੰਨ੍ਹਣ ਉੱਤੇ ਸਵਾਲ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Formless reality and the danger of narrow representation.
study.closeReading: The first two lines speak sharply about making a stone stand for the limitless. The second pair invokes Mahadev and the idea of the Eternal. In its literary setting this is a Sikh theological contrast, not permission to insult any other religion.
study.interpretationCare: This polemical register can be deeply sensitive: avoid stereotyping, insulting people or erasing their religious dignity. The exact same original source stanza also occurs here as Rehras rehras.chaupai16; source context differs, do not silently conflate variant or recitation order.
study.reflection: When does a helpful symbol begin to replace what it was meant to remind us of?
study.teachBack: How do the two images in the pauri make one larger argument?

rehras|rehras.chaupai16.sourceContext: Exact full unit/source-text hash checked against chaupai|chaupai-rehras16

simple.en: People describe the Divine through limited understanding, while the scale and beginnings of creation inspire wonder.
simple.pa: ਹਰ ਕੋਈ ਆਪਣੀ ਸੀਮਤ ਸਮਝ ਨਾਲ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਵਰਣਦਾ ਹੈ; ਸਾਰੀ ਰਚਨਾ ਦਾ ਪਸਾਰਾ ਤੇ ਆਰੰਭ ਅਚਰਜ ਜਗਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Different understandings, one source beyond calculation.
study.closeReading: Line one sets the capacity of each mind; line two explains differing descriptions. The final pair expands the question beyond any individual mind to the vastness and beginning of creation. Rather than refusing knowledge, the speaker asks with humility.

words.workingGloss: Extent, expansion, the breadth of creation

study.interpretationCare: Do not convert the unanswered poetic question into a falsifiable modern scientific hypothesis. The exact same original source stanza also occurs here as Rehras rehras.chaupai17; source context differs, do not silently conflate variant or recitation order.
study.reflection: Where could greater curiosity replace my certainty?
study.teachBack: What link connects the limited mind in line one and the question in line four?

rehras|rehras.chaupai17.sourceContext: Exact full unit/source-text hash checked against chaupai|chaupai-rehras17

simple.en: The One is present through rulers and the humble, and through diverse traditional classes of living beings.
simple.pa: ਉਹ ਇੱਕੋ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਰੰਕ, ਰਾਜੇ ਅਤੇ ਵੱਖ-ਵੱਖ ਰਵਾਇਤੀ ਜਨਮ-ਰੂਪਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਆਪਣਾ ਪਸਾਰਾ ਵਿਖਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Seeing beyond social rank and conventional categories.
study.closeReading: The pair of poor and royal points away from judging value through class. The next two lines list familiar “khanis,” traditional categories of life from egg, womb, moisture and plants. Their purpose is to communicate diversity of creation, not biological taxonomy.
study.interpretationCare: The four birth classes are premodern religious categories and do not replace contemporary biological understanding. The exact same original source stanza also occurs here as Rehras rehras.chaupai18; source context differs, do not silently conflate variant or recitation order.
study.reflection: How can I treat people with equal dignity despite different social positions?
study.teachBack: How does the shift from poor and king to birth-categories widen the idea of creation?

rehras|rehras.chaupai18.sourceContext: Exact full unit/source-text hash checked against chaupai|chaupai-rehras18

simple.en: Different conditions and appearances do not limit the timeless One who brings the changing world into view.
simple.pa: ਕਿਤੇ ਰਾਜ ਦੀ ਸ਼ਾਨ ਤੇ ਕਿਤੇ ਸਿਮਟਿਆ ਰੂਪ ਦਿੱਸਦਾ ਹੈ, ਪਰ ਉਹ ਸਾਰਿਆਂ ਦਾ ਮੂਲ ਆਪ-ਹੋਂਦ ਵਾਲਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: The movement between forms and the unchanging.
study.closeReading: Two contrasting ways of appearing—expansive royal splendour and a contracted form—are followed by creation’s countless wonders. The final epithet “self-existent through ages” stops any one picture from standing for the Divine as a whole.
study.interpretationCare: The reading of “Sankar” in line two is unsettled without Braj/Dasam source comparison; do not infer a literal transformation timeline. The exact same original source stanza also occurs here as Rehras rehras.chaupai19; source context differs, do not silently conflate variant or recitation order.
study.reflection: What can change around me without altering the values that guide me?
study.teachBack: Which word at the end contrasts most strongly with the earlier changing appearances?

rehras|rehras.chaupai19.sourceContext: Exact full unit/source-text hash checked against chaupai|chaupai-rehras19

simple.en: The speaker petitions for protection during conflict, using severe historic warfare language that requires ethical and textual care.
simple.pa: ਕਵੀ ਲੜਾਈ ਅਤੇ ਸੰਕਟ ਵਿਚ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਮੰਗਦਾ ਹੈ; ਤਿੱਖੀ ਵੈਰੀ-ਭਾਸ਼ਾ ਨੂੰ ਇਤਿਹਾਸਕ ਤੇ ਨੈਤਿਕ ਸੰਦਰਭ ਨਾਲ ਸਮਝਣਾ ਲਾਜ਼ਮੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: A protective plea, with boundaries on historical polemic.
study.closeReading: The first line asks for personal rescue; the next brings Sikhs into the concern. The final two contain hostile martial terms and ask for defeat of forces causing upheaval. Source-faithful study must acknowledge their intensity while refusing to target any present-day religious or ethnic population.

words.workingGloss: Hostile or harmful person/force in the poem

study.interpretationCare: The expression “malechh” is historically charged and sometimes derogatory. Never treat it as an authorized label for contemporary non-Sikhs or as permission to harm anyone. The exact same original source stanza also occurs here as Rehras rehras.chaupai20; source context differs, do not silently conflate variant or recitation order.
study.reflection: How can protection of my community coexist with respect for every human being?
study.teachBack: How does the prayer develop from personal protection to a broader martial plea?

rehras|rehras.chaupai20.sourceContext: Exact full unit/source-text hash checked against chaupai|chaupai-rehras20

simple.en: The poem honours those who seek shelter in the Divine and asks for their troubles to be lifted.
simple.pa: ਇਹ ਪਉੜੀ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਸ਼ਰਨ ਆਉਣ ਵਾਲਿਆਂ ਦੀ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਤੇ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਸੰਕਟ ਦੂਰ ਹੋਣ ਦੀ ਬੇਨਤੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Refuge as a relationship rather than entitlement.
study.closeReading: The two paired lines each identify a seeker and the fate of adversity. “Asidhuj” names the Divine in traditional martial vocabulary. The emphasis of the complete unit is shelter for those who depend upon the One, not power granted to private aggressors.
study.interpretationCare: Do not interpret divine protection as a reason to ignore immediate physical danger or withhold practical support. The exact same original source stanza also occurs here as Rehras rehras.chaupai21; source context differs, do not silently conflate variant or recitation order.
study.reflection: What would seeking help responsibly look like in a difficult situation?
study.teachBack: Who seeks shelter in each of the two halves of this pauri?

rehras|rehras.chaupai21.sourceContext: Exact full unit/source-text hash checked against chaupai|chaupai-rehras21

simple.en: Remembrance is described in powerful images of protection from death, danger and evil.
simple.pa: ਇੱਕ ਵਾਰ ਵੀ ਸਿਮਰਨ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲੇ ਲਈ ਕਾਲ ਤੇ ਵੈਰ ਤੋਂ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਦੀ ਡੂੰਘੀ ਭਗਤੀ-ਤਸਵੀਰ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Poetic protection without false guarantees.
study.closeReading: The poem uses an intentionally strong progression: one act of remembrance; death kept at a distance; protection through time; danger dispersed. The images communicate profound trust in the Divine. A modern learner must distinguish that spiritual claim from guarantees about bodily survival.

words.workingGloss: The present age, Kaliyug, in devotional time reckoning

study.interpretationCare: Never advertise this verse as preventing death, curing illness, avoiding a car accident or substituting for emergency services. The exact same original source stanza also occurs here as Rehras rehras.chaupai22; source context differs, do not silently conflate variant or recitation order.
study.reflection: How can a prayer strengthen courage while I still take sensible precautions?
study.teachBack: What forms of protection does the stanza describe, and what does it not promise medically?

rehras|rehras.chaupai22.sourceContext: Exact full unit/source-text hash checked against chaupai|chaupai-rehras22

simple.en: The compassionate Divine gaze is praised as bringing comfort and abundance while keeping harm away.
simple.pa: ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਕਿਰਪਾ-ਦ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਟੀ ਨਾਲ ਸੁੱਖ, ਦਾਤ ਅਤੇ ਨੁਕਸਾਨ ਤੋਂ ਬਚਾਅ ਦੀ ਅਸੀਸ ਦੱਸੀ ਗਈ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Grace and the language of blessings.
study.closeReading: The first two lines connect Divine regard with relief from burning distress; the last two name riddhi-siddhi and protection from a hostile shadow. Those terms live within religious poetry and require care in translation to avoid marketing supernatural or medical claims.

words.workingGloss: Abundance or auspicious prosperity; traditional term

study.interpretationCare: These lines cannot responsibly be presented as clinical cure claims, supernatural tests or promised financial results. The exact same original source stanza also occurs here as Rehras rehras.chaupai23; source context differs, do not silently conflate variant or recitation order.
study.reflection: Can I be grateful for what I have without blaming those who are suffering?
study.teachBack: How do relief, gifts and shelter relate to the repeated idea of compassionate regard?

rehras|rehras.chaupai23.sourceContext: Exact full unit/source-text hash checked against chaupai|chaupai-rehras23

simple.en: Even a single heartfelt remembrance is praised in powerful language of freedom from fear, poverty and wrongdoing.
simple.pa: ਇੱਕ ਵਾਰ ਸਿਮਰਨ ਕਰਨ ਨਾਲ ਕਾਲ ਦੇ ਡਰ, ਦਰਿਦ੍ਰਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਦੋਖ ਤੋਂ ਮੁਕਤੀ ਦੀ ਭਗਤੀ-ਤਸਵੀਰ ਆਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: The remembered Name as spiritual refuge.
study.closeReading: The stanza begins with remembrance and the noose of death, then repeats the idea through speaking the Divine Name. Its final line gathers deprivation, hostility and moral failing into the need for deliverance. The unit is a prayer-poem, not a transactional formula.

words.workingGloss: Time, death or a Divine epithet, by context

study.interpretationCare: An interpretation that one recitation automatically clears debt or makes a person medically immortal is not supported as an empirical claim. The exact same original source stanza also occurs here as Rehras rehras.chaupai24; source context differs, do not silently conflate variant or recitation order.
study.reflection: Where might sincere remembrance help me make steadier choices today?
study.teachBack: What does the repeated return to remembering the One contribute to the stanza?

rehras|rehras.chaupai24.sourceContext: Exact full unit/source-text hash checked against chaupai|chaupai-rehras24

simple.en: The prayer returns to surrender and support, concluding the SGPC-bounded Chaupai passage at the request to protect from harm.
simple.pa: ਇਹ ਪਉੜੀ ਸ਼ਰਨ, ਰੱਖਿਆ ਅਤੇ ਹਰ ਥਾਂ ਸਹਾਇਤਾ ਦੀ ਬੇਨਤੀ ਨਾਲ ਖਤਮ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ; SGPC-ਹੱਦ ਇੱਥੇ ਆਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: An important edition and recitation boundary.
study.closeReading: Khargket is addressed as the protecting Divine; the speaker asks for rescue by hand and support everywhere. The last line, “dusht dokh te lehu bachai,” is the endpoint named in the SGPC Rehat Maryada’s specified Benti Chaupai selection. A reader should see this boundary before any extended source material.
study.interpretationCare: Our present 29-pauri candidate is broader than this SGPC excerpt. The next four pauris are tagged extended material, not silently included in every Nitnem convention. The exact same original source stanza also occurs here as Rehras rehras.chaupai25; source context differs, do not silently conflate variant or recitation order.
study.reflection: How does preserving edition boundaries show respect for different Sikh practices?
study.teachBack: Which request ends this SGPC-bounded Chaupai selection?

rehras|rehras.chaupai25.sourceContext: Exact full unit/source-text hash checked against chaupai|chaupai-rehras25

simple.en: The speaker addresses the mind: stay connected to the Divine and do not forget the source of comfort and guidance.
simple.pa: ਆਪਣੇ ਮਨ ਨੂੰ ਆਖਿਆ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ: ਹਮੇਸ਼ਾ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਲ ਜੁੜਿਆ ਰਹੁ, ਉਸ ਸਹਾਰੇ ਨੂੰ ਨਾ ਵਿਸਾਰ।

study.focus: A direct conversation with the mind.
study.closeReading: The word “mind” at the opening makes this intimate rather than abstract. The invitation to remain with the One and move through sorrow sits in a larger teaching of remembrance, not a demand to hide feelings.
study.interpretationCare: It should not be presented as clinical treatment for sadness or a promise that grief cannot occur. The exact same original source stanza also occurs here as Rehras rehras.anand02; source context differs, do not silently conflate variant or recitation order.
study.reflection: What gentle reminder would you give your mind at a difficult moment?
study.teachBack: To whom does the speaker speak, and what is repeatedly requested?

rehras|rehras.anand02.sourceContext: Exact full unit/source-text hash checked against anand|anand02

simple.en: Everything the speaker truly needs is held within the True One. The pauri turns from asking for things to cultivating praise and Naam within the mind.
simple.pa: ਸੱਚੇ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਕੋਲ ਘਾਟ ਨਹੀਂ। ਪਉੜੀ ਮੰਗਣ ਤੋਂ ਅੱਗੇ ਮਨ ਵਿਚ ਨਾਮ ਅਤੇ ਸਿਫ਼ਤ ਵਸਾਉਣ ਵੱਲ ਧਿਆਨ ਕਰਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Abundance and gratitude.
study.closeReading: The repeated rhetorical question emphasizes the Giver’s abundance. The movement toward praise and Naam keeps this from becoming simply a request for material benefits.
study.interpretationCare: A phrase about the One having everything is not a guarantee that every personal wish is granted. The exact same original source stanza also occurs here as Rehras rehras.anand03; source context differs, do not silently conflate variant or recitation order.
study.reflection: What can gratitude change even before circumstances change?
study.teachBack: How does the pauri connect abundance to remembrance?

rehras|rehras.anand03.sourceContext: Exact full unit/source-text hash checked against anand|anand03

simple.en: True Naam is described as the speaker’s support, easing the hunger of craving and bringing inward calm.
simple.pa: ਸੱਚਾ ਨਾਮ ਆਸਰਾ ਬਣਦਾ ਹੈ; ਤ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਨਾ ਦੀ ਭੁੱਖ ਘਟਦੀ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਮਨ ਨੂੰ ਸ਼ਾਂਤੀ ਮਿਲਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: A source of steadiness stronger than craving.
study.closeReading: The repeated refrain of Naam as support frames the movement. The pauri uses inner hunger and contentment imagery rather than prescribing a dietary practice.
study.interpretationCare: Do not confuse metaphorical hunger here with physical starvation or make claims about medical appetite control. The exact same original source stanza also occurs here as Rehras rehras.anand04; source context differs, do not silently conflate variant or recitation order.
study.reflection: Where does wanting more make it harder to notice what is enough?
study.teachBack: Which recurring phrase tells you what the speaker relies upon?

rehras|rehras.anand04.sourceContext: Exact full unit/source-text hash checked against anand|anand04

simple.en: The fortunate inner home resounds with Sabad. The stanza describes freedom from impulses that once overpowered the mind.
simple.pa: ਮਨ ਦੇ ਸੁਭਾਗੇ ਘਰ ਵਿਚ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਦੀ ਧੁਨ ਹੈ। ਅੰਦਰਲੇ ਵਿਕਾਰਾਂ ਦੇ ਵੱਸ ਘਟਣ ਦੀ ਤਸਵੀਰ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਗਈ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Inner music and transformation.
study.closeReading: The poetic language of five sounds, the five troublemakers and unstruck melody expresses a transformed spiritual condition. It belongs to Gurbani’s symbolism of the mind, not a numerical recipe.

words.workingGloss: Five sounds or forms in a symbolic context

study.interpretationCare: No specific sound frequency, neurological mechanism or promised effect is established by this metaphor. The exact same original source stanza also occurs here as Rehras rehras.anand05; source context differs, do not silently conflate variant or recitation order.
study.reflection: What habits lose strength when attention grows steadier?
study.teachBack: How does the imagery of music describe an inner transformation?

rehras|rehras.anand05.sourceContext: Exact full unit/source-text hash checked against anand|anand05

simple.en: The Creator alone is the True Sovereign: all lives rest within Divine order, and Naam and understanding are received through grace.
simple.pa: ਸੱਚਾ ਕਰਤਾਰ ਸਭ ਦਾ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਹੈ; ਨਾਮ ਤੇ ਸੂਝ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਨਾਲ ਮਿਲਦੇ ਅਤੇ ਸਭ ਜੀਵ ਉਸ ਦੇ ਹੁਕਮ ਵਿੱਚ ਹਨ।

study.focus: Truthful Creator, the Divine river, grace and spiritual understanding.
study.closeReading: The source begins by naming the Creator as the True Sovereign and the reality of Hukam. It moves through grace that bestows the jewel of Naam and contrasts Guru-oriented understanding with losing sight of that gift. A river then images all existence within the Divine, including encounters and separations. The second source record returns to what it means to know the One and find natural peace through the Guru.

words.workingGloss: River; metaphor for the One holding all beings

study.interpretationCare: The river and the Divine source of meetings are spiritual metaphor, not a literal hydrological account. Hukam never excuses abuse or eliminates the need for responsible action.
study.reflection: How might recognizing something larger than myself change my response to an unexpected separation?
study.teachBack: How does the image of a river connect the hymn’s first source record with the second?

simple.en: The mind caught in the muddy pool of attachment is invited to turn again toward the One through remembrance and humility.
simple.pa: ਮੋਹ ਦੇ ਚਿੱਕੜ ਵਿੱਚ ਫਸਿਆ ਮਨ ਨਾਮ ਦੀ ਯਾਦ ਅਤੇ ਨਿਮਰਤਾ ਰਾਹੀਂ ਇੱਕ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਵੱਲ ਮੁੜਨ ਦੀ ਸੇਧ ਪਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Burning water and feet caught in the mud of attachment.
study.closeReading: The opening places human life in a troubling pool: its water is described as fire, while attachment is mud in which the foot cannot move. This reading does not introduce a lotus. The refrain then turns from the scene to the mind, whose qualities fade as it forgets Hari. In the closing first-person plea, the speaker does not claim mastery through learning or discipline, but seeks refuge among those who remember the One.

words.workingGloss: Attachment, imaged here as trapping mud; working gloss
Fire; part of the pool’s image of craving

study.interpretationCare: The contextual mud reading follows the consulted commentaries and does not change the source spelling. The disturbing pool is spiritual imagery, not a diagnosis of psychological illness or a reason to shame another person.
study.reflection: What attachment might keep me from acting according to my deeper values?
study.teachBack: How do burning water and feet caught in mud lead into the appeal to remember the One?

simple.en: The poet repeats salutations to the unassailable One, then names generosity and boundlessness.
simple.pa: ਕਵੀ ਅਜਿੱਤ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਮੁੜ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਤੇ ਉਸ ਦੀ ਉਦਾਰਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਅਪਾਰਤਾ ਯਾਦ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Repetition adds depth, not a score of spoken words.
study.closeReading: Chhand 8 deliberately repeats the first two descriptive salutations from Chhand 4, then shifts toward Udare and Apare. The pattern teaches that the One is beyond destruction and also generous and without limit. It is a sequence of names/attributes, not four unrelated deities or instructions to perform four physical acts.

words.workingGloss: Unassailable or not destroyed; working gloss
Boundless or beyond a measurable end

study.interpretationCare: The lexical forms require qualified Dasam/Braj review; Divine generosity is not a contractual guarantee that an individual will receive money or avoid injury.
study.reflection: What does repeating an idea help me notice that I might miss once?
study.teachBack: How do the final two titles extend the first two?

simple.en: The One is praised through unity and multiplicity, with further titles whose precise meanings need careful comparison.
simple.pa: ਇੱਕ ਅਤੇ ਅਨੇਕ ਦੇ ਰੂਪ ਵਿੱਚ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਵਡਿਆਈ ਹੈ; ਅਗਲੇ ਵਿਸ਼ੇਸ਼ਣਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਧਿਆਨ ਨਾਲ ਸਮਝਣ ਤੇ ਪਰਖਣ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Unity, multiplicity and the limits of a short gloss.
study.closeReading: The first pair places One beside Many. The next pair must be read on its own terms rather than treated as two interchangeable words for form. Abhute concerns created or elemental existence in the working draft; Ajupe is rendered here through freedom from constraint, with another documented reading noted beside the line. Comparing these meanings is part of the lesson, not a reason to alter the source.
study.interpretationCare: The Ajupe line retains an explicit alternative reading. These explanatory choices are provisional and should not be turned into a definitive account of cosmology or an official lexical judgment.
study.reflection: Can I notice both a shared ground and real differences without flattening either?
study.teachBack: Which two opening titles form a contrast, and why should the last two be examined separately?

simple.en: The One is praised as beyond limiting actions, confusion, place and costume.
simple.pa: ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਕਰਮਾਂ ਦੇ ਬੰਧਨ, ਭਰਮ, ਥਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਭੇਖ ਦੀਆਂ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਯਾਦ ਕੀਤਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Negative titles protect against narrow definitions.
study.closeReading: The four original salutation-lines describe what cannot confine the Divine: action and its binding consequences, bewilderment, a geographical region and a specific mode of dress. This does not make action, learning or respect for places meaningless; rather, the verse separates a human limitation from the Source revered by the speaker.

words.workingGloss: Not limited by binding action, working gloss
Without a limiting costume or appearance

study.interpretationCare: Negative Braj prefixes need qualified linguistic review. The teaching does not excuse immoral actions, reject geography or dismiss sincere physical worship.
study.reflection: What external appearance do I sometimes mistake for real understanding?
study.teachBack: What four categories does this stanza say cannot fully define the One?

simple.en: The salutations move through name, desire, bodily constituents and destruction as limits that do not define the One.
simple.pa: ਨਾਮ, ਚਾਹ, ਸਰੀਰ ਦੇ ਤੱਤ ਅਤੇ ਨਾਸ ਦੀਆਂ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਾ ਬੱਝਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕੀਤੀ ਗਈ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Distinguishing a body’s constituents from its support.
study.closeReading: The first two titles concern naming and desire. The third is now explained through bodily constituents rather than dependence on an external support. The fourth concerns destruction or harm. Reading the four separately helps prevent a plausible general idea about God from being substituted for the particular word on the page. Each salutation still addresses the same One.

words.workingGloss: Not defined by a name; working gloss

study.interpretationCare: Nirdhate receives a documented constituent-related reading, while exact historical morphology still needs specialist review. Praise of the Divine does not imply that a person can become physically immune to harm.
study.reflection: When can a familiar idea keep me from noticing what a text actually says?
study.teachBack: How is a description about bodily constituents different from a description about needing support?

simple.en: This sequence praises steadiness and freedom from created limitations, ordinary sight and sorrow.
simple.pa: ਇਹ ਲੜੀ ਅਡੋਲਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਸਿਰਜੀਆਂ ਹੱਦਾਂ, ਆਮ ਨਿਗਾਹ ਤੇ ਸੋਗ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਵਡਿਆਈ ਕਰਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Giving each repeated salutation its own meaning.
study.closeReading: Four salutations share a repeated opening but differ in their descriptive words. The first is read through steadiness, without adding an unsupported claim about stain. Abhute and Aloke then introduce different interpretive questions about created existence and seeing. Asoke brings sorrow into the sequence. The repetition is a reason to listen carefully for the changing title, rather than to assume all four mean the same thing.

words.workingGloss: Steady or not shaken; working gloss

study.interpretationCare: The revised first gloss follows a movement-related reading; the remaining old-language details are still provisional. Describing the Divine as free from sorrow is not a demand that human beings suppress grief.
study.reflection: What changes when I attend to a repeated phrase instead of rushing past it?
study.teachBack: How does the fourth title differ in subject from the first title?

simple.en: The sequence moves from freedom from affliction and dependence on establishment to reverence and the image of treasure.
simple.pa: ਛੰਦ ਤਾਪ ਅਤੇ ਕਿਸੇ ਦੇ ਸਥਾਪਿਤ ਕੀਤੇ ਹੋਣ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਗੱਲ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਫਿਰ ਉਸ ਦੇ ਮਾਣ ਅਤੇ ਨਿਧਾਨ-ਰੂਪ ਨੂੰ ਯਾਦ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: An affirmative title within a sequence of negations.
study.closeReading: The first two descriptive titles have negative force, but that pattern must not automatically be extended to the third. Trimane affirms reverence; its precise threefold reference has more than one documented explanation. Nidhane then introduces a treasury image. The sequence therefore changes its rhetorical movement, and that change would be lost by translating every unfamiliar title as beyond something.

words.workingGloss: Revered across the three times or worlds; working alternatives

study.interpretationCare: The temporal and worlds-based readings of Trimane need qualified comparison. The title is not being treated as a claim about measured dimensions, and the treasury image does not promise material reward.
study.reflection: Do I let an apparent pattern decide a word’s meaning before I examine it?
study.teachBack: Why should the negative sense of the first two titles not be imposed on Trimane?

simple.en: The One is praised as unfathomable, steadfast and uncreated; the threefold title carries a provisional reading.
simple.pa: ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਅਥਾਹਤਾ, ਅਡੋਲਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਅਜਨਮੇ ਹੋਣ ਦੀ ਵਡਿਆਈ ਹੈ; ਤਿੰਨਾਂ ਗੁਣਾਂ ਵਾਲੇ ਵਿਸ਼ੇਸ਼ਣ ਦਾ ਅਰਥ ਹਾਲੇ ਸਮੀਖਿਆ ਅਧੀਨ ਹੈ।

study.focus: A repeated title and a distinct threefold expression.
study.closeReading: Agahe opens the chhand with the difficulty of fathoming the One. Abahe repeats a title from Chhand 6 and is explained consistently through steadiness. Tribarge introduces a different threefold expression; the line note identifies the working interpretation used here instead of disguising it as a settled lexical result. Asarge closes the sequence by addressing the One as uncreated. These four titles need not all be paraphrased with the same negative formula.
study.interpretationCare: The threefold reference in Tribarge remains a matter for specialist comparison. A theological description of the gunas is not a scientific classification of people or a measure of their worth.
study.reflection: What makes a clear statement of uncertainty more useful than a vague explanation?
study.teachBack: Which title also occurs in Chhand 6, and which title has the explicitly provisional threefold reading?

simple.en: The opening invokes complete Divine joy and fitting union; the final pair turns to colour and indestructibility.
simple.pa: ਸ਼ੁਰੂ ਵਿੱਚ ਪੂਰਨ ਰੱਬੀ ਆਨੰਦ ਅਤੇ ਸੁਚੱਜੇ ਮਿਲਾਪ ਨੂੰ ਯਾਦ ਕੀਤਾ ਹੈ; ਅਖੀਰਲੀ ਜੋੜੀ ਰੰਗ ਅਤੇ ਅਭੰਗਤਾ ਵੱਲ ਮੁੜਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: A shared meaning across the two teaching languages.
study.closeReading: The revised opening explanation presents the same bliss-related working sense in English and Punjabi. Sujoge then introduces the question of fitting union or relationship, whose precise interpretation remains provisional. The final two titles change direction toward colour and what cannot be broken. The student can notice that movement without assuming that a short translation exhausts any of these words.

words.workingGloss: Not broken or destroyed; working gloss

study.interpretationCare: Prabhoge and Sujoge remain interpretive working readings. The description of Divine joy does not require a constant human mood, and language about colour must not be used to rank skin tones or caste.
study.reflection: How can two explanations in different languages support the same careful understanding?
study.teachBack: How does the final pair of titles change the focus introduced by the opening pair?

simple.en: The One is beyond our complete grasp yet present throughout existence, supporting the waters while depending on no other support.
simple.pa: ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਸਾਡੀ ਪੂਰੀ ਸਮਝ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੁੰਦਿਆਂ ਵੀ ਸਾਰੀ ਹੋਂਦ ਵਿੱਚ ਵਿਆਪਕ ਹੈ; ਉਹ ਜਲ ਦਾ ਆਸਰਾ ਹੈ, ਪਰ ਆਪ ਕਿਸੇ ਹੋਰ ਦੇ ਆਸਰੇ ਨਹੀਂ।

study.focus: Presence and support without confinement or dependence.
study.closeReading: The first two salutations hold reach and presence together: our understanding cannot contain the One, yet the selected reading does not place the One outside existence. The final pair then turns to support. Water is named before the description of independence. Read the four lines as a movement of attention, from the limits of our knowing to what sustains life and finally to the One who needs no support. This sequence offers a way to contemplate dependence without reducing the Divine to another dependent thing.

words.workingGloss: Beyond complete reach or comprehension; working sense
Support of the waters; selected reading, with an ocean-image alternative

study.interpretationCare: The pervading and water-support readings are choices among documented alternatives. Keep them visible as working interpretations; the lesson does not prescribe isolation or refusing help in human life.
study.reflection: What sustains my daily life that I seldom pause to acknowledge?
study.teachBack: How do the final two titles place support beside independence?

simple.en: Caste, lineage and creed cannot contain the One; the final salutation answers that freedom with wonder.
simple.pa: ਜਾਤ, ਗੋਤ ਅਤੇ ਮਜ਼ਹਬ ਦੀਆਂ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਨਹੀਂ ਬੰਨ੍ਹ ਸਕਦੀਆਂ; ਅਖੀਰਲੀ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਉਸ ਦੇ ਅਸਚਰਜ ਸਰੂਪ ਵੱਲ ਮੁੜਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Reverence that exceeds inherited labels.
study.closeReading: In the selected reading, the first three titles successively loosen the claim that caste, family descent or a religious label can define the Divine. The speaker continues to bow through all three: removing a limit does not remove devotion. The fourth title changes the movement. Instead of another negation, it names wonder. A student can notice how the passage opens a space for reverence after familiar classifications have proved too small, and can ask how inherited labels affect the way we regard other people.

words.workingGloss: Beyond clan or lineage; selected reading, with an unfailing alternative

study.interpretationCare: The caste and clan senses are selected readings of the opening pair. The passage does not make a person’s background shameful or give one community permission to claim exclusive possession of the Divine.
study.reflection: Which inherited label most quickly affects the way I listen to someone?
study.teachBack: What changes when the final title moves from negation to wonder?

simple.en: No country, outward guise or dwelling encloses the One; the final title is read here as freedom from Maya’s binding hold.
simple.pa: ਕੋਈ ਦੇਸ, ਭੇਖ ਜਾਂ ਨਿਵਾਸ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਸੀਮਤ ਨਹੀਂ ਕਰਦਾ; ਆਖ਼ਰੀ ਨਾਮ ਨੂੰ ਇੱਥੇ ਮਾਇਆ ਦੇ ਬੰਧਨ ਤੋਂ ਨਿਰਲੇਪ ਹੋਣ ਦੇ ਭਾਵ ਵਿੱਚ ਪੜ੍ਹਿਆ ਹੈ।

study.focus: No address or appearance can contain the Divine.
study.closeReading: The sequence passes through country, guise and dwelling. These are familiar ways of locating and recognising a person, yet each fails to contain the One being addressed. The chosen final reading adds freedom from Maya’s hold. Notice that the poem still speaks directly and intimately to the One while refusing to assign a permanent address or costume. Chhand 22 will widen the picture with presence in all places; the two passages can be read together as freedom from confinement alongside universal presence.

words.workingGloss: Not confined to an outward guise
Unaffected by Maya; selected reading among several

study.interpretationCare: The last title has more than one interpretation. Treat Maya here as binding attachment, without turning its traditional personification into a judgement about women or marriage.
study.reflection: Where do I tend to assume that the Divine can be present only in familiar surroundings?
study.teachBack: Which three ways of locating or identifying someone does this chhand move beyond?

simple.en: The chhand addresses the One through ending, compassion, every form and universal sovereignty, repeating “all” in each salutation.
simple.pa: ਇਹ ਛੰਦ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਸਭ ਦੇ ਅੰਤ, ਸਭ ਉੱਤੇ ਦਇਆ, ਸਭ ਰੂਪਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਵਿਆਪਕਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਸਭ ਦੀ ਮਾਲਕੀ ਰਾਹੀਂ ਯਾਦ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ; ਹਰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਵਿੱਚ “ਸਰਬ” ਆਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Universal power held together with universal compassion.
study.closeReading: Listen for ਸਰਬ before each changing title. Ending, mercy, form and sovereignty are all placed within that repeated scope. The second line is especially significant beside the first: the One addressed as the end of created things is also addressed as compassionate toward all. The final pair then takes the gaze across forms and their ruler. Reading the whole chhand keeps any single attribute from becoming the entire portrait and invites a reverence large enough to hold power and mercy together.

words.workingGloss: All; the repeated scope of each title
Time, death or ending; the ending sense is selected here

study.interpretationCare: The time-related title has more than one reading. The verse does not identify a particular loss as punishment or give the reader knowledge of why another person suffers.
study.reflection: How might remembering compassion change what I admire in power?
study.teachBack: What does the repeated ਸਰਬ contribute to all four titles?

simple.en: Both becoming and passing away lie under the One’s power, and the chhand closes by remembering care for all.
simple.pa: ਹੋਂਦ ਵਿੱਚ ਆਉਣਾ ਅਤੇ ਲੀਨ ਹੋਣਾ ਇੱਕੋ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੇ ਅਧੀਨ ਹਨ; ਛੰਦ ਅਖੀਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਭ ਦੀ ਪਾਲਣਾ ਨੂੰ ਯਾਦ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Making, ending and sustaining in paired titles.
study.closeReading: Notice the paired sounds ਖਾਪੇ/ਥਾਪੇ and ਕਾਲੇ/ਪਾਲੇ. The first pair brings dissolution beside establishment; the second places ending beside nurture. Every line addresses the same One, and every line repeats ਸਰਬ. The prayer therefore does not reserve Divine presence for beginnings alone or care for one favoured group. Its last word leaves the learner with sustenance after acknowledging change. A useful reflection is to hold gratitude for what is given together with humility about what we cannot make permanent.
study.interpretationCare: Dissolution is praised here as a Divine attribute. The lines give no command for people to destroy life or neglect their own responsibilities of care.
study.reflection: What can I care for today even though I cannot make it permanent?
study.teachBack: Which pair names dissolution and establishment, and which final word names nurture?

simple.en: The prayer honours Divine radiance, mystery and birthlessness, then closes with a title provisionally understood as wondrous beauty.
simple.pa: ਪ੍ਰਾਰਥਨਾ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੇ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਸ਼, ਅਥਾਹ ਭੇਦ ਅਤੇ ਅਜਨਮੇ ਸਰੂਪ ਨੂੰ ਯਾਦ ਕਰਦੀ ਹੈ; ਆਖ਼ਰੀ ਨਾਮ ਨੂੰ ਇੱਥੇ ਅਸਥਾਈ ਤੌਰ ਤੇ ਸੁੰਦਰਤਾ ਦੇ ਭਾਵ ਵਿੱਚ ਪੜ੍ਹਿਆ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Wonder without claiming to contain the Divine.
study.closeReading: The opening holds radiance beside mystery: something can be praised as light without being completely grasped. The third line removes birth as a limit on Divine being. In this draft, the final salutation returns to beauty and reverence. Notice how the speaker keeps addressing the One even while language reaches its limits. ਸੁਬਨਮੇ also has a world-as-offspring reading; that would make the final pair about the birthless source and its creation, so the alternative changes the emphasis and deserves attention.

words.workingGloss: Unfathomable; selected reading, with other senses of ਭੇਦ recorded
Wondrous beauty or splendour; provisional, not a settled derivation

study.interpretationCare: The final title remains a philological question. Preserve the source spelling and distinguish the selected beauty reading from the creation-as-offspring reading; neither is silently declared the only correct sense.
study.reflection: Can I express love and reverence while admitting that I do not fully understand?
study.teachBack: Which title clearly names birthlessness, and which has the unsettled beauty and offspring readings?

simple.en: The One is present through every place and form, while no created form escapes dissolution.
simple.pa: ਇੱਕੋ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਹਰ ਥਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਹਰ ਰੂਪ ਵਿੱਚ ਵਿਆਪਕ ਹੈ; ਸਿਰਜਿਆ ਕੋਈ ਵੀ ਰੂਪ ਸਦਾ ਕਾਇਮ ਨਹੀਂ ਰਹਿੰਦਾ।

study.focus: Everywhere present, while forms remain changeable.
study.closeReading: ਸਰਬ appears four times again, opening each title outward. The first pair joins going with dwelling: presence reaches every place and abides throughout the worlds. The second pair joins the variety of colours with the dissolution of forms. Read this beside Chhand 18: freedom from one fixed abode can coexist with presence in every abode. Likewise, a form can express beauty without becoming permanent. The passage invites attentive regard for a changing creation while keeping the One beyond any single appearance.

words.workingGloss: Going or reaching; here expressing presence everywhere
Dwelling throughout worlds or realms; working sense

study.interpretationCare: Going and dwelling are poetic ways to speak about Divine presence. This lesson does not assign a physical route or a bounded body to the One.
study.reflection: How might noticing change make my attention to the world more grateful and careful?
study.teachBack: How do going and dwelling complement one another before colour and dissolution appear?

simple.en: The stanza places sovereignty over death beside compassion. Its praise ends with the One beyond a complete description and beyond dying; strength and mercy remain together throughout the address.
simple.pa: ਇਸ ਛੰਦ ਵਿੱਚ ਮੌਤ ਉੱਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਸਰਦਾਰੀ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਉਸ ਦੀ ਦਇਆ ਆਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ। ਅਖੀਰਲੀਆਂ ਤੁਕਾਂ ਉਸ ਦੇ ਬੇਅੰਤ ਵਰਣਨ ਅਤੇ ਅਮਰ ਹੋਂਦ ਵੱਲ ਧਿਆਨ ਲਿਆਉਂਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ। ਇੱਕੋ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਸਮਰੱਥਾ ਅਤੇ ਮਿਹਰ ਨੂੰ ਇਕੱਠਿਆਂ ਯਾਦ ਕੀਤਾ ਗਿਆ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Hear compassion within the praise of a power greater than death.
study.closeReading: The first and fourth lines form a frame: death is named at the start, and deathlessness at the close. Inside that frame, ਦਿਆਲੇ prevents the strong opening from becoming a portrait of power alone. ਅਬਰਨੇ also checks the reader’s confidence that a few descriptions could contain the One being praised. A useful reading practice is to pause after each epithet, then join the four again. Each salutation adds a quality; none should erase the others.

words.workingGloss: the One sovereign even over death and time
beyond description here; also read as without a defining colour

study.interpretationCare: These are devotional descriptions of the Divine. They offer no guarantee that illness, loss or physical death will spare a person who recites them. The two attested senses of ਅਬਰਨੇ remain an editorial question.
study.reflection: When you imagine strength, how much room do you leave for tenderness and mercy?
study.teachBack: Show how the opening and closing lines frame the stanza, then explain what ਦਿਆਲੇ adds inside that frame.

simple.en: The working reading praises the ageless Creator, present in the unfolding of every activity yet free from its bonds. The last two lines hold action and freedom together; the first two epithets retain recorded alternatives.
simple.pa: ਇਸ ਕਾਰਜਕਾਰੀ ਅਰਥ ਵਿੱਚ ਬੁਢਾਪੇ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ ਕਰਤਾਰ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ। ਜਗਤ ਦੇ ਕਾਰ-ਵਿਹਾਰ ਉਸ ਦੀ ਸੱਤਾ ਨਾਲ ਚੱਲਦੇ ਹਨ, ਪਰ ਉਹ ਆਪ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਬੰਧਨਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਹੀਂ ਬੱਝਦਾ। ਪਹਿਲੇ ਦੋ ਵਿਸ਼ੇਸ਼ਣਾਂ ਦੇ ਹੋਰ ਟੀਕਾਕਾਰੀ ਅਰਥ ਵੀ ਸਮੀਖਿਆ ਲਈ ਸੰਭਾਲੇ ਗਏ ਹਨ।

study.focus: Read action and freedom from bondage together, while noticing where lexical readings differ.
study.closeReading: The clearest structural turn comes between ਸਰਬ ਧੰਧੇ and ਅਬੰਧੇ. The stanza first directs attention across the many engagements of the world and then denies that those engagements bind the One addressed. That contrast remains useful whichever documented reading of the first pair is preferred. Our main explanation uses agelessness and creative agency; the alternatives are might and release from karmic bonds. Holding those options honestly keeps a short devotional explanation from pretending to settle a scholarly question.

words.workingGloss: Creator here; alternatively cutter of karmic bonds

study.interpretationCare: Freedom from bondage is a Divine attribute in this address, not permission to evade responsibility. The ageless/mighty and Creator/karmic-liberator readings require qualified linguistic review; neither alternative is a change to the original line.
study.reflection: Can you attend carefully to a task without making its outcome the whole measure of your worth?
study.teachBack: Explain the relationship between ਸਰਬ ਧੰਧੇ and ਅਬੰਧੇ, and name one lexical question that this draft leaves open.
