simple.en: The One is free from limiting kinship and fear, yet full of mercy and generosity. The movement of the stanza joins independence with care, so freedom does not become emotional distance.
simple.pa: ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਸਾਕ-ਸੰਬੰਧਾਂ ਦੀਆਂ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਡਰ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ ਹੈ, ਪਰ ਉਸੇ ਨੂੰ ਰਹਿਮ ਅਤੇ ਬਖ਼ਸ਼ਿਸ਼ ਵਾਲਾ ਵੀ ਕਿਹਾ ਗਿਆ ਹੈ। ਛੰਦ ਆਜ਼ਾਦੀ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਦਇਆ ਨੂੰ ਜੋੜਦਾ ਹੈ; ਨਿਰਲੇਪਤਾ ਦਾ ਭਾਵ ਬੇਪਰਵਾਹੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਬਣਦਾ।

study.focus: Notice how the stanza joins freedom from constraint with a generous relationship to others.
study.closeReading: The first pair removes two familiar constraints: the claims of a particular kin group and the pressure of fear. The second pair speaks positively of mercy and generosity. Read in sequence, these qualities keep the first pair from sounding like withdrawal from care. ਨ੍ਰਿਸਾਕੇ and ਨ੍ਰਿਬਾਕੇ share a sound pattern, while ਰਹੀਮੇ and ਕਰੀਮੇ answer with another. Those audible pairs support memory, but each word still contributes its own meaning to the praise.
study.interpretationCare: The stanza does not ask people to abandon family or shame those who feel fear. Its address is to the Divine. A personal reflection about care without favouritism is an application, not a literal translation of ਨ੍ਰਿਸਾਕੇ.
study.reflection: Where could your kindness extend beyond the people you already count as your own?
study.teachBack: Explain why the second pair matters when interpreting the first pair, using one word from each pair.

simple.en: Limitless greatness is followed by the language of love and blessedness. The stanza lets closeness and wonder coexist: the One beyond every measure is also addressed through qualities that touch the heart.
simple.pa: ਬੇਅੰਤਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਮਹਾਨਤਾ ਤੋਂ ਬਾਅਦ ਛੰਦ ਪ੍ਰੇਮ ਅਤੇ ਸੁਹਾਗ-ਭਾਗ ਦੀ ਬੋਲੀ ਲਿਆਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਹਰ ਮਾਪ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈ, ਫਿਰ ਵੀ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਦਿਲ ਨਾਲ ਜੁੜੇ ਗੁਣਾਂ ਰਾਹੀਂ ਯਾਦ ਕੀਤਾ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਅਚਰਜ ਅਤੇ ਨੇੜਤਾ ਇਕੱਠੇ ਰਹਿੰਦੇ ਹਨ।

study.focus: Let the movement from greatness to love shape the reading of the whole stanza.
study.closeReading: ਅਨੰਤੇ and ਮਹੰਤੇ open the address toward what exceeds a reader’s scale. ਰਾਗੇ then changes the emphasis: greatness is also spoken of through love. ਸੁਹਾਗੇ follows with a word whose field includes blessed fortune and relational happiness. This draft chooses blessedness as its main sense and keeps the other readings visible. The sequence is worth hearing as a whole: wonder at the immeasurable does not prevent an intimate, affectionate address to the same One.

words.workingGloss: love; loving affection in this reading
blessedness or auspiciousness here; relational readings also occur

study.interpretationCare: The use of ਰਾਗੇ here is not a specification of musical raag. ਸੁਹਾਗੇ has several attested explanatory senses; its relationship imagery must not become a judgment about the spiritual worth of unmarried or widowed people.
study.reflection: Does thinking of the Divine as immeasurably great make loving address easier or harder for you?
study.teachBack: Describe the shift between the first two and last two epithets, and explain the working sense chosen for ਰਾਗੇ.

simple.en: Four universal actions are placed together: dissolving, nourishing, creating and bringing to an end. Their shared address recognises the One throughout the life of creation, including both its growth and its passing.
simple.pa: ਚਾਰਾਂ ਤੁਕਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਭ ਨੂੰ ਮਿਟਾਉਣ, ਪਾਲਣ, ਸਿਰਜਣ ਅਤੇ ਅੰਤ ਤਕ ਲਿਆਉਣ ਦੀ ਸੱਤਾ ਇੱਕੋ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨਾਲ ਜੋੜੀ ਹੈ। ਜਗਤ ਦੇ ਵਧਣ ਅਤੇ ਮੁੱਕਣ ਦੋਹਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਉਸ ਇੱਕ ਨੂੰ ਯਾਦ ਕੀਤਾ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਹਰ ਤੁਕ ਦਾ “ਸਰਬ” ਇਸ ਗੱਲ ਨੂੰ ਸਭ ਵੱਲ ਫੈਲਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Follow the two contrasting pairs without dropping either nourishment or dissolution.
study.closeReading: Every line repeats ਨਮੋ ਸਰਬ, so the scope stays wide even as the action changes. The first pair moves from dissolution to nourishment; the second moves from creation to dissolution. This is not a chronological timetable. It is a compact arrangement of contrasting powers within one act of praise. Looking closely at ਸੋਖੰ and ਪੋਖੰ also shows why sound alone is not enough for interpretation: their closeness on the page and in recitation accompanies a meaningful difference.

words.workingGloss: remover; one who brings to an end

study.interpretationCare: The lines praise cosmic creation, preservation and dissolution. They do not license human cruelty or explain a particular person’s suffering as deserved. No date or mechanism of the world’s end is stated here.
study.reflection: What changes when you remember both the nourishment you receive and the passing nature of what you possess?
study.teachBack: Identify the two contrasting pairs and explain why ਸੋਖੰ cannot be substituted with the familiar word ਸੁਖ.

simple.en: The supreme Yogi and supreme enjoyer are praised as the same One. The stanza then turns to mercy and care for all, bringing its striking opening pair into a shared devotional address.
simple.pa: ਪਰਮ ਜੋਗੀ ਅਤੇ ਪਰਮ ਭੋਗੀ ਕਹਿ ਕੇ ਇੱਕੋ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕੀਤੀ ਹੈ। ਫਿਰ ਉਸ ਦੀ ਸਭ ਉੱਤੇ ਦਇਆ ਅਤੇ ਸਭ ਦੀ ਪਾਲਣਾ ਯਾਦ ਕੀਤੀ ਜਾਂਦੀ ਹੈ। ਜੋਗ ਅਤੇ ਭੋਗ ਦੇ ਵੱਖਰੇ ਪੱਖ ਇੱਕੋ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਉਸਤਤਿ ਵਿੱਚ ਇਕੱਠੇ ਆਉਂਦੇ ਹਨ।

study.focus: Read the paired intensifications of ਜੋਗ and ਭੋਗ alongside universal compassion and care.
study.closeReading: The first two lines repeat their key word within each salutation: ਜੋਗ ਜੋਗੇ, then ਭੋਗ ਭੋਗੇ. A reader should notice that the praise does not choose one and reject the other. The same address holds the freedom associated with the Yogi and the fullness associated with enjoyment. The last pair changes to ਸਰਬ and extends compassion and nurture to all. This also closes the present Bhujang Prayat section before the new metrical heading introduces Chhand 29.

words.workingGloss: supreme in yogic union or detachment
supreme enjoyer; also explained through fullness of bliss

study.interpretationCare: ਭੋਗ here is a Divine epithet, not permission for harmful excess, and ਜੋਗ does not prescribe a bodily technique. The original ਦਿਆਲੇ is retained even where a commentary site shows a different reading.
study.reflection: How might gratitude for ordinary joys coexist with freedom from the need to possess them?
study.teachBack: Explain how the first two lines hold a striking pair together, and show what the final two lines add.

simple.en: A new Chachari metre opens with four brief addresses: formless, incomparable, birthless and beyond material composition. The repeated “You are” sustains a personal address even while each epithet denies a familiar limit.
simple.pa: ਚਾਚਰੀ ਛੰਦ ਦੀ ਨਵੀਂ ਚਾਲ ਵਿੱਚ ਚਾਰ ਛੋਟੀਆਂ ਤੁਕਾਂ ਆਉਂਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ। ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਰੂਪ ਦੀ ਹੱਦ, ਤੁਲਨਾ, ਜਨਮ ਅਤੇ ਪਦਾਰਥਕ ਬਣਤਰ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਕਿਹਾ ਹੈ। ਹਰ ਤੁਕ ਦਾ “ਹੈਂ” ਉਸੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨਾਲ ਸਿੱਧੇ ਸੰਬੋਧਨ ਦਾ ਨਾਤਾ ਬਣਾਈ ਰੱਖਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Notice the new metrical heading and the movement from repeated salutations to “You are”.
study.closeReading: The separate heading names ਚਾਚਰੀ ਛੰਦ and invokes ਤ੍ਵ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਦਿ, by Your grace. The four verse lines then share the compact pattern of an epithet followed by ਹੈਂ. This differs visibly from the preceding repeated ਨਮੋ, yet the devotional address continues. The repeated opening ਅ also invites close attention to each word rather than treating all four as interchangeable. Our working readings of ਅਜੂ and ਅਭੂ are birthlessness and freedom from material composition; documented alternatives remain in the line notes.

words.workingGloss: not composed of material elements here; alternatively uncreated

study.interpretationCare: The traditional five-element explanation is a philosophical vocabulary, not a claim about modern chemistry. The heading is separate from the four verse lines. This lesson identifies the metrical change but does not prescribe an authoritative recitation speed or pronunciation.
study.reflection: How does directly saying “You are” feel different from only listing qualities about someone?
study.teachBack: Identify the change in address and name the working meanings of ਅਜੂ and ਅਭੂ, including one recorded alternative.

simple.en: Description, dress, name and desire cannot confine the One addressed. These four brief lines invite humility about the labels people use, while continuing the personal, reverent address established in Chhand 29.
simple.pa: ਲੇਖੇ, ਭੇਖ, ਨਾਮ ਅਤੇ ਕਾਮਨਾ ਦੀਆਂ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਨਹੀਂ ਬੰਨ੍ਹਦੀਆਂ। ਇਹ ਚਾਰ ਛੋਟੀਆਂ ਤੁਕਾਂ ਮਨੁੱਖੀ ਲੇਬਲਾਂ ਦੀ ਸੀਮਾ ਯਾਦ ਕਰਾਉਂਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ। ਨਾਲ ਹੀ ਪਿਛਲੇ ਛੰਦ ਵਾਂਗ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨਾਲ ਸਿੱਧਾ ਅਤੇ ਆਦਰ ਭਰਿਆ ਸੰਬੋਧਨ ਜਾਰੀ ਰਹਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Understand negation as a limit on human categories, while keeping the address alive.
study.closeReading: The four lines retain the same short ਹੈਂ pattern. ਅਲੇਖ concerns an account or description; ਅਭੇਖ an outward presentation; ਅਨਾਮ a defining name; ਅਕਾਮ desire. Distinguishing those four domains gives the repetition depth. The third line is especially striking inside a composition full of Divine names: using a name does not mean its speaker has exhausted the One it addresses. The final line then shifts from how something is represented to what might motivate it.

words.workingGloss: beyond a complete account or description
not defined by an outward garb

study.interpretationCare: These negations describe the Divine; they do not abolish human responsibilities, meaningful religious practice or the remembrance of Naam. Desirelessness here should not be turned into shame about ordinary human needs.
study.reflection: Which label do you most readily mistake for a complete understanding of someone or something?
study.teachBack: Give the four distinct limits named in this stanza and explain why ਅਨਾਮ does not make devotional naming meaningless.

simple.en: The chhand moves from the limits of our contemplation and understanding to Divine freedom from conquest and fear. Its brief “You are” statements sustain a direct relationship even where full comprehension is impossible.
simple.pa: ਇਹ ਛੰਦ ਸਾਡੇ ਧਿਆਨ ਅਤੇ ਸਮਝ ਦੀਆਂ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਅੱਗੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਅਜਿੱਤਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਨਿਰਭਉਤਾ ਵੱਲ ਲੈ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਛੋਟੇ “ਹੈਂ” ਵਾਲੇ ਬਚਨ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨਾਲ ਸਿੱਧਾ ਸੰਬੋਧਨ ਬਣਾਈ ਰੱਖਦੇ ਹਨ, ਭਾਵੇਂ ਉਸ ਦਾ ਪੂਰਾ ਭੇਦ ਨਾ ਪਾਇਆ ਜਾ ਸਕੇ।

study.focus: Reverence without a claim to mental possession.
study.closeReading: Each line ends with ਹੈਂ, keeping the One directly addressed. In the selected opening readings, neither contemplation nor explanation makes the Divine an object we can fully possess in thought. The closing pair then changes the question: no opposing power can conquer or intimidate the One. Notice the difference between knowing a title and mastering what it names. The speaker can address the Divine with confidence while remaining modest about understanding. The first two words have competing lexical readings, so this movement is a working interpretation of the sequence, not a claim that every commentator gives the same account.

words.workingGloss: Beyond complete contemplation; selected sense, with support-related alternatives
Unfathomable in this reading; other senses remain open

study.interpretationCare: Distinguish the disputed first pair from the clearer conquest/fear pair. Divine fearlessness is not a demand to hide ordinary human fear or a guarantee of bodily invulnerability.
study.reflection: Can I be steady in devotion without pretending that I have understood everything?
study.teachBack: How do the first two titles and the final two titles address different kinds of limitation?

simple.en: The One is honoured across ages and realms and praised as a treasury of gifts. The final pair holds presence through creation’s three qualities together with freedom from a created origin.
simple.pa: ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਹਰ ਕਾਲ ਅਤੇ ਲੋਕ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਤਿਕਾਰਯੋਗ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਸਾਰੀਆਂ ਦਾਤਾਂ ਦਾ ਖ਼ਜ਼ਾਨਾ ਹੈ। ਆਖ਼ਰੀ ਜੋੜੀ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਸ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਟੀ ਦੇ ਤਿੰਨਾਂ ਗੁਣਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਵਿਆਪਕ ਦੱਸਦਿਆਂ ਵੀ ਕਿਸੇ ਹੋਰ ਤੋਂ ਪੈਦਾ ਹੋਇਆ ਨਹੀਂ ਮੰਨਦੀ।

study.focus: Present in creation without being its dependent product.
study.closeReading: The first two titles are affirmative: reverence is offered, and treasure is found in the One. The next pair asks us to hold two ideas together. In the selected reading, the three qualities of creation express Divine presence; yet the One is not created by a prior maker. The poem can therefore praise relationship with the world without confining the Divine to one changing condition within it. Notice also that ਤ੍ਰਿਮਾਨ and ਤ੍ਰਿਬਰਗ each contain a threefold element but do not name the same three. Ages or realms belong to the first interpretive question; creation’s qualities belong to the second.

words.workingGloss: Revered in the three worlds or times; working frames
Creation’s three qualities; selected working reading
Uncreated; not brought into being by another

study.interpretationCare: Three worlds, three times and three qualities are distinct traditional interpretive frames. Do not merge them into one definition or treat the open ਹੈਂ/ਹੈ source difference as already adjudicated.
study.reflection: How does gratitude change when I attend to the source of a gift as well as the gift itself?
study.teachBack: What distinction must be kept between the threefold references in ਤ੍ਰਿਮਾਨ and ਤ੍ਰਿਬਰਗ?

simple.en: The chhand removes four different limits: a defining colour, a beginning in time, conquest by another and dependence on another’s power. Its praise of freedom concerns the One’s being rather than a claim of human self-sufficiency.
simple.pa: ਇਹ ਛੰਦ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਕਿਸੇ ਨਿਸ਼ਚਿਤ ਰੰਗ, ਸਮੇਂ ਦੀ ਸ਼ੁਰੂਆਤ, ਕਿਸੇ ਦੀ ਜਿੱਤ ਅਤੇ ਪਰਾਈ ਅਧੀਨਤਾ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਯਾਦ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ। ਇਹ ਸੁਤੰਤਰਤਾ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੇ ਸਰੂਪ ਬਾਰੇ ਹੈ; ਇਸ ਨੂੰ ਮਨੁੱਖ ਲਈ ਹਰ ਸਹਾਰੇ ਤੋਂ ਬਿਨਾ ਰਹਿਣ ਦਾ ਦਾਅਵਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਬਣਾਇਆ ਗਿਆ।

study.focus: Four limits removed without erasing their differences.
study.closeReading: Listen to the succession of appearance, time, power and independence. These are different ways in which ordinary beings can be defined or constrained. Colour gives an outward description; a beginning places something within a sequence; conquest makes it subject to another; dependence requires another’s support. In the selected reading, none contains the One. The brevity of the lines should not flatten all four into the same vague idea of greatness. Their distinctions make the praise more precise. The final word also admits a source-of-Brahma reading, which changes the last emphasis from freedom to primordial source while retaining the unchanged original text.

words.workingGloss: Unstained or beyond limiting colour; working range
Independent or unbound; an alternative source-of-Brahma reading exists

study.interpretationCare: Language of colour and purity does not rank human complexions, caste or bodies. Keep the chosen final reading distinct from the documented alternative rather than presenting a single agreed derivation.
study.reflection: Which outward description most often tempts me to think I have understood someone completely?
study.teachBack: Name the different kinds of limitation addressed by the four titles.

simple.en: In the selected reading, the One is beyond birth, a fixed appearance, material composition and the need for nourishment. The closing word also has a classic adornment reading, which remains visible beside this interpretation.
simple.pa: ਇੱਥੇ ਚੁਣੇ ਅਰਥ ਅਨੁਸਾਰ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਜਨਮ, ਨਿਸ਼ਚਿਤ ਦਿੱਖ, ਭੌਤਿਕ ਤੱਤਾਂ ਦੀ ਬਣਤਰ ਅਤੇ ਪਾਲਣਾ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈ। ਆਖ਼ਰੀ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਦਾ ਪੁਰਾਣੇ ਕੋਸ਼ ਵਿੱਚ ਗਹਿਣੇ ਜਾਂ ਸ਼ਿੰਗਾਰ ਵਾਲਾ ਅਰਥ ਵੀ ਮਿਲਦਾ ਹੈ; ਉਹ ਵੱਖਰਾ ਅਰਥ ਨੋਟ ਵਿੱਚ ਸੰਭਾਲਿਆ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Divine being and the ordinary conditions of embodied life.
study.closeReading: The first three lines name conditions familiar from embodied life: birth, appearance and material composition. The selected final reading adds the need for sustenance. Read together, they refuse to make the One simply another organism among organisms. This is a statement about the Divine, not an invitation to despise the body. The final word deserves special care because the historical dictionary’s adornment sense would change the movement: instead of another negation of dependence, it would introduce a positive image of beauty or ornament. A careful learner can understand the chosen sequence while remembering that its closing interpretation is provisional.

words.workingGloss: Not composed of material elements; selected reading
Needing no sustenance in this reading; adornment is a documented alternative

study.interpretationCare: The element-free reading uses a traditional vocabulary of material composition. Divine independence from nourishment does not remove the need to nourish and care for human bodies. The adornment alternative remains unresolved.
study.reflection: Which ordinary gift of nourishment could I receive with more gratitude today?
study.teachBack: How would the adornment reading change the emphasis of the final line?

simple.en: The One cannot be destroyed, broken or overpowered. The final title turns the praise of strength toward freedom from quarrel, inviting us to distinguish steadiness from the urge to keep proving ourselves.
simple.pa: ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦਾ ਨਾਸ ਨਹੀਂ ਕੀਤਾ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ, ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਭੰਨਿਆ ਨਹੀਂ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ ਅਤੇ ਕੋਈ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਜਿੱਤ ਨਹੀਂ ਸਕਦਾ। ਆਖ਼ਰੀ ਨਾਮ ਝਗੜੇ ਤੋਂ ਮੁਕਤੀ ਵੱਲ ਧਿਆਨ ਲੈ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ; ਇਸ ਤੋਂ ਅਡੋਲਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਆਪਣੇ ਆਪ ਨੂੰ ਲਗਾਤਾਰ ਸਾਬਤ ਕਰਨ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਵਿਚਲਾ ਫ਼ਰਕ ਵਿਚਾਰਿਆ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Strength that does not depend on quarrelling.
study.closeReading: The first pair concerns destruction and breaking apart. The next line introduces an opponent or contest, but the final line, in the selected reading, removes wrangling itself. This sequence makes a useful distinction: being unconquerable is not the same as needing to argue continuously. The One is not made secure by another being’s defeat. The practical reflection about steadiness is an educational response to the sequence, not a literal command embedded in each word. Notice how four compact negatives can move from survival, to wholeness, to confrontation, and finally to freedom from agitation without changing their direct devotional address.

words.workingGloss: Not overcome through contest; working sense
Free from wrangling or agitation; selected sense

study.interpretationCare: These attributes praise the Divine; they do not promise that a person is immune to harm. Freedom from quarrel should not be used to silence a necessary, respectful objection to wrongdoing.
study.reflection: When I am challenged, what could strength look like without needing to win an argument?
study.teachBack: How does the final title change the emphasis of the preceding contest-image?

simple.en: The unfathomably deep One is also a companion to all. The chhand holds this closeness together with freedom from worldly entanglement and bondage, so mystery does not have to become distance.
simple.pa: ਅਥਾਹ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਸਭ ਦਾ ਸਾਥੀ ਅਤੇ ਮਿੱਤਰ ਵੀ ਹੈ। ਇਹ ਛੰਦ ਉਸ ਦੀ ਨੇੜਤਾ ਨੂੰ ਸੰਸਾਰੀ ਉਲਝਣਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਬੰਧਨਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਮੁਕਤੀ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਰੱਖਦਾ ਹੈ; ਪੂਰਾ ਭੇਦ ਨਾ ਪਾ ਸਕਣਾ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਦੂਰ ਮੰਨਣਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਬਣਦਾ।

study.focus: A profound presence that can still be called friend.
study.closeReading: ਅਮੀਕ and ਰਫ਼ੀਕ form an affirmative opening pair: depth is immediately followed by companionship. The first word’s Arabic origin also warns against treating every initial ਅ as a negative prefix. The second pair then names freedom from entangling occupations and bonds. Read the pairs together. Divine friendship is not presented as a limited bargain in which the One becomes indebted to a particular person. Nor does unfathomable depth prevent a direct, trusting address. This combination offers a different emphasis from the preceding chhand’s images of strength: intimacy and freedom can belong together, and a relationship need not be reduced to ownership.

words.workingGloss: Profound or fathomlessly deep; Arabic-derived word
Companion or friend; stored spelling retained
Free from entangling worldly occupations; selected sense

study.interpretationCare: The source comparison’s ਫ਼/ਫ difference remains open. The lesson’s language of freedom does not make care, honest work or mutual responsibility into spiritual failures.
study.reflection: What helps me offer friendship without trying to possess or control the other person?
study.teachBack: Why is it misleading to interpret the initial ਅ in ਅਮੀਕ as a negative prefix?

simple.en: Human understanding and insight do not contain the One, and neither time nor a net of bondage holds the One captive. The chhand brings the limits of knowing beside freedom from being caught.
simple.pa: ਮਨੁੱਖ ਦੀ ਬੁੱਧੀ ਅਤੇ ਸੂਝ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਪੂਰੀ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ ਨਹੀਂ ਸਮਝ ਸਕਦੀਆਂ; ਸਮਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਬੰਧਨਾਂ ਦਾ ਜਾਲ ਵੀ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਵੱਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਹੀਂ ਕਰ ਸਕਦੇ। ਇਹ ਛੰਦ ਸਮਝ ਦੀ ਹੱਦ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਫਸਣ ਤੋਂ ਮੁਕਤੀ ਦਾ ਭਾਵ ਰੱਖਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: The One exceeds both mental grasp and binding forces.
study.closeReading: The opening pair works through the closely related words for understanding and insight. Both place a limit on the knower’s reach, rather than attributing ignorance to the One. The third line then moves from knowledge to time and mortality. In the selected final reading, the net supplies another image of containment: what cannot be fully captured in an explanation is also not caught by a binding force. Read this after the friendship of Chhand 36. Acknowledging the limits of comprehension can coexist with trust and relationship; the prayer continues to say You are instead of falling silent because an explanation is incomplete.

words.workingGloss: Beyond the full reach of discernment
Uncaught by a binding net; selected reading

study.interpretationCare: Incomprehensibility is about human limits of understanding, not Divine ignorance. The net-related final reading is provisional, and claims about the One’s freedom are not guarantees that people cannot be harmed.
study.reflection: How can admitting a limit in my understanding make my listening more patient?
study.teachBack: Which two lines concern knowing, and how does the selected final image change the kind of limitation being considered?

simple.en: A Divine name is followed by freedom from a fixed location, endlessness and supreme greatness. In the selected reading, Allah addresses the same One throughout the stanza; the remaining words widen the reader’s sense of that address.
simple.pa: ਇਸ ਕਾਰਜਕਾਰੀ ਅਰਥ ਵਿੱਚ ਅਲਾਹ ਨਾਮ ਨਾਲ ਉਸੇ ਇੱਕ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਯਾਦ ਕੀਤਾ ਗਿਆ ਹੈ। ਅੱਗੇ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਕਿਸੇ ਇੱਕ ਥਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ, ਬੇਅੰਤ ਅਤੇ ਮਹਾਨ ਕਿਹਾ ਹੈ। ਚਾਰਾਂ ਤੁਕਾਂ ਦਾ ਸੰਬੋਧਨ ਇੱਕੋ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਵੱਲ ਹੈ; ਨਾਮ ਉਸ ਦੀ ਹਸਤੀ ਨੂੰ ਛੋਟੀ ਹੱਦ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਹੀਂ ਬੰਨ੍ਹਦਾ।

study.focus: Hear a named address together with the refusal to confine the One to a place or limit.
study.closeReading: All four lines retain the direct ਹੈਂ pattern of this Chachari section. The first line can therefore be heard as an address through a familiar Divine name, while the next three resist making that name a small container. Place, endpoint and ordinary scale fall short. The main reading of ਅਲਾਹ is supported, but it is not the only explanation in the consulted tradition. Keeping that lexical question visible allows the lesson to make its point without treating one dictionary sense as an unquestionable verdict.

words.workingGloss: Allah, the Divine name in this working reading
not confined to a fixed place

study.interpretationCare: Do not turn a Divine name into a claim that the One belongs only to one human group. The first two epithets have recorded interpretive alternatives; this educational reading does not settle their philology or make claims about agreement between all religions.
study.reflection: How can a name help you address the Divine while leaving room for what you do not understand?
study.teachBack: Explain how the final three lines expand the first line’s address, and identify which reading of ਅਲਾਹ this draft uses.

simple.en: The stanza removes four kinds of limitation: an enclosing outline, a rival, dependence on another support, and a created beginning. Each line addresses the same One while naming a different limit that does not apply.
simple.pa: ਛੰਦ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਲਕੀਰ ਦੀ ਹੱਦ, ਬਰਾਬਰ ਦੇ ਸ਼ਰੀਕ, ਬਾਹਰਲੇ ਆਸਰੇ ਅਤੇ ਜਨਮ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਕਹਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ। ਹਰ ਤੁਕ ਉਸੇ ਇੱਕ ਨੂੰ ਸੰਬੋਧਨ ਕਰਦੀ ਹੈ, ਪਰ ਹਰ ਵਿਸ਼ੇਸ਼ਣ ਵੱਖਰੀ ਹੱਦ ਹਟਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਸਾਰੇ ਸ਼ਬਦਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਇੱਕੋ ਅਰਥ ਦੇਣ ਨਾਲ ਇਹ ਫ਼ਰਕ ਗੁੰਮ ਹੋ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Distinguish the four limits being denied instead of flattening the stanza into one vague “beyond”.
study.closeReading: The repeated ending makes the stanza sound compact, but its four openings do different work. ਅਲੀਕ concerns a defining line or mark in the selected reading. ਨ੍ਰਿਸ੍ਰੀਕ concerns an equal or rival. ਨ੍ਰਿਲੰਭ turns to dependence on support, and ਅਸੰਭ to coming into existence. Asking what each word removes is a useful way to slow down the apparent repetition. The lesson’s chosen senses form a coherent reading, while the notes preserve alternatives where the consulted commentaries differ.

words.workingGloss: not enclosed by a defining line or mark

study.interpretationCare: Divine independence is not a demand that people avoid help or relationships. The unrelated falsehood sense of ਅਲੀਕ and everyday impossible sense of ਅਸੰਭ would mislead here. The draft records lexical alternatives without changing any original word.
study.reflection: Can you recognise your own need for support without treating that need as a failure?
study.teachBack: Name the four different limitations considered here, and explain why ਨ੍ਰਿਲੰਭ is not a description of helplessness.

simple.en: The four lines distinguish limits of reach, birth, material composition and touch. Their praise points beyond treating the Divine as one more object that can be produced, inspected or held in the hand.
simple.pa: ਚਾਰ ਤੁਕਾਂ ਪਹੁੰਚ, ਜਨਮ, ਤੱਤਾਂ ਦੀ ਬਣਤਰ ਅਤੇ ਸਰੀਰਕ ਛੋਹ ਦੀਆਂ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਵੱਖ-ਵੱਖ ਕਰਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ। ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਆਮ ਵਸਤ ਵਾਂਗ ਬਣਾਇਆ, ਪਰਖਿਆ ਜਾਂ ਹੱਥ ਵਿੱਚ ਫੜਿਆ ਨਹੀਂ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ। ਇਹ ਉਸ ਦੀ ਉਸਤਤਿ ਹੈ, ਮਨੁੱਖੀ ਸਰੀਰਾਂ ਜਾਂ ਇੰਦ੍ਰੀਆਂ ਦੀ ਨਿੰਦਾ ਨਹੀਂ।

study.focus: Understand the language of reach and touch without turning it into exclusion or bodily contempt.
study.closeReading: ਅਗੰਮ begins with the limit of reaching; ਅਛੂਤ ends with the limit of touching. Between them, ਅਜੰਮ and ਅਭੂਤ remove birth and material composition from the One addressed. That arrangement helps distinguish an object in the world from the Divine being praised. It also makes context essential for vocabulary. The final word has another, painful social use, but this verse applies it to the Divine and the classic dictionary links this occurrence specifically to freedom from physical touch.

words.workingGloss: beyond physical touch in this address

study.interpretationCare: ਅਛੂਤ here gives no support to caste exclusion. Nor do limits on sight, touch or understanding rank people by sensory ability. The five elements belong to a traditional explanatory framework, not a scientific claim about the body.
study.reflection: What is the difference between being unable to hold something in your hand and being unable to relate to it meaningfully?
study.teachBack: Explain the role of the first and last words, and state clearly why the last one is not a label for a human caste.

simple.en: Unseen being is joined with freedom from sorrow, karmic bondage and delusion. The stanza keeps these four qualities distinct, so being beyond ordinary sight does not become mere absence or indifference.
simple.pa: ਅਦ੍ਰਿਸ਼ ਹੋਂਦ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਸੋਗ, ਕਰਮ-ਬੰਧਨ ਅਤੇ ਭਰਮ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ ਹੋਣ ਦੀ ਉਸਤਤਿ ਆਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ। ਚਾਰੇ ਗੁਣ ਵੱਖਰੇ ਪੱਖ ਦੱਸਦੇ ਹਨ। ਆਮ ਨਜ਼ਰ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੋਣ ਦਾ ਭਾਵ ਇਹ ਨਹੀਂ ਕਿ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਹੋਂਦ ਨਹੀਂ ਜਾਂ ਉਸ ਨਾਲ ਕੋਈ ਨਾਤਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਬਣ ਸਕਦਾ।

study.focus: Hear four different freedoms while keeping the distinction between Divine praise and human experience.
study.closeReading: ਅਲੋਕ and ਅਸੋਕ are close in sound, but one concerns visibility and the other sorrow. The second pair likewise separates action and its binding consequences from confusion of understanding. This difference is easy to miss when the lines move quickly. Reading each word with its own question—can it be seen, grieved, bound by action, or confused—helps preserve the stanza’s range. These are questions about the Divine attributes named here, not tests that a learner must pass to count as devout.
study.interpretationCare: The passage is neither a judgment on bereavement nor a promise of permanent emotional calm. Freedom from karma in this address does not abolish human accountability. Curiosity and careful questioning are not equated with the delusion named by ਅਭਰਮ.
study.reflection: Which of these words are you most likely to blur together when reading quickly, and what would help you notice the difference?
study.teachBack: Distinguish ਅਲੋਕ from ਅਸੋਕ and ਅਕਰਮ from ਅਭਰਮ using one clear phrase for each.

simple.en: The stanza joins unconquerable strength, fearlessness, steadiness and unfathomable depth. Familiar qualities return in the short Chachari form, inviting recognition with renewed attention rather than automatic repetition.
simple.pa: ਇਸ ਛੰਦ ਵਿੱਚ ਅਜਿੱਤਤਾ, ਨਿਰਭਉਤਾ, ਅਡੋਲਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਅਥਾਹ ਡੂੰਘਾਈ ਇਕੱਠੀਆਂ ਆਉਂਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ। ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਸੁਣੇ ਗੁਣ ਚਾਚਰੀ ਦੀ ਛੋਟੀ ਚਾਲ ਵਿੱਚ ਮੁੜ ਆਉਂਦੇ ਹਨ। ਦੁਹਰਾਵਾ ਹਰ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਦਾ ਆਪਣਾ ਭਾਵ ਨਵੇਂ ਧਿਆਨ ਨਾਲ ਪਛਾਣਨ ਦਾ ਮੌਕਾ ਬਣਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Recognise returning epithets while distinguishing strength, fearlessness, steadiness and depth.
study.closeReading: The opening pair echoes earlier praise of the One who cannot be conquered and does not fear. The closing pair shifts from what cannot shake the Divine to what the reader cannot fully fathom. Although ਅਬਾਹ and ਅਗਾਹ rhyme closely, steadiness and depth are different ideas. The order here is also worth noticing alongside earlier salutations in the bani. Repetition allows recognition; attending to placement prevents recognition from becoming a substitute for understanding.
study.interpretationCare: The strength described belongs to the Divine address, not to a promise of physical invulnerability. A person’s fear does not prove spiritual failure. ਅਬਾਹ is read through steadiness, without importing a misleading anatomical explanation.
study.reflection: What kind of steadiness can coexist with admitting that you do not fully understand a situation?
study.teachBack: Explain the difference between ਅਬਾਹ and ਅਗਾਹ, then connect each to one of the opening qualities.

simple.en: The immeasurable treasury is praised as many and still One. The final pair asks the reader to hold multiplicity and unity together, bringing this Chachari section to a close without reducing either side to a mere counting exercise.
simple.pa: ਮਿਣਤੀ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਅਤੇ ਸਭ ਦਾਤਾਂ ਦੇ ਭੰਡਾਰ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਅਨੇਕ ਰੂਪਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਵਿਆਪਕ, ਫਿਰ ਵੀ ਇੱਕ ਕਿਹਾ ਹੈ। ਅਖੀਰਲੀ ਜੋੜੀ ਅਨੇਕਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਏਕਤਾ ਨੂੰ ਇਕੱਠੇ ਰੱਖਦੀ ਹੈ। ਇਸ ਨਾਲ ਚਾਚਰੀ ਦਾ ਇਹ ਭਾਗ ਮੁੱਕਦਾ ਹੈ; ਗੱਲ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਗਿਣਤੀ ਕਰਨ ਦੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਰਹਿੰਦੀ।

study.focus: Let the final “still One” complete the statement about the many.
study.closeReading: ਅਮਾਨ first resists measurement, and ਨਿਧਾਨ adds the image of a treasury. The final two lines then make the strongest movement: ਅਨੇਕ is followed by ਫਿਰਿ ਏਕ. The same ਹੈਂ addresses the same One in both lines. Reading only the third would miss the turn; reading only the fourth would miss the variety through which the praise has just moved. The small word ਫਿਰਿ matters because it holds the apparent contrast together rather than erasing the preceding line.
study.interpretationCare: One and many are theological terms in this address, not a mathematical proof or permission to erase differences among people. The treasury image should not become a guarantee of material reward for recitation.
study.reflection: Can you notice real variety in life while also recognising connections that make it more than isolated pieces?
study.teachBack: Explain what ਫਿਰਿ adds to the last line and why both of the final two lines are needed.

simple.en: The return to Bhujang Prayat brings back explicit salutations. Universal honour, abundance and divine supremacy are followed by freedom from outward guise and, in the selected reading, division within the One.
simple.pa: ਭੁਜੰਗ ਪ੍ਰਯਾਤ ਛੰਦ ਦੀ ਵਾਪਸੀ ਨਾਲ ਸਿੱਧੀਆਂ ਨਮਸਕਾਰਾਂ ਮੁੜ ਆਉਂਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ। ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਸਭ ਦਾ ਸਤਿਕਾਰਯੋਗ, ਦਾਤਾਂ ਦਾ ਭੰਡਾਰ ਅਤੇ ਦੇਵਤਿਆਂ ਤੋਂ ਉੱਚਾ ਕਿਹਾ ਹੈ। ਅਖੀਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਭੇਖ ਅਤੇ, ਇਸ ਕਾਰਜਕਾਰੀ ਅਰਥ ਅਨੁਸਾਰ, ਸਰੂਪ ਦੀ ਵੰਡ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ ਹੋਣ ਦੀ ਗੱਲ ਆਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Notice the return of a metrical form and how praise is paired with limits on outward definition.
study.closeReading: The heading before this stanza names ਭੁਜੰਗ ਪ੍ਰਯਾਤ ਛੰਦ, returning to a form used earlier. The direct ਹੈਂ endings give way here to explicit ਨਮੋ salutations and clauses that continue them. The first pair widens honour and abundance; the second intensifies divine supremacy before qualifying how the One is understood. ਅਭੇਖੀ prevents a particular guise from becoming the definition. Our reading of ਅਭੇਵੇ adds undivided being, while the note preserves the genuine interpretive disagreement around that word.

words.workingGloss: not defined by an outward guise
without division in this working reading; other senses remain open

study.interpretationCare: The heading is separate from the four scripture lines and gives no automatic recitation speed. ਅਭੇਵੇ remains a lexical review point; an undivided reading must not be silently presented as identical to unconcealed or free from secrets. Freedom from guise does not dismiss meaningful religious discipline.
study.reflection: What happens when an outward sign becomes the whole of what you think you know about someone?
study.teachBack: Identify the metrical change and explain how the final line qualifies the honour and supremacy expressed earlier.

simple.en: Sovereignty over death is joined with care for all, and the final pair extends Divine presence to every place. Four repeated salutations connect power, nurture and pervasiveness without restricting the address to a single location.
simple.pa: ਕਾਲ ਉੱਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਸਰਦਾਰੀ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਸਭ ਜੀਵਾਂ ਦੀ ਪਾਲਣਾ ਆਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ। ਅਖੀਰਲੀਆਂ ਦੋ ਤੁਕਾਂ ਉਸ ਦੀ ਵਿਆਪਕਤਾ ਸਭ ਥਾਵਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਭਵਨਾਂ ਤਕ ਲਿਆਉਂਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ। ਚਾਰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਮਰੱਥਾ, ਸੰਭਾਲ ਅਤੇ ਸਰਬ-ਵਿਆਪਕਤਾ ਇੱਕੋ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨਾਲ ਜੁੜਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ।

study.focus: Read sovereignty, nurture and presence as connected parts of the same address.
study.closeReading: Each line begins with ਨਮੋ, but the opening intensification ਕਾਲ ਕਾਲੇ differs from the repeated ਸਰਬ that follows. The first pair places death and nurture together. The second uses two closely related expressions of all-pervading presence, so the movement is from power and care to their unrestricted scope. These phrases have appeared earlier in the bani; their return asks the reader to bring remembered meaning into the present arrangement. The lesson can acknowledge the overlap without inventing a sharp distinction unsupported by the words.

words.workingGloss: sovereign even over death and time
pervading or moving throughout all places
present in all realms and dwellings

study.interpretationCare: This praise does not promise bodily invulnerability or supply a reason to blame anyone for suffering. All-pervading presence is a devotional claim, not a measurable travel route. Overlapping epithets need not be forced into separate technical categories.
study.reflection: Where in ordinary life might remembering care and presence change the quality of your attention?
study.teachBack: Describe the two pairs in this stanza and explain what the repeated ਸਰਬ adds after the opening line.

simple.en: The opening pairs describe the One as free from bodily limits, an external master and dependence on a companion, while also naming the power of dissolution. The closing salutations turn toward the source of radiance and honour. Independence does not make the Divine distant from what shines or deserves reverence.
simple.pa: ਪਹਿਲੀਆਂ ਜੋੜੀਆਂ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਸਰੀਰ ਦੀ ਹੱਦ, ਕਿਸੇ ਉੱਪਰਲੇ ਮਾਲਕ ਅਤੇ ਸਾਥੀ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ ਦੱਸਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ; ਨਾਲ ਹੀ ਸ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਟੀ ਦੇ ਅੰਤ ਦੀ ਸਮਰੱਥਾ ਵੀ ਉਸੇ ਦੀ ਹੈ। ਅੰਤ ਦੀਆਂ ਨਮਸਕਾਰਾਂ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਸ਼ ਅਤੇ ਮਾਣ ਦੇ ਮੂਲ ਵੱਲ ਮੁੜਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ। ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਸੁਤੰਤਰਤਾ ਦਾ ਭਾਵ ਇਹ ਨਹੀਂ ਕਿ ਚਾਨਣ ਅਤੇ ਸਤਿਕਾਰ ਨਾਲ ਉਸ ਦਾ ਕੋਈ ਸੰਬੰਧ ਨਹੀਂ।

study.focus: The independent One as the source of radiance and honour.
study.closeReading: The first two lines each carry two epithets, so pause over both halves: body and master, companion and dissolving power. They address different kinds of dependence and action. The next two lines explicitly renew ਨਮੋ and use a repeated noun to deepen praise. A sun illuminates other things, yet here the sun itself points beyond its own brightness. A person may receive honour, yet honour also points beyond the person receiving it. The movement invites gratitude without pretending that familiar greatness contains the One. Read the destruction word beside these affirming images; it is one aspect of the praise, not the entire portrait.

words.workingGloss: Without bodily limbs; not an embodied organism
Having no master above the One
Dissolving or destructive power; churning is an alternative reading
Honour or reverence in this phrase

study.interpretationCare: Body-free language does not demean human bodies, and needing no companion does not make human loneliness a spiritual ideal. The destruction title describes Divine power; it gives the reader no instruction to harm.
study.reflection: When I admire someone’s brilliance or stature, can gratitude reach beyond the admired person?
study.teachBack: Identify both epithets in each opening line, then explain how the sun and honour images change the emphasis.

simple.en: Moonlight, sunlight, song and melody become four ways of bowing to the same One. Each familiar beauty points toward a depth beyond itself. The selected reading moves from what is seen in the sky to what is heard in music, keeping the rhythm of reverence throughout.
simple.pa: ਚੰਦ ਦਾ ਚਾਨਣ, ਸੂਰਜ ਦਾ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਸ਼, ਗੀਤ ਅਤੇ ਤਾਨ—ਇਹ ਚਾਰੋ ਉਸੇ ਇੱਕ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਅੱਗੇ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਦੇ ਰੂਪ ਬਣਦੇ ਹਨ। ਜਾਣੀ ਹੋਈ ਸੁੰਦਰਤਾ ਆਪਣੇ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਕਿਸੇ ਡੂੰਘੇ ਆਧਾਰ ਵੱਲ ਧਿਆਨ ਲੈ ਜਾਂਦੀ ਹੈ। ਚੁਣੇ ਅਰਥ ਵਿੱਚ ਛੰਦ ਅਸਮਾਨ ਦੀ ਦਿੱਖ ਤੋਂ ਸੰਗੀਤ ਦੀ ਸੁਣਨ ਵਾਲੀ ਸੁੰਦਰਤਾ ਵੱਲ ਵਧਦਾ ਹੈ, ਪਰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਦੀ ਲੈ ਇੱਕੋ ਰਹਿੰਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Visible and musical beauty as languages of praise.
study.closeReading: Every line begins with ਨਮੋ, and every image is doubled: moon, sun, song, melody. This repetition does more than supply a list of attractive things. It asks where their beauty leads the attention. The sun line is unchanged from the preceding chhand, but its neighbours now make a new sequence: two celestial images followed by two musical ones. Within the selected musical reading, a song and a taan are related without being interchangeable; a taan concerns the movement or unfolding of notes. Notice how the poem can carry the same act of bowing through different experiences without requiring one experience to replace all the others.

words.workingGloss: Melodic movement or phrase; selected sense
An expression of bowing or salutation

study.interpretationCare: These images do not prescribe a ritual of sun or moon worship, a compulsory musical performance or a particular sensory experience. The power/instrument alternatives for ਤਾਨ remain provisional lexical choices, not new words inserted into the verse.
study.reflection: What familiar beauty helps me turn appreciation into gratitude?
study.teachBack: Describe the two pairs of images, and explain why the repeated sun line keeps its meaning while gaining a new setting.

simple.en: Dance, resonance, the strength of hands and instrumental sound place movement and creative capacity within the language of devotion. The hand reading is a deliberate choice: another rendering hears drum-beating in that line. The lesson keeps the distinction while attending to the repeated act of bowing.
simple.pa: ਨਾਚ, ਨਾਦ, ਹੱਥਾਂ ਦੀ ਸਮਰੱਥਾ ਅਤੇ ਸਾਜ਼ਾਂ ਦੀ ਧੁਨ—ਇਹਨਾਂ ਰਾਹੀਂ ਗਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਰਚਨਾਤਮਕ ਤਾਕਤ ਭਗਤੀ ਦੀ ਬੋਲੀ ਬਣਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ। ਪਾਨ ਦਾ ਹੱਥ ਵਾਲਾ ਅਰਥ ਇੱਥੇ ਸੋਚ ਕੇ ਚੁਣਿਆ ਹੈ; ਇੱਕ ਹੋਰ ਵਿਆਖਿਆ ਇਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਢੋਲ ਵਜਾਉਣ ਦਾ ਭਾਵ ਲੈਂਦੀ ਹੈ। ਪਾਠ ਇਹ ਫ਼ਰਕ ਸੰਭਾਲਦਿਆਂ ਵਾਰ-ਵਾਰ ਆਉਂਦੀ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਵੱਲ ਧਿਆਨ ਲਿਆਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Creative movement, sound and capacity received with gratitude.
study.closeReading: The doubled words continue the pattern of the preceding chhand, but the images draw closer to movement and making. Dance and resonance lead into the capacity of hands and the sounding of instruments. Under the selected hand reading, the third line does not have to become another musical noun merely because its neighbours concern performance. It can draw attention to the ability through which something is made or played. Under Neki’s drum reading, the sequence would remain more uniformly musical. Holding that difference openly is part of careful reading. In either account, the repeated salutation prevents the artist’s skill from becoming the sole object of admiration.

words.workingGloss: Hand in the selected reading; a drum-related alternative is recorded

study.interpretationCare: The passage is praise, not a requirement to dance, play an instrument or hear an inner sound. Hand imagery expresses capacity; it does not measure human worth by physical strength, dexterity or ability.
study.reflection: How might I practise a skill with gratitude for what makes the practice possible?
study.teachBack: What changes in the sequence when ਪਾਨ is read as the strength of hands rather than drum-beating?

simple.en: The One cannot be confined to a body or name, yet is present in every form. The same verse sequence names the dissolution of forms and the fullness of abundance. It invites a relationship with the world that notices both its gifts and its passing forms without claiming to possess the Divine.
simple.pa: ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਕਿਸੇ ਇੱਕ ਸਰੀਰ ਜਾਂ ਨਾਮ ਵਿੱਚ ਬੰਨ੍ਹਿਆ ਨਹੀਂ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ, ਫਿਰ ਵੀ ਉਹ ਹਰ ਰੂਪ ਵਿੱਚ ਵਿਆਪਕ ਹੈ। ਇਹੀ ਛੰਦ ਰੂਪਾਂ ਦੇ ਭੰਗ ਹੋਣ ਅਤੇ ਸਾਰੀ ਸੰਪਦਾ ਦੇ ਮੂਲ ਨੂੰ ਇਕੱਠੇ ਯਾਦ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ। ਇਸ ਤੋਂ ਜਗਤ ਦੀਆਂ ਦਾਤਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਉਸ ਦੇ ਬਦਲਦੇ ਰੂਪਾਂ ਦੋਹਾਂ ਵੱਲ ਧਿਆਨ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ, ਪਰ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਆਪਣੀ ਮਲਕੀਅਤ ਬਣਾਉਣ ਦਾ ਦਾਅਵਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਬਣਦਾ।

study.focus: Formlessness, pervasion, dissolution and abundance held together.
study.closeReading: Read the first and second lines beside one another before trying to resolve their tension. The One is not an organism identified by limbs or an object exhausted by a name, yet every form is included in the scope of ਸਮਸਤੀ ਸਰੂਪੇ. The third line then brings the breaking of forms into the same address. Finally, ਸਮਸਤੀ returns with abundance and splendour. The repeated word all widens both presence and treasure. This sequence can loosen possessiveness: a form can matter, and a gift can be appreciated, without either becoming permanent or capturing the whole of the Divine. That reflection arises from the passage’s contrasts, not from an instruction to abandon care for creation.

words.workingGloss: Beyond a name that could exhaustively describe the One
Abundance, wealth or splendour; selected sense

study.interpretationCare: Formlessness is not contempt for bodies, and dissolution is not permission to destroy what others need. Presence in all forms does not mean that every human action deserves approval.
study.reflection: Can I value a gift deeply without treating it as something I can keep forever?
study.teachBack: Explain why the body-free opening and the all-forms phrase need to be read together.

simple.en: This two-line chhand joins unstained being with sovereignty above every ruler. The doubled language of freedom from blemish prepares for praise of supreme authority. Its royal image does not make an earthly office or title equal to the One being addressed.
simple.pa: ਦੋ ਤੁਕਾਂ ਵਾਲਾ ਇਹ ਛੰਦ ਨਿਰਮਲ ਸਰੂਪ ਨੂੰ ਸਾਰੇ ਰਾਜਿਆਂ ਤੋਂ ਉੱਚੀ ਪ੍ਰਭੂਤਾ ਨਾਲ ਜੋੜਦਾ ਹੈ। ਕਲੰਕ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ ਹੋਣ ਦੀ ਦੁਹਰਾਈ ਪਰਮ ਅਧਿਕਾਰ ਦੀ ਸਿਫ਼ਤ ਲਈ ਭੂਮਿਕਾ ਬਣਦੀ ਹੈ। ਰਾਜਸੀ ਉਪਮਾ ਕਿਸੇ ਧਰਤੀ ਦੇ ਅਹੁਦੇ ਜਾਂ ਖ਼ਿਤਾਬ ਨੂੰ ਸੰਬੋਧਿਤ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੇ ਬਰਾਬਰ ਨਹੀਂ ਕਰਦੀ।

study.focus: Unstained being as the setting for supreme authority.
study.closeReading: Although this chhand has only two lines, each is a full phrase with more than one point of attention. The first repeats freedom from blemish, then speaks of ਸਰੂਪ. The second repeats kingship at a higher order and closes with ਪਰਮ ਰੂਪੇ. The movement from unstainedness to supreme sovereignty is therefore also held together by the language of being or form. A reader can hear authority here without stopping at the outward splendour of a throne. The ruler of rulers remains the One praised as beyond blemish. As a reflection on responsibility, this can prompt us to ask whether the authority we exercise serves what is worthy of respect.

words.workingGloss: Unstained; free of blemish in this phrase

study.interpretationCare: Blemish language here concerns the praised Divine being, not skin, disability, caste or bodily worth. The royal image gives no human leader immunity from moral responsibility.
study.reflection: Where I have responsibility, what would make my use of it worthy of trust?
study.teachBack: Identify the two linked ideas in each of the chhand’s two lines.

simple.en: Masters of spiritual discipline and holders of royal power are placed before the same supreme One. Each line adds a further quality: fullness of spiritual accomplishment and unsurpassed greatness. The parallel gives devotion a wider horizon than either spiritual prestige or worldly rank.
simple.pa: ਆਤਮਕ ਸਾਧਨਾ ਦੇ ਮਾਹਰ ਅਤੇ ਰਾਜਸੀ ਅਧਿਕਾਰ ਵਾਲੇ ਉਸੇ ਪਰਮ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਅੱਗੇ ਆਉਂਦੇ ਹਨ। ਹਰ ਤੁਕ ਇੱਕ ਹੋਰ ਗੁਣ ਜੋੜਦੀ ਹੈ: ਆਤਮਕ ਪੂਰਨਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਬੇਮਿਸਾਲ ਮਹਾਨਤਾ। ਇਹ ਸਮਾਂਤਰ ਬਣਤਰ ਭਗਤੀ ਨੂੰ ਆਤਮਕ ਪ੍ਰਸਿੱਧੀ ਜਾਂ ਦੁਨਿਆਵੀ ਦਰਜੇ ਦੀ ਹੱਦ ਤੋਂ ਅੱਗੇ ਲੈ ਜਾਂਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Spiritual and worldly distinction beneath one supreme mastery.
study.closeReading: The two lines are built in parallel. Both begin with salutation, name a sphere of mastery, and end with ਪਰਮ followed by a further quality. The first concerns yoga and accomplishment; the second concerns rule and greatness. The word supreme therefore does not attach only to power in the public world or only to achievement in spiritual practice. Both are drawn into one act of reverence. Compare the second line with Chhand 50: its kingship phrase is familiar, but the final epithet changes. Careful attention notices that change instead of treating every repeated royal phrase as an identical whole line. The passage can support humility about both credentials and position.

words.workingGloss: Yoga or spiritual discipline in this compound
Master of the masters of yoga
Accomplished or perfected; spiritual perfection in this reading
Eminent or greatly exalted in this context

study.interpretationCare: The language of siddhi does not promise supernatural abilities, and ਬ੍ਰਿਧੇ here should not be reduced to physical old age. Neither spiritual attainment nor worldly status makes one person’s dignity greater than another’s.
study.reflection: What changes when I regard an achievement as a responsibility rather than a reason to feel above others?
study.teachBack: Show the parallel between the two lines, then name the changed ending in the repeated kingship phrase.

simple.en: The chhand places the bearer and wielder of weapons beside complete knowing and the Mother of the world. Strength, discernment and care are addressed to one Divine presence. The maternal ending belongs fully to the passage and changes how its opening martial images are heard.
simple.pa: ਇਹ ਛੰਦ ਸ਼ਸਤ੍ਰ ਧਾਰਨ ਕਰਨ ਅਤੇ ਅਸਤ੍ਰ ਚਲਾਉਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਪੂਰੇ ਗਿਆਨ ਅਤੇ ਜਗਤ ਦੀ ਮਾਤਾ ਦੇ ਰੂਪ ਨਾਲ ਜੋੜਦਾ ਹੈ। ਸਮਰੱਥਾ, ਸੂਝ ਅਤੇ ਸੰਭਾਲ ਉਸੇ ਇੱਕ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਸੰਬੋਧਿਤ ਹਨ। ਮਾਂ ਵਾਲਾ ਆਖ਼ਰੀ ਰੂਪ ਛੰਦ ਦਾ ਪੂਰਾ ਹਿੱਸਾ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਪਹਿਲੀਆਂ ਜੰਗੀ ਉਪਮਾਵਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਸਮਝਣ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੀ ਰਾਹ ਦਿਖਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Strength understood alongside knowing and maternal care.
study.closeReading: The repeated ਨਮੋ holds four images within one address. The first two concern weapons: bearing them and, in the selected second reading, projecting them. The verse then turns to knowing and finally to the Mother of the world. Do not stop after the first pair, or soften the pair until its martial character disappears. Instead, listen to the whole sequence. Power is praised together with complete knowing and a relationship of care that reaches the world. The final maternal title also prevents the royal and martial imagery from fixing devotion into exclusively masculine terms. A useful reflection is how courage can remain attentive to those who need protection rather than becoming a display of dominance.

words.workingGloss: Bearing in the hand in this compound
A weapon projected or cast forth

study.interpretationCare: These salutations are not permission for aggression, cruelty or hostility toward a group. Divine motherhood is a devotional relationship, not a biological description or a hierarchy of genders.
study.reflection: Where can courage and careful concern for others guide the same action?
study.teachBack: Explain how the knowing and maternal titles affect your reading of the two martial titles.

simple.en: The first line removes four limits: a defining outfit, delusion, dependence on enjoyment, and being available for someone else to possess or consume. The second honours the Divine above even accomplished yogis. In this working reading, supreme spiritual mastery cannot be reduced to an appearance or an appetite.
simple.pa: ਪਹਿਲੀ ਤੁਕ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਭੇਖ, ਭਰਮ ਅਤੇ ਭੋਗ ਦੀਆਂ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਕਹਿੰਦੀ ਹੈ। ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਆਪਣੇ ਸੁਖ ਲਈ ਵਰਤੀ ਜਾਣ ਵਾਲੀ ਵਸਤ ਨਹੀਂ ਬਣਾਇਆ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ। ਦੂਜੀ ਤੁਕ ਜੋਗੀਆਂ ਦੇ ਵੀ ਸੁਆਮੀ ਅਤੇ ਪੂਰਨ ਜੁਗਤ ਵਾਲੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦੀ ਹੈ। ਇਸ ਕਾਰਜਕਾਰੀ ਅਰਥ ਵਿੱਚ ਆਤਮਕ ਮਹਾਨਤਾ ਕਿਸੇ ਪਹਿਰਾਵੇ ਜਾਂ ਭੋਗ ਦੀ ਲਾਲਸਾ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਹੀਂ ਸਮਾਉਂਦੀ।

study.focus: Keep the four opening epithets distinct, then ask how they shape the praise of spiritual mastery.
study.closeReading: The first source line contains four closely sounding words, each removing a different limitation. The pair about enjoyment asks particular care: freedom from wanting pleasure is not quite the same statement as freedom from being used as someone else’s pleasure. The next line changes to an explicit salutation and places even advanced yogis within a greater horizon. The repetition of ਜੋਗ does not make the One a member of one human order. Read the stanza alongside Chhand 28, where enjoyment is praised in a different formulation; neither passage should erase the other. The lesson selects a method-related sense of ਪਰਮ ਜੁਗਤੇ while leaving the union-related interpretation visible.

words.workingGloss: free from dependence on worldly enjoyment
not an object to be enjoyed or consumed, in this reading
supreme in method; complete union is an alternative reading

study.interpretationCare: These are Divine attributes, not a demand to despise the body, suppress all enjoyment or claim superiority through a religious outfit. The method/union distinction remains a question for qualified Punjabi and Sikh review.
study.reflection: When might an outward sign of discipline become more important to you than the honesty of the practice itself?
study.teachBack: Explain the difference between ਅਭੋਗੀ and ਅਭੁਗਤੇ in this draft, and name the two noted approaches to ਪਰਮ ਜੁਗਤੇ.

simple.en: The stanza addresses an enduring Divine presence through both sustaining care and fearsome action. Its second line reaches across a difficult pair, read here as the departed and the living, and closes with light and noble dharam. The praise does not make the painful side of existence disappear, and it does not make cruelty a human virtue.
simple.pa: ਛੰਦ ਸਦਾ ਕਾਇਮ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਜੀਵਨ ਦਾ ਆਸਰਾ ਅਤੇ ਭਿਆਨਕ ਕਰਮ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਾ ਕਹਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ। ਦੂਜੀ ਤੁਕ ਦੇ ਪ੍ਰੇਤ ਅਤੇ ਅਪ੍ਰੇਤ ਨੂੰ ਇੱਥੇ ਮਰ ਚੁੱਕਿਆਂ ਅਤੇ ਜੀਉਂਦਿਆਂ ਦੇ ਕਾਰਜਕਾਰੀ ਅਰਥ ਵਿੱਚ ਲਿਆ ਹੈ; ਇਸ ਜੋੜੇ ਦੇ ਹੋਰ ਅਰਥ ਵੀ ਮਿਲਦੇ ਹਨ। ਤੁਕ ਦਾ ਅੰਤ ਜੋਤਿ ਅਤੇ ਸ੍ਰੇਸ਼ਟ ਧਰਮ ਵੱਲ ਲੈ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਇਹ ਉਸਤਤਿ ਮਨੁੱਖ ਨੂੰ ਜ਼ੁਲਮ ਕਰਨ ਦਾ ਹੱਕ ਨਹੀਂ ਦਿੰਦੀ।

study.focus: Read sustaining care and fearsome power together while keeping the uncertain spirit vocabulary visible.
study.closeReading: Both lines begin with ਨਮੋ, so the grammatical direction remains an address of reverence. The first does not restrict the Divine to experiences that feel pleasant. Its fierce word should neither be hidden nor casually imitated by a person. In the second, the pair ਪ੍ਰੇਤ and ਅਪ੍ਰੇਤ resists a single confident gloss across all the consulted witnesses. The selected departed/living contrast gives the reader a clear way through the line, while the note preserves the other readings. ਦੇਵੇ and ਸੁਧਰਮੇ complete the address; omitting them would leave the stanza sounding like a catalogue of frightening beings rather than praise of the One.

words.workingGloss: the enduring Divine sustainer in this address
departed and not-departed in the selected reading

study.interpretationCare: The verse supplies no permission to harm, intimidate or identify another person as an evil spirit. Its traditional vocabulary is not evidence about the cause of someone’s distress. The spirits/pure-souls and inanimate/conscious readings remain alternatives, not settled classifications.
study.reflection: Can you acknowledge that an experience is painful without turning that pain into a judgment against the person enduring it?
study.teachBack: Identify the gentle and fearsome aspects named in the first line, then explain the chosen meaning and the uncertainty of the second line’s paired words.

simple.en: The stanza places the language of healing and love beside two expressions of supreme sovereignty. Its movement invites the reader to understand greatness in relation to care for vulnerability. The prayer’s confidence is devotional; a person who remains ill has not failed this lesson.
simple.pa: ਛੰਦ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਰੋਗ ਦੂਰ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲੇ ਅਤੇ ਪਿਆਰ ਸਰੂਪ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਫਿਰ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਸ਼ਾਹਾਂ ਦਾ ਸ਼ਾਹ ਅਤੇ ਰਾਜਿਆਂ ਦਾ ਰਾਜਾ ਕਹਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ। ਇਸ ਲੜੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਮਹਾਨਤਾ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਜੀਵਾਂ ਦੇ ਦੁੱਖ ਦੀ ਚਿੰਤਾ ਵੀ ਆਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ। ਇਹ ਭਗਤੀ ਦਾ ਸੰਬੋਧਨ ਹੈ; ਬਿਮਾਰੀ ਰਹਿ ਜਾਣਾ ਕਿਸੇ ਮਨੁੱਖ ਦੀ ਸ਼ਰਧਾ ਦੀ ਘਾਟ ਦਾ ਸਬੂਤ ਨਹੀਂ।

study.focus: Notice what happens when royal greatness is preceded by care for suffering and the language of love.
study.closeReading: Four salutations create a steady movement through the stanza. The first names affliction, the second love in the selected reading, and the final two use royal titles. Those last titles reinforce each other without becoming names of two different deities. Their placement also gives the reader a question to carry into daily life: what should power be for when suffering is already in view? That question is an application, not an extra clause hidden in the original. The love reading of ਰਾਗ has contextual support; the bliss reading is also noted. Neither requires a particular voice, musical skill or sensory capacity.

words.workingGloss: love in its very being; bliss is another reading

study.interpretationCare: Praise of healing is not a clinical prediction, a treatment instruction or a guarantee of recovery. Illness, disability and continued pain do not establish spiritual failure. The royal language gives no human being unlimited authority.
study.reflection: Where do you have a little influence, and how could you use it to make room for someone who is struggling?
study.teachBack: Describe the stanza’s movement from affliction and love to sovereignty, and explain why its first line should not be presented as a cure guarantee.

simple.en: The repeated expressions turn giving, honour and affliction back towards the Divine. The last line adds cleansing imagery. In the selected reading, the One supplies what generosity and honour depend on, overcomes affliction, and is addressed as a source of purity. The language asks for reverence, not a judgment about anyone’s health or social standing.
simple.pa: ਛੰਦ ਦਾਨ, ਮਾਣ ਅਤੇ ਰੋਗ ਦੇ ਦੁਹਰਾਏ ਹੋਏ ਸ਼ਬਦਾਂ ਰਾਹੀਂ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਵੱਲ ਧਿਆਨ ਲੈ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਦਾਤੇ ਨੂੰ ਦਾਨੀਆਂ ਦਾ ਦਾਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਮਾਣ ਵਾਲਿਆਂ ਦਾ ਮਾਣ ਕਿਹਾ ਹੈ। ਰੋਗਾਂ ਦਾ ਰੋਗ ਉਸ ਦੀ ਰੋਗ-ਨਾਸਕ ਸਮਰੱਥਾ ਦਾ ਕਾਰਜਕਾਰੀ ਅਰਥ ਹੈ; ਅਖ਼ੀਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਪਵਿੱਤਰ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲੇ ਇਸ਼ਨਾਨ ਦਾ ਰੂਪਕ ਆਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਇਸ ਤੋਂ ਕਿਸੇ ਮਨੁੱਖ ਦੀ ਸਿਹਤ ਜਾਂ ਪਵਿੱਤਰਤਾ ਬਾਰੇ ਫ਼ੈਸਲਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਕੱਢਣਾ।

study.focus: Follow the repeated-word pattern without forcing giving, honour, affliction and cleansing into one identical meaning.
study.closeReading: The first three lines each repeat a key noun, but their relationships differ. A giver may receive before giving; honour can point beyond the person being praised; disease directed against disease becomes an image of its defeat. The final line changes the pattern and offers a bath as an image of purification. This variation matters: the stanza is not a list of interchangeable superlatives. The reading of ਰੋਗ ਰੋਗੇ is explicitly selected rather than treated as unanimous. Keeping its alternative separate also prevents a slide from broad Divine sovereignty into a personal explanation for why a particular individual is ill.

words.workingGloss: honour of all who are honoured
affliction overcoming affliction, in this reading

study.interpretationCare: Purification language must not be used to label an ill or disabled person impure. This lesson makes no cure promise and gives no medical or bathing instructions. Its reflection on generosity does not require money, status or public recognition.
study.reflection: Think of something you have received that you can pass on without taking all the credit for it.
study.teachBack: Explain how the repeated nouns work differently in the first three lines, and describe the final bathing image without making a claim about physical health.

simple.en: Four repeated expressions place sacred utterance, ritual device, object of worship and ritual method in relation to the Divine. Their common direction is reverence for the One above any technique. Keeping the terms distinct helps the reader avoid treating the stanza as a set of instructions for obtaining power.
simple.pa: ਚਾਰ ਤੁਕਾਂ ਮੰਤ੍ਰ, ਜੰਤ੍ਰ, ਇਸਟ ਅਤੇ ਤੰਤ੍ਰ ਨੂੰ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੇ ਸੰਬੰਧ ਵਿੱਚ ਰੱਖਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ। ਮੰਤ੍ਰ ਦਾ ਸੰਬੰਧ ਉਚਾਰੇ ਜਾਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਬੋਲਾਂ ਨਾਲ, ਜੰਤ੍ਰ ਦਾ ਰਸਮੀ ਸਾਧਨ ਨਾਲ, ਇਸਟ ਦਾ ਪੂਜਣਯੋਗ ਨਾਲ ਅਤੇ ਤੰਤ੍ਰ ਦਾ ਵਿਧੀ ਨਾਲ ਜੋੜ ਕੇ ਕਾਰਜਕਾਰੀ ਅਰਥ ਕੀਤਾ ਹੈ। ਹਰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਉਸ ਇੱਕ ਵੱਲ ਹੈ ਜੋ ਕਿਸੇ ਵਿਧੀ ਦੇ ਅਧੀਨ ਨਹੀਂ। ਇਹ ਜਾਦੂਈ ਤਾਕਤ ਹਾਸਲ ਕਰਨ ਦੀਆਂ ਹਦਾਇਤਾਂ ਨਹੀਂ ਹਨ।

study.focus: Identify four different kinds of religious means and keep the salutation directed towards the Divine.
study.closeReading: The surface pattern is very regular: ਨਮੋ followed by a repeated noun. Yet a spoken formula, a diagram or device, a revered object and a ritual system are not the same thing. Their juxtaposition supplies context for selecting among dictionary senses. Each phrase carries the same movement beyond the ordinary authority of that noun. There are no directions here for drawing, binding, counting or commanding. The Study reading therefore asks what the practitioner relies on, rather than supplying a new technique. An account of historical vocabulary can help comprehension without certifying the powers that people have attributed to such practices.

words.workingGloss: yantra of yantras; ritual-device language here
the worship-worthy One above all objects of worship
tantra of tantras; method or ritual-system language here

study.interpretationCare: No magical technique, supernatural result or control over another person is promised. The words have broader dictionary ranges than this one stanza requires. The teaching should not disparage a reader for knowing or not knowing ritual terminology.
study.reflection: When you practise something regularly, how can you remain sincere without treating the practice as a bargain that guarantees an outcome?
study.teachBack: Give one plain-language distinction between mantra, yantra, isht and tantra, then explain why this stanza is an address of praise rather than an instruction manual.

simple.en: Enduring true being, awareness and bliss are named beside the power that ends creation. The second line brings together incomparability, formlessness and presence in all. The stanza asks the reader to hold these descriptions together without reducing the Divine to a pleasant feeling or one visible object.
simple.pa: ਸਦਾ ਕਾਇਮ ਸੱਚੀ ਹੋਂਦ, ਚੇਤਨਾ ਅਤੇ ਅਨੰਦ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਹੀ ਸਾਰੀ ਰਚਨਾ ਦੇ ਅੰਤ ਦਾ ਜ਼ਿਕਰ ਆਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਦੂਜੀ ਤੁਕ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਉਪਮਾ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ, ਰੂਪ ਰਹਿਤ ਅਤੇ ਸਭ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੱਸਦਾ ਕਹਿੰਦੀ ਹੈ। ਛੰਦ ਦੇ ਇਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਪੱਖਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਇਕੱਠੇ ਪੜ੍ਹਨਾ ਹੈ; ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਸੁਖਦਾਇਕ ਭਾਵਨਾ ਜਾਂ ਇੱਕ ਨਜ਼ਰ ਆਉਣ ਵਾਲੀ ਵਸਤ ਤਕ ਘਟਾ ਦੇਣਾ ਪੂਰਾ ਅਰਥ ਨਹੀਂ ਬਣਦਾ।

study.focus: Notice the deliberate proximity of lasting being, bliss, endings and universal presence.
study.closeReading: ਸਦਾ stands at the opening, but the same line also contains ਪ੍ਰਣਾਸੀ. A quick reading that notices only bliss misses the ending of created things; a reading that notices only destruction misses the opening attributes. The next line moves from what cannot adequately describe or contain the Divine to presence within all. The movement is not a new physical description of the universe. It is a pattern of praise that both uses words and acknowledges their limits. The familiar sat-chit-anand explanation helps unpack the compound, while the source line itself keeps its own spelling and is never replaced with an expanded formula.

words.workingGloss: true being, awareness and bliss in the conventional explanation
the One who brings all to its end

study.interpretationCare: Anand is ascribed to the Divine; it does not require every reader to feel happy at every moment. The line gives no date for cosmic destruction and no permission to hasten anyone’s death. The traditional compound is not a claim about a measurable state of the brain.
study.reflection: How might gratitude for something valuable change when you also recognise that its present form will not last forever?
study.teachBack: Name both sides of the first line and all three descriptions in the second, explaining why none should be omitted.

simple.en: The first line names gifts of attainment, understanding and growth. The second, in the selected spatial reading, moves through below, above and between before naming the removal of accumulated wrongdoing. The lesson keeps both the gifts and moral responsibility in view while leaving the disputed compound spellings open.
simple.pa: ਪਹਿਲੀ ਤੁਕ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਿੱਧੀ, ਬੁੱਧੀ ਅਤੇ ਵਾਧੇ ਦੀਆਂ ਦਾਤਾਂ ਦਾ ਜ਼ਿਕਰ ਹੈ। ਦੂਜੀ ਤੁਕ ਦੇ ਚੁਣੇ ਹੋਏ ਅਰਥ ਵਿੱਚ ਹੇਠਾਂ, ਉੱਪਰ ਅਤੇ ਵਿਚਕਾਰ ਹਰ ਥਾਂ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਵਿਆਪਕਤਾ ਆਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ, ਫਿਰ ਪਾਪਾਂ ਦੇ ਸਮੂਹ ਨੂੰ ਦੂਰ ਕਰਨ ਦੀ ਗੱਲ ਹੈ। ਦਾਤ ਮਿਲਣ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਆਪਣੇ ਕਰਮਾਂ ਦੀ ਜ਼ਿੰਮੇਵਾਰੀ ਵੀ ਯਾਦ ਰਹੇ। ਸੰਯੁਕਤ ਸ਼ਬਦਾਂ ਦੇ ਲਿਖਤ-ਫ਼ਰਕ ਹਾਲੇ ਖੁੱਲ੍ਹੇ ਹਨ।

study.focus: Distinguish attainment, understanding and growth, then read the whole second line without losing its final moral language.
study.closeReading: The opening line repeats a giving-related ending before moving to ਕਰਤਾ. This supports a reading of several related gifts, rather than treating ਸਿਧਦਾ and ਬੁਧਦਾ as personal names. The source spellings still differ from another consulted text, so the analysis remains bounded. In the second line the selected spatial sequence covers below, above and the intervening region; the last words turn to the amassed burden of wrongdoing. A second commentary attaches the initial descriptors to wrongdoing itself. Stating that difference openly is more useful than making the sentence sound certain by silently choosing different original letters or suppressing half of the line.

words.workingGloss: granting attainment, in the selected compound reading
granting understanding, in the selected compound reading
below, above and between in the selected reading
an accumulation or multitude of wrongdoing

study.interpretationCare: Attainment language does not guarantee occult powers, wealth or increasing status. The reading about wrongdoing should not be carried backwards into Chhands 55–56 as an explanation for someone’s illness. Hope for release from wrongdoing does not cancel apology, repair or accountability.
study.reflection: What is one place where increased understanding could help you recognise and repair harm you previously overlooked?
study.teachBack: Name the three gifts in the first line, explain the selected spatial reading of the second, and identify the alternative that remains open.

simple.en: Supreme greatness is joined to sustaining care that is not ordinarily seen. The next line repeats the sense of always and names a merciful giver of attainment. The focus is a continuing relationship of dependence and gratitude. The reading of ਸਿੱਧ remains provisional because the consulted texts differ.
simple.pa: ਛੰਦ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਸ੍ਰੇਸ਼ਟ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਗੁਪਤ ਰੂਪ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਭ ਦੀ ਪਾਲਣਾ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਾ ਕਹਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ। ਅਗਲੀ ਤੁਕ ਸਦਾ ਅਤੇ ਸਰਬਦਾ ਰਾਹੀਂ ਹਰ ਵੇਲੇ ਦੀ ਗੱਲ ਦੋਹਰਾਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਦਿਆਲੂ ਦਾਤੇ ਨੂੰ ਯਾਦ ਕਰਦੀ ਹੈ। ਇਸ ਅਰਥ ਵਿੱਚ ਆਸਰੇ ਅਤੇ ਸ਼ੁਕਰਾਨੇ ਦਾ ਭਾਵ ਮੁੱਖ ਹੈ। ਸਿੱਧ ਅਤੇ ਸਿਧਿ ਦੇ ਲਿਖਤ-ਫ਼ਰਕ ਦਾ ਨਿਰਣਾ ਹਾਲੇ ਨਹੀਂ ਕੀਤਾ ਗਿਆ।

study.focus: Read supreme greatness together with hidden care, continuity and mercy.
study.closeReading: The first line builds its address through ਪਰੰ, ਪਰਮ and ਪਰਮੇਸ੍ਵਰੰ before arriving at ਪਾਲੰ. Grandeur therefore leads into the language of sustaining. ਪ੍ਰੋਛ qualifies how that care is understood in the selected reading: it need not appear as an object that can be pointed out. The second line repeats temporal language before naming the giver and mercy. The lesson retains attainment vocabulary without converting it into a technique for acquiring powers. The spelling difference around ਸਿੱਧ is part of the source line’s review history; a plausible explanation is not a substitute for qualified source review.

words.workingGloss: sustaining while unseen, in this reading
giver of attainment, provisionally following commentary

study.interpretationCare: Hidden care is not a claim that a reader must have a vision or that visual ability determines spiritual worth. The verse offers no guarantee of special powers or fulfilled wishes. Its praise should leave room to acknowledge the real people whose often unnoticed work supports daily life.
study.reflection: What care or support have you received without seeing all the work behind it, and how might you respond with gratitude?
study.teachBack: Explain what the selected ਪ੍ਰੋਛ ਪਾਲੰ reading adds to the first line, and identify the three emphases of the closing line: continuity, giving and mercy.

jaap|jaap001.line01.simpleEn: The Divine is not contained by emblems, social colour, caste or inherited rank.
jaap|jaap001.line01.simplePa: ਅਕਾਲ ਪੁਰਖ ਨੂੰ ਚਿੰਨ੍ਹ, ਰੰਗ, ਜਾਤ ਜਾਂ ਪਾਤ ਦੀ ਹੱਦ ਵਿਚ ਨਹੀਂ ਬੰਨ੍ਹ ਸਕਦੇ।
jaap|jaap001.line01.interpretiveCaution: The opening names human categories to question their application to the One.

jaap|jaap001.line02.simpleEn: No outward shape, appearance, distinguishing mark or clothing can fully depict the One.
jaap|jaap001.line02.simplePa: ਕੋਈ ਰੂਪ, ਰੰਗ, ਨਿਸ਼ਾਨ ਜਾਂ ਭੇਖ ਉਸ ਦੀ ਪੂਰੀ ਪਛਾਣ ਨਹੀਂ ਬਣਾ ਸਕਦਾ।
jaap|jaap001.line02.interpretiveCaution: Keep this poetic refusal of limiting form distinct from claims about how a human should dress.

jaap|jaap002.line01.simpleEn: A salutation to the Timeless One.
jaap|jaap002.line01.interpretiveCaution: A short salutation, not a definition that exhausts the Divine.

jaap|jaap002.line02.simpleEn: A salutation to the Compassionate One.
jaap|jaap002.line02.interpretiveCaution: Compassion sits beside timelessness in this chhand.

jaap|jaap002.line03.simpleEn: A salutation to the One beyond limiting form.
jaap|jaap002.line03.simplePa: ਰੂਪ ਦੀ ਹੱਦ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ।
jaap|jaap002.line03.interpretiveCaution: A devotional name, not an argument that images are the same as the One.

jaap|jaap002.line04.simpleEn: A salutation to the Incomparable One.
jaap|jaap002.line04.simplePa: ਜਿਸ ਦੀ ਤੁਲਨਾ ਨਹੀਂ, ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ।
jaap|jaap002.line04.interpretiveCaution: The phrase completes the fourfold salutation.

savaiye|savaiye09.line04.simpleEn: The stanza culminates in a striking affirmation that love is the way to encounter the Divine.
savaiye|savaiye09.line04.simplePa: ਆਖ਼ਰੀ ਤੁਕ ਪ੍ਰੇਮ ਨੂੰ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨਾਲ ਮਿਲਾਪ ਦਾ ਮੁੱਖ ਰਾਹ ਦੱਸਦੀ ਹੈ।
savaiye|savaiye09.line04.interpretiveCaution: Interpretation of ਪ੍ਰੇਮ here needs contextual Sikh/Dasam scholarly review.

savaiye|savaiye04.line01.simpleEn: The line lists pilgrimage, giving, restraint and other religious disciplines.
savaiye|savaiye04.line01.simplePa: ਇਸ ਤੁਕ ਵਿਚ ਤੀਰਥ, ਦਾਨ, ਸੰਜਮ ਅਤੇ ਹੋਰ ਧਾਰਮਿਕ ਕਰਮਾਂ ਦਾ ਜ਼ਿਕਰ ਹੈ।
savaiye|savaiye04.line01.interpretiveCaution: This line lists practices; the entire stanza develops the contrast with inner devotion.

chaupai|chaupai-rehras01.line01.simpleEn: An opening request for Divine protection.
chaupai|chaupai-rehras01.line01.simplePa: ਪਹਿਲੀ ਤੁਕ ਵਿਚ ਰੱਬੀ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਦੀ ਬੇਨਤੀ ਹੈ।
chaupai|chaupai-rehras01.line01.interpretiveCaution: Do not present this plea as a safety guarantee.

chaupai|chaupai-rehras01.line02.simpleEn: A prayer that heartfelt hopes may be fulfilled.
chaupai|chaupai-rehras01.line02.simplePa: ਮਨ ਦੀਆਂ ਆਸਾਂ ਪੂਰੀਆਂ ਹੋਣ ਦੀ ਬੇਨਤੀ ਹੈ।
chaupai|chaupai-rehras01.line02.interpretiveCaution: This is prayer language, not a prediction of material results.

chaupai|chaupai-rehras01.line03.simpleEn: May my mind remain turned toward Your feet, an image of devoted refuge.
chaupai|chaupai-rehras01.line03.simplePa: ਮੇਰਾ ਮਨ ਤੇਰੇ ਚਰਨਾਂ ਦੀ ਸ਼ਰਨ ਵਿਚ ਲੱਗਾ ਰਹੇ।
chaupai|chaupai-rehras01.line03.interpretiveCaution: Feet/charan functions as devotional imagery, not merely physical geography.

chaupai|chaupai-rehras01.line04.simpleEn: Care for me as one who belongs to You.
chaupai|chaupai-rehras01.line04.interpretiveCaution: The relationship matters as much as the protection requested.

anand|anand01.line01.simpleEn: Bliss has arisen, O mother, because I have found the True Guru.
anand|anand01.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਮਾਏ, ਸਤਿਗੁਰੂ ਮਿਲਣ ਨਾਲ ਮੇਰੇ ਅੰਦਰ ਅਨੰਦ ਹੋਇਆ ਹੈ।
anand|anand01.line01.interpretiveCaution: A poetic first-person declaration, not a diagnosis of constant emotional happiness.

anand|anand02.line01.simpleEn: O my mind, remain in remembrance of the Divine.
anand|anand02.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਮੇਰੇ ਮਨ, ਸਦਾ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਲ ਜੁੜਿਆ ਰਹੁ।
anand|anand02.line01.interpretiveCaution: The speaker is addressing the mind; do not convert this into a medical claim.

anand|anand07.line01.simpleEn: Many speak of bliss, but the Guru’s wisdom shows what it truly is.
anand|anand07.line01.simplePa: ਅਨੰਦ ਦਾ ਨਾਂ ਸਭ ਲੈਂਦੇ ਹਨ; ਉਸ ਦੀ ਡੂੰਘੀ ਸਮਝ ਗੁਰੂ ਤੋਂ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ।
anand|anand07.line01.interpretiveCaution: The distinction between saying a word and experiencing its meaning matters.

sohila|sohila01.line03.simpleEn: Where the Creator is praised and reflected upon, spiritual understanding is cultivated.
sohila|sohila01.line03.simplePa: ਜਿੱਥੇ ਕਰਤਾਰ ਦੀ ਸਿਫ਼ਤ ਅਤੇ ਵਿਚਾਰ ਹੁੰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਉੱਥੇ ਮਨ ਨੂੰ ਸਿੱਖਣ ਦਾ ਮੌਕਾ ਮਿਲਦਾ ਹੈ।
sohila|sohila01.line03.interpretiveCaution: Read with the following invitation to sing praise, not as an address to one physical house only.

sohila|sohila03.line02.simpleEn: The sky is imagined as a platter, the sun and moon as lamps, and stars as jewels.
sohila|sohila03.line02.simplePa: ਆਕਾਸ਼ ਥਾਲ, ਸੂਰਜ ਤੇ ਚੰਦ ਦੀਵੇ ਅਤੇ ਤਾਰੇ ਮੋਤੀਆਂ ਵਾਂਗ ਹਨ।
sohila|sohila03.line02.interpretiveCaution: Cosmic aarti poetry, not an astronomical mechanism.

sohila|sohila05.line02.simpleEn: Listen, friends: this is the time to serve with humility.
sohila|sohila05.line02.simplePa: ਸੁਣੋ ਮਿੱਤਰੋ, ਇਹ ਸੇਵਾ ਦਾ ਵੇਲਾ ਹੈ।
sohila|sohila05.line02.interpretiveCaution: Its urgency arises from the whole shabad’s reflection on time.

rehras|rehras.chaupai-rehras01.line01.simpleEn: The Rehras source now turns to a request for protection from Benti Chaupai.
rehras|rehras.chaupai-rehras01.line01.simplePa: ਰਹਿਰਾਸਿ ਵਿਚ ਇੱਥੇ ਬੇਨਤੀ ਚੌਪਈ ਦੀ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਵਾਲੀ ਅਰਦਾਸ ਸ਼ੁਰੂ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ।
rehras|rehras.chaupai-rehras01.line01.interpretiveCaution: The source family changes to Dasam Bani at this point.

rehras|rehras.anand01.line01.simpleEn: The selected Anand portion begins with joy arising through finding the True Guru.
rehras|rehras.anand01.line01.simplePa: ਰਹਿਰਾਸਿ ਦੇ ਚੁਣੇ ਅਨੰਦ ਭਾਗ ਦੀ ਸ਼ੁਰੂਆਤ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੂ ਮਿਲਣ ਦੀ ਖੁਸ਼ੀ ਨਾਲ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ।
rehras|rehras.anand01.line01.interpretiveCaution: Anand’s forty-pauri original composition remains separate.

sohila|sohila01.line01.simpleEn: Source heading: this is Sohila, in Raag Gauree Deepakee, attributed to Guru Nanak Sahib (Mahala 1).
sohila|sohila01.line01.simplePa: ਇਹ ਬਾਣੀ ਦਾ ਸਿਰਲੇਖ ਹੈ: ਸੋਹਿਲਾ, ਰਾਗ ਗਉੜੀ ਦੀਪਕੀ, ਮਹਲਾ ਪਹਿਲਾ — ਗੁਰੂ ਨਾਨਕ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਜੀ।
sohila|sohila01.line01.interpretiveCaution: A musical/source heading identifies the composition. It is not a new verse or a prescribed recording.

sohila|sohila01.line02.simpleEn: The opening invocation remembers the One, approached through the grace of the True Guru.
sohila|sohila01.line02.simplePa: ਆਰੰਭ ਵਿੱਚ ਇੱਕ ਅਕਾਲ ਪੁਰਖ ਅਤੇ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੂ ਦੀ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਰਾਹੀਂ ਉਸ ਦੀ ਪਛਾਣ ਦੀ ਯਾਦ ਹੈ।
sohila|sohila01.line02.interpretiveCaution: This is the written invocation, distinct from the shabad’s subsequent numbered lines.

sohila|sohila01.line04.simpleEn: In that place, sing the song of praise and keep the Creator in remembrance.
sohila|sohila01.line04.simplePa: ਉਸ ਥਾਂ ਸਿਫ਼ਤ ਦਾ ਸੋਹਿਲਾ ਗਾਵੋ ਅਤੇ ਆਪਣੇ ਸਿਰਜਣਹਾਰ ਨੂੰ ਯਾਦ ਰੱਖੋ।
sohila|sohila01.line04.interpretiveCaution: The phrase “that home” refers back to the gathering/place of praise and reflection in the previous line.

sohila|sohila01.line05.simpleEn: Sing the joyful song of praise to the Fearless One.
sohila|sohila01.line05.simplePa: ਮੇਰੇ ਨਿਰਭਉ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਵਡਿਆਈ ਦਾ ਸੋਹਿਲਾ ਗਾਓ।
sohila|sohila01.line05.interpretiveCaution: The Fearless One is the Divine being praised, not a claim that the worshipper never feels fear.

sohila|sohila01.line06.simpleEn: I cherish this song of praise, through which lasting spiritual peace is sought. This is the refrain.
sohila|sohila01.line06.simplePa: ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਸੋਹਿਲੇ ਤੋਂ ਸਦਕੇ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜਿਸ ਨਾਲ ਟਿਕਾਊ ਆਤਮਕ ਸੁਖ ਮਿਲਦਾ ਹੈ; ਇਹ ਰਹਾਉ ਦੀ ਤੁਕ ਹੈ।
sohila|sohila01.line06.interpretiveCaution: “Rahau” is the poem’s interpretive refrain, not a mechanical instruction about audio length.

sohila|sohila01.line07.simpleEn: Living beings are continually cared for; the Giver watches over and sustains them.
sohila|sohila01.line07.simplePa: ਜੀਵਾਂ ਦੀ ਨਿੱਤ ਸੰਭਾਲ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ; ਦਾਤਾਰ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੀ ਦੇਖਭਾਲ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।
sohila|sohila01.line07.interpretiveCaution: The care of living beings is a devotional statement, not a guarantee against hardship or illness.

sohila|sohila01.line08.simpleEn: Your gifts cannot be fully measured; how could we set a limit on You, the Giver?
sohila|sohila01.line08.simplePa: ਤੇਰੀਆਂ ਦਾਤਾਂ ਦਾ ਮੁੱਲ ਪੂਰਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਪਾਇਆ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ; ਉਸ ਦਾਤਾਰ ਦਾ ਅੰਤ ਕੌਣ ਜਾਣ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ?
sohila|sohila01.line08.interpretiveCaution: The rhetorical question emphasizes the limits of human reckoning of generosity.

sohila|sohila01.line09.simpleEn: A date has been appointed; in wedding imagery, friends gather to prepare and anoint the bride with oil.
sohila|sohila01.line09.simplePa: ਵਿਆਹ ਦੇ ਰੂਪਕ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਾਹਾ ਮਿਥਿਆ ਗਿਆ ਹੈ; ਸਹੇਲੀਆਂ ਰਲ ਕੇ ਤੇਲ ਦੀ ਰਸਮ ਦੀ ਤਿਆਰੀ ਕਰਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ।
sohila|sohila01.line09.interpretiveCaution: Wedding preparations are a metaphor for a soul facing a destined departure, not a literal ceremony required of readers.

sohila|sohila01.line10.simpleEn: Friends, give your blessings so that union with the Beloved Lord may come about.
sohila|sohila01.line10.simplePa: ਹੇ ਸੱਜਣੋ, ਅਸੀਸਾਂ ਦਿਓ ਕਿ ਮੇਰਾ ਆਪਣੇ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਨਾਲ ਮਿਲਾਪ ਹੋਵੇ।
sohila|sohila01.line10.interpretiveCaution: The blessings continue the wedding/union metaphor; they are not a predicted event date.

sohila|sohila01.line11.simpleEn: The invitation reaches every home; calls to depart keep arriving.
sohila|sohila01.line11.simplePa: ਹਰ ਘਰ ਸੱਦੇ ਪਹੁੰਚਦੇ ਹਨ; ਵਿਦਾਈ ਦਾ ਬੁਲਾਵਾ ਨਿੱਤ ਆ ਰਿਹਾ ਹੈ।
sohila|sohila01.line11.interpretiveCaution: The imagery speaks to mortality across all households, not a request to fear a particular day.

sohila|sohila01.line12.simpleEn: Remember the One who calls, says Nanak; our own days of departure will also come.
sohila|sohila01.line12.simplePa: ਨਾਨਕ ਆਖਦੇ ਹਨ: ਸੱਦਾ ਭੇਜਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਨੂੰ ਸਿਮਰੋ, ਕਿਉਂਕਿ ਸਾਡੇ ਲਈ ਵੀ ਉਹ ਦਿਨ ਆਉਣੇ ਹਨ।
sohila|sohila01.line12.interpretiveCaution: Mortality imagery invites meaningful remembrance; it is not a prediction of anyone’s lifespan.

sohila|sohila02.line01.simpleEn: Source heading: Raag Aasaa, Mahala 1, attributed to Guru Nanak Sahib.
sohila|sohila02.line01.simplePa: ਇਹ ਸਿਰਲੇਖ ਰਾਗ ਆਸਾ ਅਤੇ ਮਹਲਾ ਪਹਿਲਾ — ਗੁਰੂ ਨਾਨਕ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਜੀ — ਦਰਸਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
sohila|sohila02.line01.interpretiveCaution: Raag information is source metadata; it does not certify a particular modern melody.

sohila|sohila02.line02.simpleEn: The verse names six schools, six teachers and six forms of instruction.
sohila|sohila02.line02.simplePa: ਤੁਕ ਛੇ ਮੱਤਾਂ ਜਾਂ ਸ਼ਾਸਤਰਾਂ, ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਛੇ ਗੁਰੂਆਂ ਅਤੇ ਛੇ ਉਪਦੇਸ਼ਾਂ ਦਾ ਜ਼ਿਕਰ ਕਰਦੀ ਹੈ।
sohila|sohila02.line02.interpretiveCaution: The traditional “six” refers to philosophical systems, not necessarily six separate physical houses.

sohila|sohila02.line03.simpleEn: Their forms and teachings may be many, yet the ultimate Divine Source is One.
sohila|sohila02.line03.simplePa: ਉਪਦੇਸ਼ ਅਤੇ ਰੂਪ ਕਈ ਹੋ ਸਕਦੇ ਹਨ, ਪਰ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਪਿੱਛੇ ਮੂਲ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਇੱਕੋ ਹੈ।
sohila|sohila02.line03.interpretiveCaution: This poetic claim of oneness does not mean that all historical philosophies agree on every doctrine.

sohila|sohila02.line04.simpleEn: O friend, hold close the place in which the Creator’s praise is spoken.
sohila|sohila02.line04.simplePa: ਹੇ ਭਾਈ, ਜਿਸ ਥਾਂ ਕਰਤਾਰ ਦੀ ਸਿਫ਼ਤ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ, ਉਸ ਥਾਂ ਵੱਲ ਧਿਆਨ ਦੇ।
sohila|sohila02.line04.interpretiveCaution: The “house” can describe the gathering or environment of praise and reflection.

sohila|sohila02.line05.simpleEn: Protect that place of praise; it is for your good. This is the central refrain.
sohila|sohila02.line05.simplePa: ਉਸ ਸਿਫ਼ਤ ਵਾਲੇ ਆਸਰੇ ਨੂੰ ਸੰਭਾਲ ਕੇ ਰੱਖ, ਇਸੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਤੇਰੀ ਭਲਾਈ ਹੈ; ਇਹ ਰਹਾਉ ਹੈ।
sohila|sohila02.line05.interpretiveCaution: The refrain gives practical focus to praise, not preference for any particular building.

sohila|sohila02.line06.simpleEn: Moments, hours, watches, lunar days, weekdays and months make up the changing measures of time.
sohila|sohila02.line06.simplePa: ਵਿਸੁਏ, ਚਸੇ, ਘੜੀਆਂ, ਪਹਰ, ਥਿੱਤਾਂ, ਵਾਰ ਅਤੇ ਮਹੀਨੇ — ਸਮੇਂ ਦੇ ਕਈ ਮਾਪ ਹਨ।
sohila|sohila02.line06.interpretiveCaution: Ancient time units are named as a poetic list; their precise conversion is not the focus of this teaching note.

sohila|sohila02.line07.simpleEn: There is one sun, though it is experienced across many seasons.
sohila|sohila02.line07.simplePa: ਸੂਰਜ ਇੱਕੋ ਹੈ ਪਰ ਰੁੱਤਾਂ ਅਨੇਕ ਹਨ।
sohila|sohila02.line07.interpretiveCaution: The single sun and many seasons illustrate unity amid changing appearances.

sohila|sohila02.line08.simpleEn: Nanak says the Creator appears to us in countless forms and expressions.
sohila|sohila02.line08.simplePa: ਨਾਨਕ ਆਖਦੇ ਹਨ ਕਿ ਕਰਤਾਰ ਦੇ ਰੂਪ ਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਗਟਾਵੇ ਅਨੇਕ ਹਨ।
sohila|sohila02.line08.interpretiveCaution: This closes the sun/seasons comparison without limiting the Divine to visible physical shapes.

sohila|sohila03.line01.simpleEn: Source heading: Raag Dhanaasree, Mahala 1, attributed to Guru Nanak Sahib.
sohila|sohila03.line01.simplePa: ਇਹ ਸਿਰਲੇਖ ਰਾਗ ਧਨਾਸਰੀ ਅਤੇ ਮਹਲਾ ਪਹਿਲਾ — ਗੁਰੂ ਨਾਨਕ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਜੀ — ਦੱਸਦਾ ਹੈ।
sohila|sohila03.line01.interpretiveCaution: A written raag heading is separate from a claim about an audio recording’s performance.

sohila|sohila03.line03.simpleEn: Fragrant air becomes incense, the wind waves the ceremonial fan, and the flowering forest joins the light-filled offering.
sohila|sohila03.line03.simplePa: ਸੁਗੰਧੀ ਹਵਾ ਧੂਪ ਵਾਂਗ, ਪਵਣ ਚੌਰ ਵਾਂਗ ਅਤੇ ਫੁੱਲਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਭਰੇ ਬਨ ਸਿਰਜਣਹਾਰ ਦੀ ਆਰਤੀ ਦਾ ਰੂਪ ਬਣਦੇ ਹਨ।
sohila|sohila03.line03.interpretiveCaution: Nature supplies poetic ritual imagery; the text is not prescribing a ritual instrument list.

sohila|sohila03.line04.simpleEn: What an extraordinary act of praise this is!
sohila|sohila03.line04.simplePa: ਕਿੰਨੀ ਅਦਭੁਤ ਆਰਤੀ ਦੀ ਇਹ ਤਸਵੀਰ ਹੈ!
sohila|sohila03.line04.interpretiveCaution: The exclamation follows cosmic imagery; it is not an ordinary question about how to perform a ritual.

sohila|sohila03.line05.simpleEn: O One who frees beings from the bondage of coming and going, this vast praise is Your aarti.
sohila|sohila03.line05.simplePa: ਹੇ ਜਨਮ-ਮਰਨ ਦੇ ਬੰਧਨ ਕੱਟਣ ਵਾਲੇ, ਇਹ ਵਿਸ਼ਾਲ ਵਡਿਆਈ ਤੇਰੀ ਆਰਤੀ ਹੈ।
sohila|sohila03.line05.interpretiveCaution: Bhav-khandan is devotional language about spiritual bondage, not a clinical claim.

sohila|sohila03.line06.simpleEn: The unstruck sound is imagined as a great drum of praise; the refrain calls attention to the divine offering.
sohila|sohila03.line06.simplePa: ਅਨਹਦ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਵੱਡੀ ਭੇਰੀ ਦੇ ਨਾਦ ਵਾਂਗ ਵੱਜਦਾ ਦਿਖਾਇਆ ਹੈ; ਰਹਾਉ ਆਰਤੀ ਦੇ ਭਾਵ ਉੱਤੇ ਧਿਆਨ ਦਿਵਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
sohila|sohila03.line06.interpretiveCaution: Anhad imagery should not be turned into a scientifically specified acoustic frequency.

sohila|sohila03.line07.simpleEn: You are praised as having countless eyes, yet no one limited eye; countless forms, yet no single confining form.
sohila|sohila03.line07.simplePa: ਤੇਰੀਆਂ ਅਣਗਿਣਤ ਅੱਖਾਂ ਤੇ ਰੂਪ ਕਹੇ ਗਏ ਹਨ, ਫਿਰ ਵੀ ਤੂੰ ਕਿਸੇ ਇੱਕ ਅੱਖ ਜਾਂ ਰੂਪ ਦੀ ਹੱਦ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਹੀਂ।
sohila|sohila03.line07.interpretiveCaution: The apparent contradiction is deliberate: Divine presence throughout creation without a limiting body.

sohila|sohila03.line08.simpleEn: Countless pure feet and perceptions are Yours, yet You are not restricted to one physical foot or sense of smell; this wonder captivates the speaker.
sohila|sohila03.line08.simplePa: ਅਨੇਕ ਪਵਿੱਤਰ ਚਰਨ ਅਤੇ ਸੁਗੰਧ ਦੇ ਅਨੁਭਵ ਤੇਰੇ ਦੱਸੇ ਹਨ, ਪਰ ਤੂੰ ਇੱਕ ਸਰੀਰਕ ਚਰਨ ਜਾਂ ਇੰਦਰੀ ਦੀ ਹੱਦ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਹੀਂ; ਇਹ ਅਚਰਜ ਮਨ ਨੂੰ ਮੋਹ ਲੈਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
sohila|sohila03.line08.interpretiveCaution: The verse pairs presence in all beings with the inability to assign one limiting physical body.
