jaap|jaap029.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਬੇਮਿਸਾਲ ਹੈਂ; ਕੋਈ ਤੁਲਨਾ ਤੇਰਾ ਪੂਰਾ ਸਰੂਪ ਨਹੀਂ ਦੱਸ ਸਕਦੀ।
jaap|jaap029.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਅਨੂਪ concerns the absence of an adequate comparison. Commentary also expresses this through the limits of praise; the line does not say that devotion or speaking of the Divine is pointless.

jaap|jaap029.line03.simpleEn: You are birthless; Your being does not begin with a birth.
jaap|jaap029.line03.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਅਜਨਮਾ ਹੈਂ; ਤੇਰੀ ਹੋਂਦ ਕਿਸੇ ਜਨਮ ਤੋਂ ਸ਼ੁਰੂ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੁੰਦੀ।
jaap|jaap029.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਅਜੂ is read as birthless here, as in the Rampur Khera steek. Mahan Kosh records both birthless and unmoving, while the Bhai Vir Singh commentary favours the latter. These are retained as distinct readings of this exact word.

jaap|jaap029.line04.simpleEn: You are not made from the material elements that compose created bodies.
jaap|jaap029.line04.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੇਰੀ ਹੋਂਦ ਸਿਰਜੇ ਹੋਏ ਸਰੀਰਾਂ ਵਾਂਗ ਪਦਾਰਥ ਦੇ ਤੱਤਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਬਣੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap029.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਅਭੂ is read here as not composed of the traditional five elements, following the Rampur Khera steek. The Bhai Vir Singh commentary gives an uncreated reading. Neither sense means nonexistent; the precise derivation remains for review.

jaap|jaap030.line01.simpleEn: You cannot be fully captured by an account, calculation or written description.
jaap|jaap030.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਕੋਈ ਲੇਖਾ, ਗਿਣਤੀ ਜਾਂ ਲਿਖਿਆ ਵਰਣਨ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਪੂਰੀ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ ਨਹੀਂ ਸਮੇਟ ਸਕਦਾ।
jaap|jaap030.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਅਲੇਖ is read through the limits of accounting and description. Some commentary stresses freedom from a written destiny. The main point is not that writing or careful study has no value.

jaap|jaap030.line02.simpleEn: You are not confined to a particular dress or outward religious appearance.
jaap|jaap030.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਕਿਸੇ ਇੱਕ ਪਹਿਰਾਵੇ ਜਾਂ ਬਾਹਰਲੇ ਧਾਰਮਿਕ ਭੇਖ ਵਿੱਚ ਸੀਮਤ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap030.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਅਭੇਖ denies that an outward costume defines the Divine. It does not dismiss the significance of a person’s chosen discipline, religious dress or Sikh identity.

jaap|jaap030.line03.simpleEn: No single name can contain the whole of who You are.
jaap|jaap030.line03.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਕੋਈ ਇੱਕ ਨਾਮ ਤੇਰੀ ਪੂਰੀ ਹਸਤੀ ਨੂੰ ਆਪਣੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਹੀਂ ਸਮੇਟ ਸਕਦਾ।
jaap|jaap030.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਅਨਾਮ is explained here as beyond the reach of a fully defining name. The poem itself uses many names, so namelessness is not a prohibition on Naam, remembrance or devotional address.

jaap|jaap030.line04.simpleEn: You are free from desire and are not driven by personal craving.
jaap|jaap030.line04.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਨਿੱਜੀ ਚਾਹ ਜਾਂ ਲਾਲਸਾ ਦੇ ਵੱਸ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap030.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਅਕਾਮ means without desire in this context; Mahan Kosh explicitly gives that sense for the Jaap Sahib usage. Do not confuse ਕਾਮ, desire, with an assertion that the Divine is useless or unable to act.

jaap|jaap031.line01.simpleEn: You are beyond what the mind can fully hold in contemplation.
jaap|jaap031.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਮਨ ਧਿਆਨ ਰਾਹੀਂ ਵੀ ਤੇਰੇ ਪੂਰੇ ਸਰੂਪ ਨੂੰ ਨਹੀਂ ਫੜ ਸਕਦਾ।
jaap|jaap031.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਅਧੇ is read through the limits of thought or contemplation, following Neki and the Bhai Vir Singh-derived account. Other readings differ: Mahan Kosh gives independence from external support, while Sant Sewa Singh says the Divine has no need to meditate on another. This draft selects the first sense without resolving the alternatives.

jaap|jaap031.line02.simpleEn: Your full mystery cannot be fathomed.
jaap|jaap031.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੇਰਾ ਪੂਰਾ ਭੇਦ ਨਹੀਂ ਪਾਇਆ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ।
jaap|jaap031.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਅਭੇ is read here through an unfathomable ਭੇਦ, following Sant Sewa Singh. The Bhai Vir Singh-derived account suggests absence of distinction or secrecy, and Neki uses a fearlessness-related sense. These readings should not be silently collapsed; ਅਭੀਤ in the final line clearly names fearlessness.

jaap|jaap031.line03.simpleEn: No power can conquer You or make You subject to another.
jaap|jaap031.line03.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਕੋਈ ਤਾਕਤ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਜਿੱਤ ਕੇ ਕਿਸੇ ਹੋਰ ਦੇ ਅਧੀਨ ਨਹੀਂ ਕਰ ਸਕਦੀ।
jaap|jaap031.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਅਜੀਤ denies being conquered. It renews the title already heard in earlier salutations, now in the direct ਹੈਂ form: You are. The claim concerns Divine sovereignty, not a prediction that a devotee will win every struggle.

jaap|jaap031.line04.simpleEn: You are free from fear of any other power.
jaap|jaap031.line04.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਕਿਸੇ ਹੋਰ ਤਾਕਤ ਦਾ ਡਰ ਨਹੀਂ।
jaap|jaap031.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਅਭੀਤ directly concerns freedom from fear. Beside ਅਜੀਤ, it distinguishes being beyond conquest from being beyond intimidation. The two descriptions are closely related without becoming one identical word meaning.

jaap|jaap032.line01.simpleEn: You are worthy of reverence throughout every age and realm.
jaap|jaap032.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਹਰ ਕਾਲ ਅਤੇ ਹਰ ਲੋਕ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਤਿਕਾਰਯੋਗ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap032.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਤ੍ਰਿਮਾਨ carries a threefold reference. Neki reads the three worlds, the Bhai Vir Singh-derived account reads the three times, and Sant Sewa Singh includes both. The broad paraphrase preserves reverence across those frames rather than inventing a negative meaning such as beyond honour.

jaap|jaap032.line02.simpleEn: You are the treasury of all gifts.
jaap|jaap032.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਸਾਰੀਆਂ ਦਾਤਾਂ ਦਾ ਖ਼ਜ਼ਾਨਾ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap032.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਨਿਧਾਨ introduces the image of a treasury or store. After the title of reverence, the verse turns toward what is received from the One. This image concerns abundance and its source; it does not specify a particular material reward.

jaap|jaap032.line03.simpleEn: You are present through the three qualities of creation.
jaap|jaap032.line03.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਸ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਟੀ ਦੇ ਤਿੰਨਾਂ ਗੁਣਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਵਿਆਪਕ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap032.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਤ੍ਰਿਬਰਗ is read here through the three gunas, following the selected Neki, Sewa Singh and Bhai Vir Singh-derived readings. Their precise descriptions of source and pervasion vary. The frozen ਹੈਂ is retained; the second digital witness has ਹੈ, an unresolved verb-form difference rather than a reason to rewrite the source.

jaap|jaap032.line04.simpleEn: You Yourself have not been brought into being by another.
jaap|jaap032.line04.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਕਿਸੇ ਹੋਰ ਨੇ ਪੈਦਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਕੀਤਾ।
jaap|jaap032.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਅਸਰਗ is read as uncreated. Beside ਤ੍ਰਿਬਰਗ, it places the One’s relation to creation alongside freedom from being one more created product. The two titles can be considered together without treating creation as absent.

jaap|jaap033.line01.simpleEn: You are unstained, beyond any limiting colour.
jaap|jaap033.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਨਿਰਮਲ ਹੈਂ ਅਤੇ ਕਿਸੇ ਇੱਕ ਰੰਗ ਨਾਲ ਸੀਮਤ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੁੰਦਾ।
jaap|jaap033.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਅਨੀਲ is approached through colourlessness and unstainedness in the consulted commentaries. The main sentence gives that devotional range rather than a physical colour. It returns to a theme heard earlier in ਅਨੀਲੇ without altering either source spelling.

jaap|jaap033.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੇਰੀ ਹੋਂਦ ਦਾ ਕੋਈ ਆਰੰਭ ਨਹੀਂ।
jaap|jaap033.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਅਨਾਦਿ negates an ਆਦਿ, beginning. It is stronger than saying the One is merely very old: the title does not assign an earlier date to an otherwise ordinary origin.

jaap|jaap033.line03.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਕੋਈ ਤਾਕਤ ਤੇਰੇ ਉੱਤੇ ਜਿੱਤ ਨਹੀਂ ਪਾ ਸਕਦੀ।
jaap|jaap033.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਅਜੇ is selected as unconquerable, agreeing with Neki, Sant Sewa Singh and the Bhai Vir Singh-derived account. Its shorter form should not automatically be confused with an unborn gloss; the explicit birth-related ਅਜਨਮ follows in the next chhand.

jaap|jaap033.line04.simpleEn: You are free in Your being, subject to no other power.
jaap|jaap033.line04.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਸੁਤੰਤਰ ਹੈਂ ਅਤੇ ਕਿਸੇ ਹੋਰ ਦੀ ਅਧੀਨਤਾ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਹੀਂ।
jaap|jaap033.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਅਜਾਦਿ is read through freedom or independence, following Neki and the Bhai Vir Singh-derived account. Sant Sewa Singh instead reads the One as the source even of Brahma, the traditional creator figure. The differing interpretations remain open; no unverified dictionary derivation is asserted.

jaap|jaap034.line01.simpleEn: You do not come into existence through birth.
jaap|jaap034.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੇਰੀ ਹੋਂਦ ਜਨਮ ਲੈਣ ਨਾਲ ਸ਼ੁਰੂ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੁੰਦੀ।
jaap|jaap034.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਅਜਨਮ directly removes birth as an origin. It concerns Divine being and does not make human birth, family life or the care of children spiritually inferior.

jaap|jaap034.line02.simpleEn: You cannot be confined to one colour or outward form.
jaap|jaap034.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਕਿਸੇ ਇੱਕ ਰੰਗ ਜਾਂ ਬਾਹਰਲੇ ਰੂਪ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਹੀਂ ਬੰਨ੍ਹਿਆ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ।
jaap|jaap034.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਅਬਰਨ is read through colour and appearance, as in the Punjabi steek and Bhai Vir Singh-derived account; Neki emphasises unstainedness. It renews the resistance to a fixed visible description, not an assertion that one human appearance is more sacred than another.

jaap|jaap034.line03.simpleEn: You are not composed of the material elements of the world.
jaap|jaap034.line03.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਸੰਸਾਰ ਦੇ ਭੌਤਿਕ ਤੱਤਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਬਣਿਆ ਹੋਇਆ ਨਹੀਂ।
jaap|jaap034.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਅਭੂਤ is read here through the classical material elements, supported by Sant Sewa Singh and Neki’s incorporeal sense. The Bhai Vir Singh-derived account also offers an unmanifest reading. This title does not say that the Divine is nonexistent or has no relation to the world.

jaap|jaap034.line04.simpleEn: You need no one to nourish or sustain Your existence.
jaap|jaap034.line04.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੇਰੀ ਹੋਂਦ ਦੀ ਪਾਲਣਾ ਲਈ ਕਿਸੇ ਹੋਰ ਆਸਰੇ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਨਹੀਂ।
jaap|jaap034.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਅਭਰਨ is provisionally read as needing no sustenance, following Sant Sewa Singh and Neki. Mahan Kosh explicitly cites Jaap for an adornment meaning, also reflected in the Bhai Vir Singh-derived account. That is a substantive alternative, not a spelling mistake to be silently repaired.

jaap|jaap035.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੇਰਾ ਨਾਸ ਨਹੀਂ ਕੀਤਾ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ।
jaap|jaap035.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਅਗੰਜ is approached as indestructible in the consulted readings. It resumes an earlier salutation’s theme in the short ਹੈਂ form, with the same Divine addressee.

jaap|jaap035.line02.simpleEn: Your being cannot be broken apart.
jaap|jaap035.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੇਰਾ ਸਰੂਪ ਟੁੱਟਣ ਜਾਂ ਭੰਨੇ ਜਾਣ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap035.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਅਭੰਜ concerns being unbroken. Beside ਅਗੰਜ, it adds the image of wholeness: destruction and fragmentation are related, but the two epithets need not be treated as one mechanically interchangeable word.

jaap|jaap035.line03.simpleEn: No opponent can overpower You in a contest.
jaap|jaap035.line03.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਕੋਈ ਤੇਰੇ ਨਾਲ ਜੂਝ ਕੇ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਵੱਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਹੀਂ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ।
jaap|jaap035.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਅਝੂਝ is read through the impossibility of successfully contending with the One. Sant Sewa Singh and the Bhai Vir Singh-derived account retain the struggle-image; Neki gives a broader invulnerability sense. The line offers praise, not instructions for fighting.

jaap|jaap035.line04.simpleEn: You are free from quarrel and turmoil.
jaap|jaap035.line04.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਝਗੜੇ ਅਤੇ ਉਲਝਣ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap035.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਅਝੰਝ is read through freedom from wrangling or agitation, following the Punjabi and Bhai Vir Singh-derived explanations. Neki’s inviolability wording is broader. The selected reading changes the final emphasis from resisting force to being untouched by quarrel.

jaap|jaap036.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੇਰੀ ਗਹਿਰਾਈ ਦੀ ਥਾਹ ਨਹੀਂ ਪਾਈ ਜਾ ਸਕਦੀ।
jaap|jaap036.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਅਮੀਕ is a depth-related word of Arabic origin, documented in Mahan Kosh with a Jaap citation. Its initial ਅ belongs to the word itself; it is not the negative prefix found in ਅਬੰਧ. Here depth describes Divine profundity rather than a measurable physical distance.

jaap|jaap036.line02.simpleEn: You are the companion and friend of all.
jaap|jaap036.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਸਭ ਦਾ ਸਾਥੀ ਅਤੇ ਮਿੱਤਰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap036.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਰਫ਼ੀਕ supplies companionship beside the preceding image of depth. The frozen ਫ਼ is retained even though the second digital witness prints ਫ; that open spelling difference does not authorize a silent source change or a different friendship meaning.

jaap|jaap036.line03.simpleEn: You remain free of the entangling business of the world.
jaap|jaap036.line03.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਸੰਸਾਰ ਦੇ ਧੰਧਿਆਂ ਦੀ ਉਲਝਣ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਹੀਂ ਫਸਦਾ।
jaap|jaap036.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਅਧੰਧ is read through freedom from worldly occupations and their entanglement. Neki’s unoccupied wording and the Bhai Vir Singh-derived illusion-related sense vary in emphasis. The selected reading concerns non-entanglement, not an instruction for people to abandon useful work.

jaap|jaap036.line04.simpleEn: No bond can hold You captive.
jaap|jaap036.line04.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਕੋਈ ਬੰਧਨ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਬੰਨ੍ਹ ਨਹੀਂ ਸਕਦਾ।
jaap|jaap036.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਅਬੰਧ directly names freedom from bondage. Placed after friendship and worldly affairs, it helps distinguish relationship from captivity: the One can be addressed as a friend without becoming someone’s possession.

jaap|jaap037.line01.simpleEn: You cannot be fully comprehended by our understanding.
jaap|jaap037.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਮਨੁੱਖੀ ਬੁੱਧੀ ਤੇਰੀ ਪੂਰੀ ਸਮਝ ਨਹੀਂ ਪਾ ਸਕਦੀ।
jaap|jaap037.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਨ੍ਰਿਬੂਝ concerns the limits of what can be understood about the One. The negation falls on our ability to comprehend fully; it is not a statement that the Divine lacks intelligence.

jaap|jaap037.line02.simpleEn: You lie beyond the full reach of our perception and insight.
jaap|jaap037.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਸਾਡੀ ਸੂਝ ਅਤੇ ਪਛਾਣ ਦੀ ਪੂਰੀ ਪਹੁੰਚ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap037.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਅਸੂਝ carries a related limit on discernment or recognition. The first two lines overlap deliberately, approaching incomprehensibility through ਬੂਝ and ਸੂਝ; they need not be forced into two unrelated doctrines.

jaap|jaap037.line03.simpleEn: You are beyond the rule of time and death.
jaap|jaap037.line03.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਸਮੇਂ ਅਤੇ ਮੌਤ ਦੇ ਵੱਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਹੀਂ।
jaap|jaap037.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਅਕਾਲ addresses the One beyond ਕਾਲ, whose range includes time and death. This title resumes a central name from Jaap’s opening salutations. It does not assign the reader a lifespan or promise escape from ordinary mortality.

jaap|jaap037.line04.simpleEn: No net of bondage can ensnare You.
jaap|jaap037.line04.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਬੰਧਨਾਂ ਦਾ ਕੋਈ ਜਾਲ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਫਸਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਸਕਦਾ।
jaap|jaap037.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਅਜਾਲ is read through freedom from a ਜਾਲ, net, with Maya and birth/death associations in the Punjabi and Bhai Vir Singh-derived explanations. Neki instead uses an unshakeable sense. The selected ਜਾਲ image is distinct from ਜਲ, water, encountered in Chhand 16.

jaap|jaap038.line01.simpleEn: You are the One addressed as Allah, worthy of devoted reverence.
jaap|jaap038.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਅਲਾਹ ਕਹਿ ਕੇ ਵੀ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਹੀ ਆਦਰ ਨਾਲ ਯਾਦ ਕੀਤਾ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap038.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਅਲਾਹ is read as the Divine name Allah, as in Neki and the Bhai Vir Singh commentary. Other Punjabi explanations connect it with freedom from gain or with being beyond attainment. These readings are distinct; the selected Divine-name sense does not change the frozen spelling.

jaap|jaap038.line02.simpleEn: You are not confined to any particular place or dwelling.
jaap|jaap038.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਕੋਈ ਇੱਕ ਥਾਂ ਜਾਂ ਟਿਕਾਣਾ ਤੇਰੀ ਹੋਂਦ ਨੂੰ ਸੀਮਤ ਨਹੀਂ ਕਰਦਾ।
jaap|jaap038.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਅਜਾਹ is read as without a fixed location, supported by Neki and the Rampur Khera steek. Another commentary uses glory and unveiled imagery; that alternative is recorded for specialist review, without asserting a settled etymology.

jaap|jaap038.line03.simpleEn: You are without end; no boundary brings Your being to a close.
jaap|jaap038.line03.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਬੇਅੰਤ ਹੈਂ; ਤੇਰੀ ਹੋਂਦ ਦਾ ਕੋਈ ਅੰਤ ਨਹੀਂ।
jaap|jaap038.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਅਨੰਤ names endlessness. The devotional claim is not a measurable estimate of physical size or a statement about the reader’s own lifespan.

jaap|jaap038.line04.simpleEn: You are supreme in greatness, beyond every ordinary comparison.
jaap|jaap038.line04.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਮਹਾਨ ਹੈਂ; ਆਮ ਤੁਲਨਾਵਾਂ ਤੇਰੀ ਵਡਿਆਈ ਨਹੀਂ ਸਮੇਟ ਸਕਦੀਆਂ।
jaap|jaap038.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਮਹੰਤ means supremely great in this address. The contextual sense should be distinguished from the title used for the head of a religious institution.

jaap|jaap039.line01.simpleEn: You cannot be enclosed by a defining outline or boundary.
jaap|jaap039.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਕੋਈ ਲਕੀਰ ਜਾਂ ਨਿਸ਼ਚਿਤ ਹੱਦ ਤੇਰੇ ਸਰੂਪ ਨੂੰ ਘੇਰ ਨਹੀਂ ਸਕਦੀ।
jaap|jaap039.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਅਲੀਕ is read through the absence of a limiting line or mark, the sense linked to Jaap Sahib in Mahan Kosh. Other commentary stresses inscrutability or affection. The separate Sanskrit dictionary sense of falsehood is not applied to this Divine epithet.

jaap|jaap039.line02.simpleEn: You have no equal or rival who can share Your supreme place.
jaap|jaap039.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੇਰੇ ਬਰਾਬਰ ਦਾ ਕੋਈ ਸ਼ਰੀਕ ਜਾਂ ਮੁਕਾਬਲੇ ਵਾਲਾ ਨਹੀਂ।
jaap|jaap039.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਨ੍ਰਿਸ੍ਰੀਕ is read as without an equal or rival. The source’s exact spelling is retained; this praise is not a claim that any human community is entitled to dominate another.

jaap|jaap039.line03.simpleEn: You need no outside support to sustain Your being.
jaap|jaap039.line03.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਆਪਣੀ ਹੋਂਦ ਲਈ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਕਿਸੇ ਹੋਰ ਆਸਰੇ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਨਹੀਂ।
jaap|jaap039.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਨ੍ਰਿਲੰਭ is read as needing no external support, supported by the Rampur Khera steek and Neki. The Bhai Vir Singh commentary offers an unreachable reading. It does not mean helpless or abandoned; its spelling is not silently changed to another witness’s form.

jaap|jaap039.line04.simpleEn: You are uncreated; no other being brings You into existence.
jaap|jaap039.line04.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਜਨਮ ਰਹਿਤ ਹੈਂ; ਤੈਨੂੰ ਕਿਸੇ ਹੋਰ ਨੇ ਪੈਦਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਕੀਤਾ।
jaap|jaap039.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਅਸੰਭ is read as birthless or ungenerated, the sense Mahan Kosh explicitly associates with Jaap Sahib. Other commentary emphasises unmanifest or self-radiant being. The ordinary sense of impossible is not the selected meaning here.

jaap|jaap040.line01.simpleEn: You are beyond the full reach of our senses and understanding.
jaap|jaap040.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਮਨ ਅਤੇ ਇੰਦ੍ਰੀਆਂ ਤੇਰੇ ਪੂਰੇ ਸਰੂਪ ਤਕ ਨਹੀਂ ਪਹੁੰਚ ਸਕਦੀਆਂ।
jaap|jaap040.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਅਗੰਮ concerns what cannot be fully reached or fathomed. The line expresses the limit of ordinary grasp; it does not declare remembrance, learning or a loving relationship impossible.

jaap|jaap040.line02.simpleEn: You are birthless; Your being does not begin through birth.
jaap|jaap040.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਅਜਨਮਾ ਹੈਂ; ਤੇਰੀ ਹੋਂਦ ਜਨਮ ਲੈਣ ਨਾਲ ਸ਼ੁਰੂ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੁੰਦੀ।
jaap|jaap040.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਅਜੰਮ names freedom from birth. This is a Divine attribute, not a statement that a person can avoid ordinary birth and death simply by repeating the line.

jaap|jaap040.line03.simpleEn: You are not composed of the material elements of the world.
jaap|jaap040.line03.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਸੰਸਾਰ ਦੇ ਭੌਤਿਕ ਤੱਤਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਬਣਿਆ ਹੋਇਆ ਨਹੀਂ।
jaap|jaap040.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਅਭੂਤ is read as beyond material or elemental composition, consistently with the identical line in Chhand 34. Commentary also gives an unmanifest reading of this repeated epithet. The traditional five-element vocabulary is not a modern chemical model, and the word does not mean a ghost here.

jaap|jaap040.line04.simpleEn: You are beyond physical touch and cannot be grasped as a material object.
jaap|jaap040.line04.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਸਰੀਰਕ ਛੋਹ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈਂ; ਤੈਨੂੰ ਪਦਾਰਥ ਵਾਂਗ ਫੜਿਆ ਨਹੀਂ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ।
jaap|jaap040.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਅਛੂਤ is explicitly glossed for Jaap Sahib in Mahan Kosh as beyond touch. This Divine epithet must be distinguished from the word’s harmful caste usage; it does not declare any people impure or unworthy of contact.

jaap|jaap041.line01.simpleEn: You are unseen, beyond the reach of ordinary sight.
jaap|jaap041.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਆਮ ਅੱਖੀਂ ਵੇਖਣ ਦੀ ਹੱਦ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap041.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਅਲੋਕ is read as unseen, as in the consulted Punjabi steek and Neki. Here it is not a dismissal of the world or a claim that particular visual experiences prove spiritual attainment.

jaap|jaap041.line02.simpleEn: You are free from sorrow; grief does not overwhelm Your being.
jaap|jaap041.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਸੋਗ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ ਹੈਂ; ਦੁੱਖ ਤੇਰੀ ਹੋਂਦ ਨੂੰ ਵੱਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਹੀਂ ਕਰਦਾ।
jaap|jaap041.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਅਸੋਕ names freedom from sorrow. It addresses the Divine; it does not shame human grief or promise that a devoted person will never feel sadness.

jaap|jaap041.line03.simpleEn: You are not bound by actions and their karmic consequences.
jaap|jaap041.line03.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਕਰਮ ਅਤੇ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਫਲਾਂ ਦੇ ਬੰਧਨ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਹੀਂ ਬੰਨ੍ਹਦੇ।
jaap|jaap041.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਅਕਰਮ is read through freedom from karmic bondage. Some translations emphasise freedom from ritual obligation. Neither reading makes the Divine incapable of action or excuses a person from responsibility.

jaap|jaap041.line04.simpleEn: You are free from delusion and the confusion it brings.
jaap|jaap041.line04.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਭਰਮ ਅਤੇ ਉਸ ਤੋਂ ਪੈਦਾ ਹੋਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਭੁਲੇਖੇ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap041.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਅਭਰਮ denies delusion or confusion. It should not be turned into a prohibition on honest questions; the poem describes the One addressed rather than a rule against inquiry.

jaap|jaap042.line01.simpleEn: You cannot be conquered or overcome by another power.
jaap|jaap042.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਕੋਈ ਹੋਰ ਤਾਕਤ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਜਿੱਤ ਜਾਂ ਹਰਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਸਕਦੀ।
jaap|jaap042.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਅਜੀਤ names the unconquerable One. The line does not transfer that quality to a reader’s body, status or personal conflicts.

jaap|jaap042.line02.simpleEn: You are fearless, not ruled by fear of another.
jaap|jaap042.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਨਿਰਭਉ ਹੈਂ; ਕਿਸੇ ਹੋਰ ਦਾ ਡਰ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਹੀਂ ਚਲਾਉਂਦਾ।
jaap|jaap042.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਅਭੀਤ concerns fearlessness. It is paired with being unconquerable but names a distinct quality: fear and defeat are not the same thing.

jaap|jaap042.line03.simpleEn: You remain unshaken; no outside force can dislodge Your being.
jaap|jaap042.line03.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਅਡੋਲ ਹੈਂ; ਕੋਈ ਬਾਹਰਲੀ ਤਾਕਤ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਡੁਲਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਸਕਦੀ।
jaap|jaap042.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਅਬਾਹ is read as unmoving or unshakable, consistently supported by Neki, the Rampur Khera steek and the Bhai Vir Singh commentary. It is not read as a statement about lacking arms.

jaap|jaap042.line04.simpleEn: Your depth cannot be fully fathomed or measured.
jaap|jaap042.line04.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਅਥਾਹ ਹੈਂ; ਤੇਰੀ ਪੂਰੀ ਡੂੰਘਾਈ ਮਾਪੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਜਾ ਸਕਦੀ।
jaap|jaap042.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਅਗਾਹ concerns unfathomable depth. Keep it distinct from ਅਬਾਹ: the first stresses steadiness, while this word points to the limit of reaching the full depth.

jaap|jaap043.line01.simpleEn: You are beyond measure; no scale can contain Your extent.
jaap|jaap043.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਮਿਣਤੀ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈਂ; ਕੋਈ ਮਾਪ ਤੇਰਾ ਪੂਰਾ ਵਿਸਥਾਰ ਨਹੀਂ ਦੱਸ ਸਕਦਾ।
jaap|jaap043.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਅਮਾਨ is read as immeasurable, the sense Mahan Kosh explicitly associates with Jaap Sahib. Other dictionary senses involving dishonour, trust or safety are not selected for this line.

jaap|jaap043.line02.simpleEn: You are the treasury from which every kind of abundance comes.
jaap|jaap043.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਹਰ ਕਿਸਮ ਦੀ ਦਾਤ ਅਤੇ ਖ਼ਜ਼ਾਨੇ ਦਾ ਸੋਮਾ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap043.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਨਿਧਾਨ supplies a treasury or storehouse image. In this praise it can include spiritual qualities and the gifts of existence; it is not a promise of money or possessions.

jaap|jaap043.line03.simpleEn: You are present through countless forms, appearing as many.
jaap|jaap043.line03.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਅਨੇਕਾਂ ਰੂਪਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਤੇਰੀ ਹੀ ਵਿਆਪਕਤਾ ਦਿੱਸਦੀ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap043.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਅਨੇਕ points to multiplicity. The following ਫਿਰਿ ਏਕ must remain with it: this line is not treated as a separate claim that the many have displaced the One.

jaap|jaap043.line04.simpleEn: Yet through all that multiplicity, You remain One.
jaap|jaap043.line04.simplePa: ਇਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਅਨੇਕ ਰੂਪਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੀ, ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਇੱਕੋ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap043.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਫਿਰਿ carries the return or contrast here: many, and still One. The frozen spelling ਫਿਰਿ is retained. The stanza does not describe a timetable in which separate gods later merge.

jaap|jaap044.line01.simpleEn: I bow to You, worthy of honour throughout creation.
jaap|jaap044.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਸਾਰੇ ਜਗਤ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਤਿਕਾਰਯੋਗ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap044.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਸਰਬ ਮਾਨੇ gives honour a universal scope. This is devotional praise, not a survey claiming that every person consciously holds the same belief. A separate Bhujang Prayat heading precedes this stanza.

jaap|jaap044.line02.simpleEn: You are the source and treasury of all abundance.
jaap|jaap044.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਸਭ ਨਿਧੀਆਂ ਅਤੇ ਦਾਤਾਂ ਦਾ ਭੰਡਾਰ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap044.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਸਮਸਤੀ ਨਿਧਾਨੇ continues the preceding salutation through the treasury image. Its opening is not ਨਮੋ in the frozen line; the explanation follows the continuing address without inserting a word into the scripture.

jaap|jaap044.line03.simpleEn: I bow to You, supreme even among those called divine.
jaap|jaap044.line03.simplePa: ਹੇ ਦੇਵਤਿਆਂ ਤੋਂ ਵੀ ਉੱਚੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap044.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਦੇਵ ਦੇਵੇ is a repeated-word intensification, commonly explained as the Divine above the devas. The Bhai Vir Singh commentary emphasises the radiance that gives them light. It does not require a modern factual ranking of celestial beings.

jaap|jaap044.line04.simpleEn: You are not defined by an outward guise, and Your being is undivided.
jaap|jaap044.line04.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਕਿਸੇ ਭੇਖ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਹੀਂ ਬੱਝਦਾ ਅਤੇ ਤੇਰੇ ਸਰੂਪ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੰਡ ਨਹੀਂ।
jaap|jaap044.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਅਭੇਖੀ concerns outward guise. ਅਭੇਵੇ is provisionally read as without division or distinction, within the ਭੇਦ-ਰਹਿਤ reading of the Punjabi steek and Bhai Vir Singh commentary. Explanations involving absence of concealment or secrets also occur; these distinct senses remain for qualified review.

jaap|jaap045.line01.simpleEn: I bow to You, whose sovereignty reaches even over death and time.
jaap|jaap045.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਕਾਲ ਵੀ ਤੇਰੇ ਵੱਸ ਹੈ; ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap045.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਕਾਲ ਕਾਲੇ renews the earlier intensified address: the One beyond the authority of death and time. It is not a guarantee that the person reciting will escape mortality.

jaap|jaap045.line02.simpleEn: I bow to You, who sustain and care for all beings.
jaap|jaap045.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਸਭ ਜੀਵਾਂ ਦੀ ਪਾਲਣਾ ਅਤੇ ਸੰਭਾਲ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap045.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਸਰਬ ਪਾਲੇ places universal care beside sovereignty over death. Both qualities address the same One; neither should be omitted when explaining this pair.

jaap|jaap045.line03.simpleEn: I bow to You, whose presence extends everywhere.
jaap|jaap045.line03.simplePa: ਹੇ ਸਭ ਥਾਵਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਵਿਆਪਕ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap045.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਸਰਬ ਗਉਣੇ is read through pervading or moving throughout all places. The exact ਗਉਣੇ spelling is retained; its sense here should not be selected simply by resemblance to the modern Punjabi verb for singing.

jaap|jaap045.line04.simpleEn: I bow to You, present throughout every realm and dwelling.
jaap|jaap045.line04.simplePa: ਹੇ ਸਾਰੇ ਭਵਨਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਟਿਕਾਣਿਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਵਿਆਪਕ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap045.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਸਰਬ ਭਉਣੇ reinforces presence in all places and realms. It is not limited to one building or shrine. Its overlap with the preceding line enriches the praise without requiring an artificial technical distinction.

jaap|jaap046.line01.simpleEn: You are without a physical body, and no other master rules over You.
jaap|jaap046.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਸਰੀਰ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ ਹੈਂ ਅਤੇ ਤੇਰੇ ਉੱਪਰ ਕੋਈ ਹੋਰ ਮਾਲਕ ਨਹੀਂ।
jaap|jaap046.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਅਨੰਗੀ concerns the absence of bodily limbs; ਅਨਾਥੇ concerns having no ਨਾਥ, master, above the One. Both epithets belong to this line. The second is a statement of Divine independence, not the ordinary social condition of an abandoned or unsupported person.

jaap|jaap046.line02.simpleEn: You depend on no companion and hold the power that brings creation to its end.
jaap|jaap046.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਕਿਸੇ ਸਾਥੀ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਨਹੀਂ ਅਤੇ ਸ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਟੀ ਦਾ ਅੰਤ ਕਰਨ ਦੀ ਸਮਰੱਥਾ ਤੇਰੇ ਕੋਲ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap046.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਨ੍ਰਿਸੰਗੀ is read through freedom from a necessary companion. ਪ੍ਰਮਾਥੇ is provisionally read as destructive or dissolving power, supported by Sant Sewa Singh and Neki. The Bhai Vir Singh-derived account instead develops a churning image. That alternative remains open; the main sentence does not turn the two words into a single title.

jaap|jaap046.line03.simpleEn: I bow to You, the radiance from which every sun receives its light.
jaap|jaap046.line03.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ; ਹਰ ਸੂਰਜ ਦਾ ਚਾਨਣ ਤੇਰੇ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਸ਼ ਤੋਂ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap046.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਭਾਨ is the sun. The repeated ਭਾਨ ਭਾਨੇ construction directs praise through the image of a sun beyond suns; the explanation selects the source-of-radiance emphasis. This whole original line recurs at 47.02, where its main bilingual explanation is identical.

jaap|jaap046.line04.simpleEn: I bow to You, the honour of all who are honoured.
jaap|jaap046.line04.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ; ਸਾਰੇ ਮਾਣ ਵਾਲਿਆਂ ਦਾ ਵੀ ਮਾਣ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap046.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਮਾਨ ਮਾਨੇ intensifies honour and reverence. It is read here as the One to whom even the honoured owe reverence, not as praise of personal arrogance. The same wording is used at 56.02; a bestower-of-honour emphasis also appears in Neki’s rendering there.

jaap|jaap047.line01.simpleEn: I bow to You, whose gentle radiance shines through every moon.
jaap|jaap047.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ; ਹਰ ਚੰਦ ਦੀ ਠੰਢੀ ਰੌਸ਼ਨੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਤੇਰੀ ਹੀ ਜੋਤ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap047.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਚੰਦ੍ਰ ਚੰਦ੍ਰੇ repeats the moon image to direct praise toward its supreme source. Coolness and gentle radiance follow the Punjabi commentary’s devotional emphasis. These are poetic associations of moonlight, not an explanation of how a physical moon produces or reflects light.

jaap|jaap047.line02.simpleEn: I bow to You, the radiance from which every sun receives its light.
jaap|jaap047.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ; ਹਰ ਸੂਰਜ ਦਾ ਚਾਨਣ ਤੇਰੇ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਸ਼ ਤੋਂ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap047.line02.interpretiveCaution: This is the exact original line already encountered at 46.03. Keeping the main explanation unchanged makes the repetition visible: the same sun image now stands immediately beside moon, song and melody. Context adds a relation without changing the word ਭਾਨ into a new epithet.

jaap|jaap047.line03.simpleEn: I bow to You, the song at the heart of every song.
jaap|jaap047.line03.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ; ਗੀਤਾਂ ਦਾ ਸਾਰ ਅਤੇ ਮਿਠਾਸ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap047.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਗੀਤ ਗੀਤੇ uses the same repeated-noun pattern as the celestial images. Song becomes a way of praising the One as its inner essence and delight. The line names no particular song, singer or musical tradition as an exclusive dwelling of the Divine.

jaap|jaap047.line04.simpleEn: I bow to You, the melody within every melody.
jaap|jaap047.line04.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ; ਹਰ ਤਾਨ ਦੀ ਸੁਰਿਲੀ ਧੁਨ ਦਾ ਆਧਾਰ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap047.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਤਾਨ is selected in its musical sense, supported by the adjacent ਗੀਤ, Sant Sewa Singh, Neki and the historical dictionary’s account of melodic movement. The Bhai Vir Singh-derived page gives power and instrument alternatives. Those are recorded rather than silently merged with the selected melody reading.

jaap|jaap048.line01.simpleEn: I bow to You, the living rhythm of every dance.
jaap|jaap048.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ; ਹਰ ਨਾਚ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੱਸਦੀ ਲੈ ਤੈਥੋਂ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap048.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਨ੍ਰਿੱਤ is read through dance and movement. Neki retains the dance image, while Sant Sewa Singh relates it to the movement of the world; the Bhai Vir Singh-derived account develops bliss and churning associations. The main explanation keeps the dance image without prescribing a performance. The frozen addak in ਨ੍ਰਿੱਤ is preserved.

jaap|jaap048.line02.simpleEn: I bow to You, the resonance at the heart of every sound.
jaap|jaap048.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ; ਹਰ ਨਾਦ ਦੇ ਅੰਦਰ ਗੂੰਜਦਾ ਸੁਰ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap048.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਨਾਦ concerns sound or resonance. The repeated ਨਾਦ ਨਾਦੇ carries praise through that image, following the dance line. It does not name one required pitch, an audible inner phenomenon or a test of the reader’s spiritual progress.

jaap|jaap048.line03.simpleEn: I bow to You, the strength within all hands.
jaap|jaap048.line03.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ; ਸਾਰੇ ਹੱਥਾਂ ਦੀ ਸਮਰੱਥਾ ਦਾ ਮੂਲ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap048.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਪਾਨ is provisionally read as hand, supported by Sant Sewa Singh, the Bhai Vir Singh-derived account and Mahan Kosh’s ਪਾਣਿ/ਹੱਥ sense. Neki instead gives a drum-beating image. The dictionary also lists unrelated homonyms, including drinking; they should not be substituted automatically. The original ਪਾਨ spelling is unchanged.

jaap|jaap048.line04.simpleEn: I bow to You, the music voiced through every instrument.
jaap|jaap048.line04.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ; ਹਰ ਸਾਜ਼ ਵਿੱਚ ਗੂੰਜਦੀ ਸੰਗੀਤ ਦੀ ਧੁਨ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap048.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਬਾਦ is read through ਵਾਦਯ, instrumental sound, following the musical context and the consulted commentaries. It is not taken here as the ordinary homonym for a quarrel. The pair praises the One through the sounding of instruments without naming a required instrument or method.

jaap|jaap049.line01.simpleEn: You are without bodily limbs, and no single name can contain You.
jaap|jaap049.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਸਰੀਰ ਦੇ ਅੰਗਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ ਹੈਂ ਅਤੇ ਕੋਈ ਇੱਕ ਨਾਮ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਪੂਰਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਬਿਆਨ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ।
jaap|jaap049.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਅਨੰਗੀ repeats the body-free title; ਅਨਾਮੇ adds namelessness. The explanation treats namelessness as the inability of a fixed descriptive name to exhaust the One. It does not deny the devotional remembrance of Naam, nor omit the first of the two epithets.

jaap|jaap049.line02.simpleEn: You are present in all the forms of creation.
jaap|jaap049.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਸ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਟੀ ਦੇ ਸਾਰੇ ਰੂਪਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਵਿਆਪਕ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap049.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਸਮਸਤੀ ਸਰੂਪੇ is a connected phrase concerning all forms, not two unrelated titles. Beside ਅਨੰਗੀ, it places pervasion of forms alongside freedom from a single body. The wording preserves that tension rather than claiming that the first line has been withdrawn.

jaap|jaap049.line03.simpleEn: You break apart what has been formed and bring it to an end.
jaap|jaap049.line03.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਬਣੇ ਹੋਏ ਰੂਪਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਭੰਗ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਾ ਅਤੇ ਉਹਨਾਂ ਦਾ ਅੰਤ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਾ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap049.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਪ੍ਰਭੰਗੀ and ਪ੍ਰਮਾਥੇ are both retained in this account of breaking and dissolution. Their overlap is not evidence that one may be skipped. The selected reading follows the Punjabi steek’s destruction emphasis; the Bhai Vir Singh-derived account distinguishes a breaking title from a churning title. The latter remains a real alternative.

jaap|jaap049.line04.simpleEn: All the abundance and splendour of creation rest in You.
jaap|jaap049.line04.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਸ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਟੀ ਦੀ ਸਾਰੀ ਸੰਪਦਾ ਅਤੇ ਵਡਿਆਈ ਤੇਰੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap049.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਬਿਭੂਤੇ is read through abundance, wealth and splendour; ਸਮਸਤੀ extends the phrase to all. Mahan Kosh distinguishes the wealth sense of ਬਿਭੂਤ from its ash-related homonym. Sant Sewa Singh stresses the treasury of all things, while Neki stresses the source of wealth. No material reward is promised to the reader.

jaap|jaap050.line01.simpleEn: Your being is entirely unstained; no blemish attaches to You.
jaap|jaap050.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੇਰਾ ਸਰੂਪ ਪੂਰੀ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ ਨਿਰਮਲ ਹੈ; ਕੋਈ ਕਲੰਕ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਹੀਂ ਲੱਗਦਾ।
jaap|jaap050.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਕਲੰਕੰ ਬਿਨਾ and ਨੇਕਲੰਕੀ reinforce one another: absence of blemish and unstained being. The whole phrase occupies one line. In this context, ਨੇਕਲੰਕੀ is not used to identify a particular Kalki incarnation or to replace the frozen spelling with another edition’s form.

jaap|jaap050.line02.simpleEn: I bow to You, the sovereign over every ruler, whose being is supreme.
jaap|jaap050.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ; ਤੂੰ ਸਾਰੇ ਰਾਜਿਆਂ ਦਾ ਮਹਾਰਾਜਾ ਹੈਂ ਅਤੇ ਤੇਰਾ ਸਰੂਪ ਪਰਮ ਮਹਾਨ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap050.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਰਾਜ ਰਾਜੇਸ੍ਵਰੰ and ਪਰਮ ਰੂਪੇ both belong to this line. The first places kings beneath Divine sovereignty; the second praises supreme being or form. Sant Sewa Singh brings out radiance, while Neki brings out supreme existence. The main paraphrase avoids reducing ਰੂਪ to bodily appearance.

jaap|jaap051.line01.simpleEn: I bow to You, master of the masters of yoga and supreme in spiritual perfection.
jaap|jaap051.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ; ਤੂੰ ਵੱਡੇ ਯੋਗੀਆਂ ਦਾ ਵੀ ਮਾਲਕ ਹੈਂ ਅਤੇ ਆਤਮਕ ਪੂਰਨਤਾ ਦਾ ਸਰਬੋਤਮ ਸਰੂਪ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap051.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਜੋਗ ਜੋਗੇਸ੍ਵਰੰ names mastery beyond the masters of yoga; ਪਰਮ ਸਿੱਧੇ adds supreme perfection or accomplishment. The Punjabi steek also emphasises mastery over siddhis. The draft keeps both clauses without claiming that the Divine had to acquire perfection through a bodily practice or that a reader will gain extraordinary powers.

jaap|jaap051.line02.simpleEn: I bow to You, ruler over all rulers, whose greatness is unsurpassed.
jaap|jaap051.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ; ਤੂੰ ਸਾਰੇ ਰਾਜਿਆਂ ਦਾ ਮਹਾਰਾਜਾ ਹੈਂ ਅਤੇ ਤੇਰੀ ਮਹਾਨਤਾ ਦਾ ਕੋਈ ਸਾਨੀ ਨਹੀਂ।
jaap|jaap051.line02.interpretiveCaution: The kingship phrase recurs from Chhand 50, but the ending is now ਪਰਮ ਬ੍ਰਿਧੇ. Sant Sewa Singh and the Bhai Vir Singh-derived account emphasise greatness; Neki emphasises esteem. The selected sense is eminence, not the age of a Divine body. The frozen ਬ੍ਰਿਧੇ is retained despite a comparator commentary’s ਬ੍ਰਿੱਧੇ spelling.

jaap|jaap052.line01.simpleEn: I bow to You, the bearer of weapons.
jaap|jaap052.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਸ਼ਸਤ੍ਰ ਧਾਰਨ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap052.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਪਾਣੇ presents a martial image of weapons borne in the hand. ਪਾਣੇ supplies the hand-bearing element. ਸਸਤ੍ਰ is a broad weapons term; it need not exclude the projected weapons named in the next line. This is a salutation to Divine power, not an instruction to arm or attack.

jaap|jaap052.line02.simpleEn: I bow to You, who wield weapons that are sent forth.
jaap|jaap052.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਅਸਤ੍ਰ ਚਲਾਉਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap052.line02.interpretiveCaution: Mahan Kosh distinguishes ਅਸਤ੍ਰ as a weapon projected or cast forth. Sant Sewa Singh explains the compound through using such weapons, while Neki stresses their projection. The Bhai Vir Singh-derived account develops an arrow-of-wisdom interpretation. That metaphor remains an attributed alternative, not a replacement of the martial wording.

jaap|jaap052.line03.simpleEn: I bow to You, whose knowing is complete.
jaap|jaap052.line03.simplePa: ਹੇ ਸਭ ਕੁਝ ਪੂਰੀ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ ਜਾਣਨ ਵਾਲੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap052.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਪਰਮ ਗਿਆਤਾ praises supreme knowing. It adds discernment to the preceding power images rather than naming another weapon. The frozen ਗਿਆਤਾ spelling is retained; a consulted commentary prints ਗਯਾਤਾ, which is recorded as that witness’s form rather than a correction.

jaap|jaap052.line04.simpleEn: I bow to You, the Mother who gives life and care to the world.
jaap|jaap052.line04.simplePa: ਹੇ ਜਗਤ ਦੀ ਮਾਤਾ ਸਰੂਪ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ; ਤੂੰ ਸਭ ਨੂੰ ਜੀਵਨ ਅਤੇ ਸੰਭਾਲ ਦਿੰਦਾ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap052.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਲੋਕ ਮਾਤਾ directly introduces the world’s Mother. The draft retains this maternal form of address and draws out its life-giving care. It is not a claim that the Divine is exclusively male or female, nor a restriction of human caregiving to women. The same One receives all four salutations.

jaap|jaap053.line01.simpleEn: You have no defining garb and are free from delusion; You do not depend on worldly enjoyment and cannot be made an object of enjoyment.
jaap|jaap053.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੇਰਾ ਕੋਈ ਨਿਸ਼ਚਿਤ ਭੇਖ ਨਹੀਂ ਅਤੇ ਤੂੰ ਭਰਮ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ ਹੈਂ; ਤੂੰ ਭੋਗਾਂ ਦਾ ਮੁਥਾਜ ਨਹੀਂ ਅਤੇ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਭੋਗ ਦੀ ਵਸਤ ਨਹੀਂ ਬਣਾਇਆ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ।
jaap|jaap053.line01.interpretiveCaution: The four epithets are kept distinct: ਅਭੇਖੀ concerns garb, ਅਭਰਮੀ delusion, ਅਭੋਗੀ worldly indulgence, and ਅਭੁਗਤੇ being enjoyed or consumed. The final phrase is a working paraphrase of the non-enjoyed sense in Punjabi commentary. Neki instead emphasises detachment and freedom from temptation. This address does not condemn human bodies or every form of joy.

jaap|jaap053.line02.simpleEn: I bow to You, supreme master of the yogis, whose way is complete.
jaap|jaap053.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਜੋਗੀਆਂ ਦੇ ਵੀ ਮਹਾਨ ਸੁਆਮੀ ਅਤੇ ਪੂਰਨ ਜੁਗਤ ਵਾਲੇ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap053.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਜੋਗ ਜੋਗੇਸ੍ਵਰੰ honours the Divine above masters of spiritual discipline. ਪਰਮ ਜੁਗਤੇ is provisionally read as supreme in method or wisdom of practice, following Punjabi commentary. A complete-union reading also occurs; Mahan Kosh includes both method and union within the related ਜੁਗਤਿ vocabulary. Neither reading supplies a physical yoga technique.

jaap|jaap054.line01.simpleEn: I bow to You, the enduring Narayan who sustains life and acts with fearsome power.
jaap|jaap054.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਸਦਾ ਕਾਇਮ ਨਾਰਾਇਣ, ਜੀਵਨ ਨੂੰ ਆਸਰਾ ਦੇਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਅਤੇ ਭਿਆਨਕ ਕਰਮ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap054.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਨਿੱਤ gives the enduring sense; ਨਾਰਾਇਣੇ is a Divine name associated here with sustaining care. ਕ੍ਰੂਰ ਕਰਮੇ retains the unsettling force of fierce or terrible action, including destruction, rather than turning it into gentle action alone. This is praise addressed to the Divine, not permission for human cruelty. The consulted texts differ between ਕ੍ਰੂਰ and ਕਰੂਰ; this explanation keeps the original wording.

jaap|jaap054.line02.simpleEn: I bow to You, the Divine light of the departed and the living, whose dharam is noble.
jaap|jaap054.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਮਰ ਚੁੱਕਿਆਂ ਤੇ ਜੀਉਂਦਿਆਂ ਦੀ ਜੋਤਿ ਅਤੇ ਸ੍ਰੇਸ਼ਟ ਧਰਮ ਵਾਲੇ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap054.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਪ੍ਰੇਤ/ਅਪ੍ਰੇਤ is provisionally heard as departed/not-departed, following one commentary’s contrast. Mahan Kosh supports departed as a sense of ਪ੍ਰੇਤ; it does not independently establish this whole paired reading. The Rampur Khera steek gives unsettled spirits and pure souls; another gloss contrasts inanimate and conscious being. ਦੇਵੇ is heard as Divine light and ਸੁਧਰਮੇ as excellent dharam. These alternatives remain open, without changing the text or treating spirit language as a diagnosis.

jaap|jaap055.line01.simpleEn: I bow to You, praised as the remover of illness and suffering.
jaap|jaap055.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਰੋਗ ਅਤੇ ਦੁੱਖ ਦੂਰ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲੇ ਵਜੋਂ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap055.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਰੋਗ ਹਰਤਾ is devotional praise of the remover of affliction. It is not a promise that recitation will cure a condition or proof that ongoing illness reflects weak faith. The consulted texts differ in punctuation and line grouping here; this explanation follows the four lines as presented.

jaap|jaap055.line02.simpleEn: I bow to You, whose being is love.
jaap|jaap055.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪਿਆਰ ਸਰੂਪ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap055.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਰਾਗ is read as love or affection, supported by Punjabi commentary and the Mahan Kosh entry. Neki and the Bhai Vir Singh-derived commentary emphasise bliss here. The word also has musical senses, but this line does not prescribe a particular raag or make musical ability a condition of devotion.

jaap|jaap055.line03.simpleEn: I bow to You, sovereign over every sovereign.
jaap|jaap055.line03.simplePa: ਹੇ ਸ਼ਾਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਵੀ ਸ਼ਾਹ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap055.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਸਾਹ ਸਾਹੰ is the repeated royal title, heard as Shah of shahs. In this context ਸਾਹ does not mean a breathing exercise. The spelling in the original is retained even though explanatory Punjabi commonly writes ਸ਼ਾਹ.

jaap|jaap055.line04.simpleEn: I bow to You, ruler over all earthly rulers.
jaap|jaap055.line04.simplePa: ਹੇ ਧਰਤੀ ਦੇ ਸਾਰੇ ਰਾਜਿਆਂ ਦੇ ਵੀ ਰਾਜੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap055.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਭੂਪ ਭੂਪੇ repeats the language of rulers to place human authority beneath the Divine. It does not make any present ruler, institution or community exempt from moral responsibility.

jaap|jaap056.line01.simpleEn: I bow to You, the giver from whom all givers receive.
jaap|jaap056.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਸਭ ਦਾਨੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਵੀ ਦੇਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਦਾਤੇ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap056.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਦਾਨ ਦਾਨੇ is read as the giver of givers, supported by the Punjabi commentaries. The repeated expression places generosity in relation to its Divine source rather than measuring a person’s worth by the amount they donate.

jaap|jaap056.line02.simpleEn: I bow to You, the honour of all who are honoured.
jaap|jaap056.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ; ਸਾਰੇ ਮਾਣ ਵਾਲਿਆਂ ਦਾ ਵੀ ਮਾਣ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap056.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਮਾਨ ਮਾਨੇ has the same selected English and Punjabi explanation as its occurrence in Chhand 46. The honour-of-the-honoured reading follows Punjabi commentary; bestower of honour is another rendering. Honour here need not mean social rank or pride.

jaap|jaap056.line03.simpleEn: I bow to You, praised as the affliction that overcomes afflictions.
jaap|jaap056.line03.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਰੋਗਾਂ ਲਈ ਵੀ ਰੋਗ ਬਣ ਕੇ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਮਿਟਾਉਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਵਜੋਂ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap056.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਰੋਗ ਰੋਗੇ uses the striking disease-of-disease expression. This draft selects the destroyer-of-affliction reading found in Punjabi commentary and Neki. A Rampur Khera footnote instead stresses that even diseases receive their power within Divine sovereignty; that is a distinct interpretation. Neither reading makes illness a person’s fault or promises a particular medical outcome.

jaap|jaap056.line04.simpleEn: I bow to You, source of purity, praised through the image of a cleansing bath.
jaap|jaap056.line04.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪਵਿੱਤਰਤਾ ਦੇ ਸੋਮੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ; ਤੇਰੀ ਹਜ਼ੂਰੀ ਨੂੰ ਪਵਿੱਤਰ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲੇ ਇਸ਼ਨਾਨ ਵਾਂਗ ਯਾਦ ਕੀਤਾ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap056.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਸਨਾਨੇ is heard through bathing and purification imagery, supported by Punjabi commentary and the related dictionary entry ਇਸਨਾਨ. Neki’s health-focused rendering is not adopted as a medical claim. Some other witnesses print ਇਸਨਾਨੰ; the original ਸਨਾਨੇ remains unchanged. The source comparison also notes differences in punctuation and grouping, without replacing the original words.

jaap|jaap057.line01.simpleEn: I bow to You as the mantra of mantras, supreme over sacred formulas.
jaap|jaap057.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਸਭ ਮੰਤ੍ਰਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਸ੍ਰੇਸ਼ਟ ਮੰਤ੍ਰ ਰੂਪ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap057.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਮੰਤ੍ਰ can name a sacred utterance, formula or counsel. The repeated ਮੰਤ੍ਰ ਮੰਤ੍ਰੰ is an address of supremacy in this context. It gives no recitation count, operational formula or guarantee that a desired event will occur.

jaap|jaap057.line02.simpleEn: I bow to You as the yantra of yantras, supreme over ritual devices and diagrams.
jaap|jaap057.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਸਭ ਜੰਤ੍ਰਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਸ੍ਰੇਸ਼ਟ ਜੰਤ੍ਰ ਰੂਪ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ; ਕੋਈ ਰਸਮੀ ਸਾਧਨ ਤੇਰੇ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਡਾ ਨਹੀਂ।
jaap|jaap057.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਜੰਤ੍ਰ has several dictionary senses, including device, instrument and ritual diagram or talisman. The pairing with mantra and tantra supports the ritual-device sense selected here. The lesson does not claim that diagrams, amulets or objects control the Divine, and it does not substitute the unrelated living-creature sense.

jaap|jaap057.line03.simpleEn: I bow to You, the One worthy of worship even by those whom others worship.
jaap|jaap057.line03.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਲੋਕ ਪੂਜਦੇ ਹਨ, ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਵੀ ਪੂਜਣਯੋਗ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ; ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap057.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਇਸਟ is read as a cherished or worship-worthy object of devotion; ਇਸਟ ਇਸਟੇ places the Divine above all such objects of worship. It is a reverent superlative, not an instruction to insult other people’s religious practice.

jaap|jaap057.line04.simpleEn: I bow to You as the tantra of tantras, supreme over ritual systems and techniques.
jaap|jaap057.line04.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਸਭ ਤੰਤ੍ਰਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਸ੍ਰੇਸ਼ਟ ਤੰਤ੍ਰ ਰੂਪ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ; ਸਾਰੀਆਂ ਰਸਮੀ ਵਿਧੀਆਂ ਤੋਂ ਉੱਚਾ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap057.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਤੰਤ੍ਰ can mean a system, method or ritual practice, among other senses. In this sequence the working reading concerns methods associated with ritual power. The phrase praises the One; it is not a recipe, endorsement of coercive magic or promise of special abilities.

jaap|jaap058.line01.simpleEn: You are eternally true being, awareness and bliss, and the One who brings all created things to their end.
jaap|jaap058.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਸਦਾ ਸੱਚੀ ਹੋਂਦ, ਚੇਤਨਾ ਅਤੇ ਅਨੰਦ ਸਰੂਪ ਹੈਂ; ਸਾਰੀ ਰਚਨਾ ਦਾ ਅੰਤ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਾ ਵੀ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap058.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਸੱਚਦਾਨੰਦ is conventionally explained through sat, chit and anand: true being, consciousness and bliss. ਸਰਬੰ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਸੀ names the ending of all, not merely the removal of bad habits. This reading follows the consulted commentaries without silently expanding the source spelling or making a prediction about when the world will end.

jaap|jaap058.line02.simpleEn: You are beyond comparison and without form, yet dwell within all.
jaap|jaap058.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੇਰੀ ਪੂਰੀ ਉਪਮਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਜਾ ਸਕਦੀ; ਤੂੰ ਰੂਪ ਰਹਿਤ ਹੈਂ ਅਤੇ ਸਭ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੱਸਦਾ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap058.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਅਨੂਪੇ denies an adequate comparison, ਅਰੂਪੇ a bounded form, and ਸਮਸਤੁਲ ਨਿਵਾਸੀ affirms presence within all. These are three distinct claims in one source line. Another website prints ਸਮਸਤੁਲਿ; this text’s ਸਮਸਤੁਲ is retained. Divine presence does not mean every human action is approved.

jaap|jaap059.line01.simpleEn: You always grant spiritual attainment and understanding, and bring about growth.
jaap|jaap059.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਸਦਾ ਸਿੱਧੀ ਅਤੇ ਬੁੱਧੀ ਬਖ਼ਸ਼ਦਾ ਹੈਂ ਅਤੇ ਵਾਧਾ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap059.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਸਿਧਦਾ and ਬੁਧਦਾ are provisionally read as granting attainment and understanding; ਬ੍ਰਿਧ ਕਰਤਾ as bringing increase or growth. Another consulted text reads ਸਿਧਿਦਾ ਬੁਧਿਦਾ ਬ੍ਰਿਧਿ. The commentary-supported compound reading does not settle that spelling question. Traditional siddhi can include extraordinary accomplishments or powers; this draft does not promise them to a reader.

jaap|jaap059.line02.simpleEn: You are present below, above and between, and remove the gathered burden of wrongdoing.
jaap|jaap059.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਹੇਠਾਂ, ਉੱਪਰ ਅਤੇ ਵਿਚਕਾਰ ਹਰ ਥਾਂ ਤੂੰ ਵਿਆਪਕ ਹੈਂ; ਪਾਪਾਂ ਦੇ ਸਮੂਹ ਨੂੰ ਦੂਰ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਾ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap059.line02.interpretiveCaution: This selects the Rampur Khera spatial reading of ਅਧੋ ਉਰਧ ਅਰਧੰ, followed by ਅਘੰ ਓਘ as an accumulation of wrongdoing and ਹਰਤਾ as remover. Another Punjabi commentary instead relates the three descriptors to classes or degrees of wrongdoing. The alternatives are not merged into a fabricated single explanation. Removing wrongdoing is not permission to avoid responsibility for harm.

jaap|jaap060.line01.simpleEn: You are the supreme Lord, higher than every greatness, who sustains all while remaining unseen.
jaap|jaap060.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਸ੍ਰੇਸ਼ਟ ਪਰਮੇਸ਼ਰ, ਤੂੰ ਸਭ ਦੀ ਪਾਲਣਾ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈਂ ਅਤੇ ਆਪ ਨਜ਼ਰ ਨਹੀਂ ਆਉਂਦਾ।
jaap|jaap060.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਪਰੰ ਪਰਮ ਪਰਮੇਸ੍ਵਰੰ intensifies the address to the supreme Lord. ਪ੍ਰੋਛ ਪਾਲੰ is read as unseen or hidden sustenance, supported by Punjabi commentary and Neki. This contextual explanation does not claim a settled derivation of ਪ੍ਰੋਛ. Unseen describes the Divine mode of care, not the worth of people with different visual abilities.

jaap|jaap060.line02.simpleEn: You are forever merciful, the giver of spiritual attainments at every time.
jaap|jaap060.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਦਿਆਲੂ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਹਰ ਵੇਲੇ ਸਦਾ ਸਿੱਧੀਆਂ ਬਖ਼ਸ਼ਣ ਵਾਲਾ ਦਾਤਾ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap060.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਸਦਾ ਸਰਬਦਾ reinforces continuity; ਦਿਆਲੰ names mercy. ਸਿੱਧ ਦਾਤਾ is provisionally read with the commentaries as bestower of siddhi, including traditional spiritual accomplishments or powers. Another consulted text prints ਸਿਧਿ ਦਾਤਾ; the original ਸਿੱਧ ਦਾਤਾ is unchanged and the edition question remains open. The line is not a guarantee that every wish or practice produces an extraordinary result.

editorialAmendments.reason: Clarifies the relation of sahaj to finding the Guru; the earlier wording could make natural ease the manner or prerequisite of the encounter.

before.simpleEn: By meeting the True Guru with natural ease, a new celebration begins within my mind.
before.simplePa: ਸਹਜ ਨਾਲ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੂ ਮਿਲਿਆ ਅਤੇ ਮੇਰੇ ਮਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਖੁਸ਼ੀ ਦੀ ਵਧਾਈ ਗੂੰਜੀ।
before.interpretiveCaution: Sahaj means inward poise in this poetic context; it is not a clinically measured mood state or a prescribed meditation technique.

after.simpleEn: I have found the True Guru and inward steadiness; celebration resounds in my mind.
after.simplePa: ਸਤਿਗੁਰੂ ਮਿਲਣ ਨਾਲ ਮਨ ਸਹਜ ਵਿੱਚ ਟਿਕਿਆ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਅੰਦਰ ਖੁਸ਼ੀ ਦੀਆਂ ਵਧਾਈਆਂ ਗੂੰਜ ਰਹੀਆਂ ਹਨ।
after.interpretiveCaution: This working reading treats sahaj as inward poise accompanying the meeting with the Guru. It does not mean merely that meeting the Guru was easy, or prescribe a technique for producing a mood.

editorialAmendments.reason: Restores the continuing third-person subject and descriptive sense, which the earlier English wish and Punjabi first-person exhortation obscured.

before.simpleEn: May Your praise always be spoken, and may Your Naam abide in the mind.
before.simplePa: ਤੇਰੀ ਸਿਫ਼ਤ-ਸਲਾਹ ਸਦਾ ਕਰੀਏ ਅਤੇ ਨਾਮ ਨੂੰ ਮਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਵਸਾਈਏ।
before.interpretiveCaution: Praise and remembrance describe a way of living rather than an external prize or purchase.

after.simpleEn: That person continually praises You and keeps Your Naam within the mind.
after.simplePa: ਜਿਸ ਨੂੰ ਤੇਰੀ ਦਾਤ ਮਿਲਦੀ ਹੈ, ਉਹ ਸਦਾ ਤੇਰੀ ਸਿਫ਼ਤ ਕਰਦਾ ਅਤੇ ਤੇਰਾ ਨਾਮ ਮਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਵਸਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
after.interpretiveCaution: The person receiving the gift in the preceding line remains the subject here. Praise and Naam describe that person’s life; the line is not a separate wish or a new first-person instruction.

editorialAmendments.reason: Clarifies the contextual musical sense of sabada ghanere instead of treating the plural as a definite set of canonical Shabads.

before.simpleEn: Those whose hearts hold Naam are pictured as filled with many resonant Shabads.
before.simplePa: ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਮਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਾਮ ਵੱਸਦਾ ਹੈ, ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਅੰਦਰ ਸ਼ਬਦਾਂ ਦੀ ਗੂੰਜ ਦਿਖਾਈ ਗਈ ਹੈ।
before.interpretiveCaution: This sound imagery is poetic and not a claim that a particular audible frequency or track must play.

after.simpleEn: In minds where Naam dwells, many melodies of joy are pictured as resounding.
after.simplePa: ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਮਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਾਮ ਵੱਸਦਾ ਹੈ, ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਅੰਦਰ ਮਾਨੋ ਅਨੰਦ ਦੀਆਂ ਅਨੇਕ ਸੁਰਾਂ ਗੂੰਜਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ।
after.interpretiveCaution: Sabada is read here in its musical sense of sounds or melodies. It should not automatically imply a collection of distinct canonical hymns, or require the reader to hear an actual sound.

editorialAmendments.reason: Explains the fivefold musical image without implying five identified canonical hymns. The recovered original Punjabi was valid UTF-8 and is retained in the audit fields; no encoding repair is claimed.

before.simpleEn: In the blessed inner home, five Shabads are pictured as sounding.
before.simplePa: ਭਾਗਾਂ ਵਾਲੇ ਹਿਰਦੇ-ਘਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਪੰਜ ਸ਼ਬਦਾਂ ਦੀ ਗੂੰਜ ਦੀ ਤਸਵੀਰ ਹੈ।
before.interpretiveCaution: “Five Shabads” and blessed home require qualified Sikh interpretive review; this is not evidence of five specific audio tracks or external sound waves.

after.simpleEn: In that fortunate inner home, a fivefold music of celebration is pictured as resounding.
after.simplePa: ਉਸ ਸੁਭਾਗੇ ਹਿਰਦੇ-ਘਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਮਾਨੋ ਪੰਜ ਕਿਸਮਾਂ ਦੇ ਸਾਜ਼ਾਂ ਦੀ ਸਾਂਝੀ ਧੁਨ ਵੱਜਦੀ ਹੈ।
after.interpretiveCaution: Panch sabad is read here as five kinds of musical sounds. This musical image is distinct from the five disruptive impulses in line three; neither five particular hymns nor five audible tones are prescribed.

editorialAmendments.reason: Restores the vocative address and the Guru as the giver of grace in this reading; the previous wording treated piaariaa as a title for the Divine.

before.simpleEn: True Anand is understood through the Guru and the grace of the Beloved One.
before.simplePa: ਸੱਚੇ ਅਨੰਦ ਦੀ ਸੂਝ ਗੁਰੂ ਦੀ ਸੇਧ ਤੇ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਨਾਲ ਮਿਲਦੀ ਹੈ।
before.interpretiveCaution: Anand here is a spiritual relationship, not a demand for constant pleasant mood or an emotional-performance score.

after.simpleEn: Dear one, Anand is always learned through the Guru, through the Guru’s grace.
after.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪਿਆਰੇ, ਅਨੰਦ ਦੀ ਸਮਝ ਸਦਾ ਗੁਰੂ ਤੋਂ ਹੀ ਮਿਲਦੀ ਹੈ, ਜਦ ਗੁਰੂ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।
after.interpretiveCaution: In this grammatical reading, piaariaa addresses the dear listener and the Guru grants grace. Anand names spiritual understanding and relationship, not a demand for a constantly pleasant mood.

editorialAmendments.reason: Retains the existing supported Shabad-centred explanation while making a material alternative reading explicit, rather than presenting one interpretation as settled.

before.simpleEn: When attachment loosens from within, the true Shabad reshapes their understanding and living.
before.simplePa: ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦਾ ਅੰਦਰਲਾ ਮੋਹ ਟੁੱਟਦਾ ਹੈ, ਸੱਚਾ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੀ ਸੇਧ ਸੰਵਾਰਦਾ ਹੈ।
before.interpretiveCaution: Breaking moh refers to attachment, not rejecting family responsibilities or cutting off loving relationships.

after.simpleEn: When attachment loosens from within, the true Shabad reshapes their understanding and living.
after.simplePa: ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦਾ ਅੰਦਰਲਾ ਮੋਹ ਟੁੱਟਦਾ ਹੈ, ਸੱਚਾ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੀ ਸੇਧ ਸੰਵਾਰਦਾ ਹੈ।
after.interpretiveCaution: The main explanation retains the Shabad-centred reading. Prof. Sahib Singh instead reads sabadu as the person’s speech, made gracious by the True One as attachment falls away. These alternatives need qualified review; loosening moh does not mean abandoning loving relationships or family responsibilities.

editorialAmendments.reason: Replace an unsupported anatomical guess with the documented steadiness reading.

before.simpleEn: I bow to the One described as beyond the limits of physical arms or ordinary force, a working sense needing review.
before.simplePa: ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਜੋ ਸਰੀਰਕ ਬਾਹਾਂ ਜਾਂ ਆਮ ਬਲ ਦੀ ਹੱਦ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਦੱਸਿਆ ਹੈ; ਅਰਥ ਦੀ ਸਮੀਖਿਆ ਬਾਕੀ ਹੈ।
before.nuance: Abaha and Adhaha spellings are not adjudicated. The martial images praise the Divine; they do not instruct readers to be violent or promise invulnerability.

after.simpleEn: I bow to the steadfast One, whom nothing can displace.
after.simplePa: ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਅਡੋਲ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜਿਸ ਨੂੰ ਹਿਲਾਇਆ ਨਹੀਂ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ।
after.nuance: For Abahe, this working reading follows the movement-related root explained in the consulted commentary. The earlier reference to bodily arms was unsupported; the original spelling is unchanged.

editorialAmendments.reason: Use a consistent movement-related gloss for the repeated epithet.

before.simpleEn: I bow to the One beyond the grasp of ordinary arms or force; the precise Abahe word sense remains under review.
before.simplePa: ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜੋ ਆਮ ਬਲ ਜਾਂ ਬਾਂਹਾਂ ਦੀ ਪਹੁੰਚ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈ; “ਅਬਾਹੇ” ਦਾ ਅਰਥ ਅਸਥਾਈ ਹੈ।
before.nuance: This cluster has multiple difficult lexical items. Do not claim certain literal translations for Abahe, Tribarge or Asarge until qualified textual review.

after.simpleEn: I bow to the One who remains unshaken.
after.simplePa: ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਅਡੋਲ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜੋ ਕਿਸੇ ਦੇ ਹਿਲਾਇਆਂ ਨਹੀਂ ਹਿਲਦਾ।
after.nuance: The same Abahe occurs in Chhand 6. This draft uses the same steadiness reading in both occurrences; it does not infer arms or bodily force from the spelling. Linguistic review remains open.

editorialAmendments.reason: Replace the unsupported fixed-form gloss and make the attested interpretive difference visible.

before.simpleEn: I bow to the One not limited by a fixed form; the Ajūpe wording needs Sanskrit/Braj review.
before.simplePa: ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜੋ ਇੱਕ ਨਿਸ਼ਚਿਤ ਰੂਪ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਹੀਂ ਬੱਝਦਾ; “ਅਜੂਪੇ” ਦੀ ਸਮੀਖਿਆ ਲੋੜੀਂਦੀ ਹੈ।
before.nuance: This juxtaposes One and many; Abhute/Ajupe are working editorial glosses and must not be treated as a definitive doctrine about physical existence.

after.simpleEn: I bow to the unbound One, free from constraint.
after.simplePa: ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਮੁਕਤ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜੋ ਕਿਸੇ ਬੰਧਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਹੀਂ।
after.nuance: Ajupe is read here as freedom from bondage, supported by the consulted Narain Singh steek. The Bhai Vir Singh-derived commentary connects it with freedom from pain. These readings remain open for specialist comparison; neither makes Ajupe simply another word for formlessness.

editorialAmendments.reason: Restore the bodily-constituents sense documented in the Mahan Kosh entry.

before.simpleEn: I bow to the One praised as beyond a created support or fixed dependence; “Nirdhate” requires a qualified gloss.
before.simplePa: ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜੋ ਬਣਾਏ ਆਸਰੇ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈ; “ਨ੍ਰਿਧਾਤੇ” ਦੇ ਪੱਕੇ ਅਰਥ ਦੀ ਜਾਂਚ ਬਾਕੀ ਹੈ।
before.nuance: Nirdhate and Nirghate are difficult Sanskrit/Braj epithets. These are working educational senses only, NOT verified morphological interpretations; no claim of immunity to harm.

after.simpleEn: I bow to the One not made from bodily elements.
after.simplePa: ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜੋ ਸਰੀਰ ਦੇ ਤੱਤਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਬਣਿਆ ਨਹੀਂ।
after.nuance: Nirdhate is related here to dhatu, the constituents of a body. This is a theological working gloss, not a scientific claim about matter. The earlier wording about dependence or support confused this epithet with a different idea.

editorialAmendments.reason: Remove the unsupported impurity gloss while retaining the attested movement sense.

before.simpleEn: I bow to the One beyond being soiled or shaken; the exact old-form “Nirdhute” requires review.
before.simplePa: ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜੋ ਮੈਲ ਜਾਂ ਹਿਲਾਉ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈ; “ਨ੍ਰਿਧੂਤੇ” ਦਾ ਅਰਥ ਅਸਥਾਈ ਹੈ।
before.nuance: Nirdhute/Abhute/Aloke are lexically complex and could admit more than one qualified reading. Assumption is documented, not asserted as standard scholarly translation.

after.simpleEn: I bow to the steady One, beyond being shaken.
after.simplePa: ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਅਡੋਲ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜਿਸ ਨੂੰ ਡੋਲਾਇਆ ਨਹੀਂ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ।
after.nuance: For Nirdhute, the consulted commentary connects the word with movement. The draft therefore uses steadiness and removes the earlier added stain or impurity gloss. This remains an educational reading pending linguistic review.

editorialAmendments.reason: Correct a mistaken negation and retain the temporal/worlds interpretive difference.

before.simpleEn: I bow to the One transcending narrowly measured threefold categories; “Trimane” remains provisional.
before.simplePa: ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜੋ ਸੀਮਤ ਤਿੰਨ-ਭੇਦਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈ; “ਤ੍ਰਿਮਾਨੇ” ਦਾ ਅਰਥ ਅਸਥਾਈ ਹੈ।
before.nuance: Nritape, Athape, Trimane and Nidhane require a specialist Braj/Sanskrit review; do not use the idea of a “treasury” as a promised financial reward.

after.simpleEn: I bow to the One revered in every age and realm.
after.simplePa: ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜੋ ਹਰ ਕਾਲ ਅਤੇ ਹਰ ਲੋਕ ਵਿੱਚ ਮੰਨਣਯੋਗ ਹੈ।
after.nuance: Trimane is an affirmative title of reverence. Consulted readings connect its threefold reference with past, present and future, or with the three worlds. This broad paraphrase leaves that distinction open; it does not invent a negative prefix meaning beyond categories.

editorialAmendments.reason: Replace an unexplained generic threefold negation with an attributed working interpretation.

before.simpleEn: I bow to the One beyond limiting threefold categories or pursuits; the exact Tribarge use needs scholarly checking.
before.simplePa: ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜੋ ਸੀਮਤ ਤਿੰਨ-ਭੇਦਾਂ ਜਾਂ ਲਾਲਸਾਵਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈ; “ਤ੍ਰਿਬਰਗੇ” ਦੀ ਸਮੀਖਿਆ ਚਾਹੀਦੀ ਹੈ।
before.nuance: This cluster has multiple difficult lexical items. Do not claim certain literal translations for Abahe, Tribarge or Asarge until qualified textual review.

after.simpleEn: I bow to the One expressed through the three qualities of nature.
after.simplePa: ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜੋ ਕੁਦਰਤ ਦੇ ਤਿੰਨਾਂ ਗੁਣਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੀ ਪ੍ਰਗਟ ਹੁੰਦਾ ਹੈ।
after.nuance: This working reading of Tribarge follows the consulted Bhai Vir Singh-derived account of the three gunas: sattva, rajas and tamas. Other teaching traditions gloss the epithet differently. The exact compound remains under review; this line is not a settled definition of Divine nature.

editorialAmendments.reason: Resolve the English/Punjabi mismatch using a documented bliss-related reading.

before.simpleEn: I bow to the One related to every experience and enjoyment, yet not bounded by it; Prabhoge is a working sense.
before.simplePa: ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜੋ ਜੀਵਾਂ ਦੇ ਭੋਗ ਤੇ ਅਨੁਭਵ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈ; “ਪ੍ਰਭੋਗੇ” ਦਾ ਅਰਥ ਅਸਥਾਈ ਹੈ।
before.nuance: Prabhoge/Sujoge require qualified interpretation, and the critique of colour is about Divine transcendence, never caste, race or human worth.

after.simpleEn: I bow to the One whose joy is complete.
after.simplePa: ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜਿਸ ਦਾ ਆਨੰਦ ਪੂਰਨ ਹੈ।
after.nuance: Prabhoge is read here through supreme enjoyment or bliss. Both language drafts now express that same working reading. This does not settle every sense of bhog or promise that a reader will always feel happy.

editorialAmendments.reason: Remove the assumption that Ajupe is a fixed-form epithet; keep the source-specific interpretive comparison.

before.simpleEn: One Divine reality is invoked through both unity and many expressions, while remaining beyond fixed created form.
before.simplePa: ਇੱਕ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਇਕਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਅਨੇਕ ਪ੍ਰਗਟਾਵਿਆਂ ਦੀ ਵਡਿਆਈ ਹੈ, ਪਰ ਉਹ ਬਣੇ ਰੂਪਾਂ ਤਕ ਸੀਮਤ ਨਹੀਂ।

study.focus: One and many held together in praise.
study.closeReading: The first line greets the One, the second invokes the Many, and the remaining two use complex epithets relating to created and defined forms. The meaningful interpretive move is not to treat these as contradictions, but to explore the difference between the one unbounded Source and its diverse expressions. The exact old-word morphology has not been independently settled.
study.care: Abhute and Ajupe remain provisional working glosses. Do not present a precise cosmological mechanism or equate religious metaphor with scientific measurements.
study.reflection: Where might I see unity without denying genuine differences?
study.teachBack: Which first two words set up this chhand’s central comparison?

after.simpleEn: The One is praised through unity and multiplicity, with further titles whose precise meanings need careful comparison.
after.simplePa: ਇੱਕ ਅਤੇ ਅਨੇਕ ਦੇ ਰੂਪ ਵਿੱਚ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਵਡਿਆਈ ਹੈ; ਅਗਲੇ ਵਿਸ਼ੇਸ਼ਣਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਧਿਆਨ ਨਾਲ ਸਮਝਣ ਤੇ ਪਰਖਣ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Unity, multiplicity and the limits of a short gloss.
study.closeReading: The first pair places One beside Many. The next pair must be read on its own terms rather than treated as two interchangeable words for form. Abhute concerns created or elemental existence in the working draft; Ajupe is rendered here through freedom from constraint, with another documented reading noted beside the line. Comparing these meanings is part of the lesson, not a reason to alter the source.
study.care: The Ajupe line retains an explicit alternative reading. These explanatory choices are provisional and should not be turned into a definitive account of cosmology or an official lexical judgment.
study.reflection: Can I notice both a shared ground and real differences without flattening either?
study.teachBack: Which two opening titles form a contrast, and why should the last two be examined separately?

editorialAmendments.reason: Align the Study explanation with the corrected dhatu-related line meaning.

before.simpleEn: Names, desire and the causes of loss do not confine the One in this poetic salutation.
before.simplePa: ਨਾਂ, ਚਾਹ ਅਤੇ ਨਾਸ-ਵਿਨਾਸ ਦੀਆਂ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਉਪਰ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਵਡਿਆਈ ਕੀਤੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: A source-specific study of four difficult epithets.
study.closeReading: The opening lines invoke the One beyond a fixed name and without grasping desire. The second pair uses the harder Nirdhate/Nirghate forms, which have not been philologically adjudicated. These later terms should be taught as tentative meanings with explicit uncertainty, rather than building large doctrinal conclusions on an unverified short gloss.
study.care: Nirdhate and Nirghate are not approved dictionary definitions. Do not promise bodily invulnerability or suggest the Divine commands harmful behaviour.
study.reflection: How do names help us learn while still limiting what they describe?
study.teachBack: Which two familiar words precede the more difficult pair requiring specialist review?

after.simpleEn: The salutations move through name, desire, bodily constituents and destruction as limits that do not define the One.
after.simplePa: ਨਾਮ, ਚਾਹ, ਸਰੀਰ ਦੇ ਤੱਤ ਅਤੇ ਨਾਸ ਦੀਆਂ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਾ ਬੱਝਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕੀਤੀ ਗਈ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Distinguishing a body’s constituents from its support.
study.closeReading: The first two titles concern naming and desire. The third is now explained through bodily constituents rather than dependence on an external support. The fourth concerns destruction or harm. Reading the four separately helps prevent a plausible general idea about God from being substituted for the particular word on the page. Each salutation still addresses the same One.
words: Not defined by a name; working gloss
study.care: Nirdhate receives a documented constituent-related reading, while exact historical morphology still needs specialist review. Praise of the Divine does not imply that a person can become physically immune to harm.
study.reflection: When can a familiar idea keep me from noticing what a text actually says?
study.teachBack: How is a description about bodily constituents different from a description about needing support?

editorialAmendments.reason: Remove the unsupported stain interpretation from the summary, close reading and vocabulary.

before.simpleEn: The chhand addresses the One beyond ordinary stain, worldly form, limited perception and sorrow.
before.simplePa: ਇਹ ਛੰਦ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਮੈਲ, ਬਣੇ ਰੂਪ, ਆਮ ਨਿਗਾਹ ਅਤੇ ਸੋਗ ਦੀਆਂ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਯਾਦ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: The limits of appearance and the language of sorrow.
study.closeReading: These four names form a cluster of negations. The specific meanings of Nirdhute, Abhute and Aloke are provisional, while Asoke invites a relatively clear contrast with sorrow. The reader can learn how Braj salutation syntax works without pretending every compound has one certain English equivalent.
study.care: Do not equate “without sorrow” with a clinical guarantee or suggest that anyone experiencing grief has failed spiritually. Linguistic review is open.
study.reflection: What is the difference between respecting grief and finding hope in a spiritual text?
study.teachBack: Which of these four titles most directly names sorrow?

after.simpleEn: This sequence praises steadiness and freedom from created limitations, ordinary sight and sorrow.
after.simplePa: ਇਹ ਲੜੀ ਅਡੋਲਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਸਿਰਜੀਆਂ ਹੱਦਾਂ, ਆਮ ਨਿਗਾਹ ਤੇ ਸੋਗ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਵਡਿਆਈ ਕਰਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Giving each repeated salutation its own meaning.
study.closeReading: Four salutations share a repeated opening but differ in their descriptive words. The first is read through steadiness, without adding an unsupported claim about stain. Abhute and Aloke then introduce different interpretive questions about created existence and seeing. Asoke brings sorrow into the sequence. The repetition is a reason to listen carefully for the changing title, rather than to assume all four mean the same thing.
words: Steady or not shaken; working gloss
study.care: The revised first gloss follows a movement-related reading; the remaining old-language details are still provisional. Describing the Divine as free from sorrow is not a demand that human beings suppress grief.
study.reflection: What changes when I attend to a repeated phrase instead of rushing past it?
study.teachBack: How does the fourth title differ in subject from the first title?

editorialAmendments.reason: Correct the falsely negative account of Trimane in the deeper explanation.

before.simpleEn: The poem bows to a One beyond ordinary affliction or establishment and describes inexhaustible treasure.
before.simplePa: ਕਵੀ ਆਮ ਤਾਪ ਤੇ ਠਿਕਾਣੇ ਦੀ ਹੱਦ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਅਤੇ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਨਿਧਾਨ ਆਖਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Unsettled old vocabulary beside the image of a treasury.
study.closeReading: The sequence moves through Nritape and Athape, followed by Trimane and Nidhane. Nidhane suggests a repository or treasury, while the preceding forms need close textual and morphological attention. Rather than asserting a sure “three worlds” or “three gunas” gloss, the Study layer should leave the third term openly unresolved until a qualified scholar can compare dictionaries and textual witnesses.
words: Treasury, source or store of gifts
study.care: “Treasure” is devotional praise and not evidence of financial returns; Trimane’s meaning is unsettled and should not be inserted as a certain doctrine.
study.reflection: How can I learn to hold an unresolved word without making up certainty?
study.teachBack: Which term in the fourth line introduces the treasury image?

after.simpleEn: The sequence moves from freedom from affliction and dependence on establishment to reverence and the image of treasure.
after.simplePa: ਛੰਦ ਤਾਪ ਅਤੇ ਕਿਸੇ ਦੇ ਸਥਾਪਿਤ ਕੀਤੇ ਹੋਣ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਗੱਲ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਫਿਰ ਉਸ ਦੇ ਮਾਣ ਅਤੇ ਨਿਧਾਨ-ਰੂਪ ਨੂੰ ਯਾਦ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: An affirmative title within a sequence of negations.
study.closeReading: The first two descriptive titles have negative force, but that pattern must not automatically be extended to the third. Trimane affirms reverence; its precise threefold reference has more than one documented explanation. Nidhane then introduces a treasury image. The sequence therefore changes its rhetorical movement, and that change would be lost by translating every unfamiliar title as beyond something.
words: Revered across the three times or worlds; working alternatives
study.care: The temporal and worlds-based readings of Trimane need qualified comparison. The title is not being treated as a claim about measured dimensions, and the treasury image does not promise material reward.
study.reflection: Do I let an apparent pattern decide a word’s meaning before I examine it?
study.teachBack: Why should the negative sense of the first two titles not be imposed on Trimane?

editorialAmendments.reason: Remove the arms gloss and the unsupported blanket description beyond categories.

before.simpleEn: The One is praised as unfathomable and beyond ordinary reach, categories and created origin.
before.simplePa: ਅਥਾਹ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਆਮ ਪਹੁੰਚ, ਵੰਡ ਅਤੇ ਸ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਟੀ ਦੀਆਂ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ।

study.focus: A cluster of attributes requiring source comparison.
study.closeReading: Agahe points toward unfathomability, while Abahe, Tribarge and Asarge carry additional old-language possibilities. This chhand is useful for learning to distinguish an easy general religious idea from a precise word-level translation. The final three terms should remain visibly provisional until review, even though the four original source lines themselves are fully displayed.
study.care: Uncertain Braj/Sanskrit words require qualified review, not a silent source correction. No word here is authority for a physical or medical experiment.
study.reflection: What is gained by acknowledging the limits of an explanation?
study.teachBack: Which title begins the chhand and what general theme does it establish?

after.simpleEn: The One is praised as unfathomable, steadfast and uncreated; the threefold title carries a provisional reading.
after.simplePa: ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਅਥਾਹਤਾ, ਅਡੋਲਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਅਜਨਮੇ ਹੋਣ ਦੀ ਵਡਿਆਈ ਹੈ; ਤਿੰਨਾਂ ਗੁਣਾਂ ਵਾਲੇ ਵਿਸ਼ੇਸ਼ਣ ਦਾ ਅਰਥ ਹਾਲੇ ਸਮੀਖਿਆ ਅਧੀਨ ਹੈ।

study.focus: A repeated title and a distinct threefold expression.
study.closeReading: Agahe opens the chhand with the difficulty of fathoming the One. Abahe repeats a title from Chhand 6 and is explained consistently through steadiness. Tribarge introduces a different threefold expression; the line note identifies the working interpretation used here instead of disguising it as a settled lexical result. Asarge closes the sequence by addressing the One as uncreated. These four titles need not all be paraphrased with the same negative formula.
study.care: The threefold reference in Tribarge remains a matter for specialist comparison. A theological description of the gunas is not a scientific classification of people or a measure of their worth.
study.reflection: What makes a clear statement of uncertainty more useful than a vague explanation?
study.teachBack: Which title also occurs in Chhand 6, and which title has the explicitly provisional threefold reading?

editorialAmendments.reason: Align the Study discussion with the corrected bilingual opening line.

before.simpleEn: The chhand praises a sustaining One beyond limiting colour and disintegration.
before.simplePa: ਇਹ ਛੰਦ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਜੀਵਨ ਦਾ ਮੂਲ, ਰੰਗ-ਹੱਦਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਅਤੇ ਅਭੰਗ ਦੱਸਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Enjoyment, relationship and transcendence in four titles.
study.closeReading: Prabhoge and Sujoge are difficult source words for which the draft offers only a provisional sense. The final pair is more clearly structured around absence of limiting colour and indestructibility. The student is invited to notice how devotional naming moves from relation with the world to a reality that cannot be assigned one human appearance or broken apart.
study.care: Never use the absence of colour to rank human skin tones, caste or race. No explanation here proves invulnerability to harm; Prabhoge/Sujoge need human review.
study.reflection: How might I look beyond appearance when assessing someone’s character?
study.teachBack: How do the last two descriptive titles differ from the first two?

after.simpleEn: The opening invokes complete Divine joy and fitting union; the final pair turns to colour and indestructibility.
after.simplePa: ਸ਼ੁਰੂ ਵਿੱਚ ਪੂਰਨ ਰੱਬੀ ਆਨੰਦ ਅਤੇ ਸੁਚੱਜੇ ਮਿਲਾਪ ਨੂੰ ਯਾਦ ਕੀਤਾ ਹੈ; ਅਖੀਰਲੀ ਜੋੜੀ ਰੰਗ ਅਤੇ ਅਭੰਗਤਾ ਵੱਲ ਮੁੜਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: A shared meaning across the two teaching languages.
study.closeReading: The revised opening explanation presents the same bliss-related working sense in English and Punjabi. Sujoge then introduces the question of fitting union or relationship, whose precise interpretation remains provisional. The final two titles change direction toward colour and what cannot be broken. The student can notice that movement without assuming that a short translation exhausts any of these words.
words: Not broken or destroyed; working gloss
study.care: Prabhoge and Sujoge remain interpretive working readings. The description of Divine joy does not require a constant human mood, and language about colour must not be used to rank skin tones or caste.
study.reflection: How can two explanations in different languages support the same careful understanding?
study.teachBack: How does the final pair of titles change the focus introduced by the opening pair?
